units.title: Nota - Litiasis renal
units.body:
# Nota - Litiasis renal

## Promesa de la nota

Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder reconocer colico renal, identificar el
tipo de calculo por pH/radiologia/cristales/contexto, elegir imagen, separar
colico simple de obstruccion infectada, y decidir tratamiento por tamano,
localizacion y recurrencia.

## Take-home global

Litiasis renal se resuelve con una pregunta de ruta:

```text
dolor tipo colico renal
-> complicado o no complicado?
-> que imagen necesito?
-> que tipo de calculo parece?
-> que tamano/localizacion tiene?
-> pasa solo, necesita MET, procedimiento o drenaje urgente?
```

## Como la preguntan

| Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patron clinico | Es colico renal? | Dolor lumbar a ingle + inquietud + hematuria | Litiasis/colico renal |
| Tipo de calculo | Que calculo es? | pH, radiopacidad, cristales, gota, Proteus | Uric acid, struvite, calcium, cystine |
| Imagen | Que examen pido? | adulto/pregnancy/child, local vs confirmatory | US or non-contrast CT |
| Urgencia | Alta o drenaje? | fever, sepsis, solitary kidney, anuria, pain | Admit, antibiotics, decompression |
| Tamano | Que manejo? | <5, 5-10, >10, >20 mm + location | observe, MET, SWL/URS, PCNL |
| Prevencion | Como evitar recurrencia? | stone type, hypercalciuria, uric acid, cystine | fluids, low salt, citrate, thiazide, alkalinization |

## Gatillo de reconocimiento

Piensa en colico renal si hay:

- acute lumbar/flank pain;
- radiation to groin or genitals;
- patient cannot find a comfortable position;
- nausea, vomiting or sweating;
- microhematuria;
- urinary symptoms if distal ureter/UVJ.

Piensa en complicated stone if there is:

- fever or sepsis;
- hypotension/tachycardia;
- solitary kidney;
- pregnancy;
- diabetes or high-risk host;
- uncontrolled pain/vomiting;
- anuria or renal dysfunction;
- obstructing large stone.

**Take-home:** the restless patient with flank-to-groin pain is renal colic;
the febrile obstructed patient is a urologic emergency.

## Guion de la enfermedad

### 1. Por que da

A stone forms when urine becomes supersaturated with a solute and the balance
between promoters and inhibitors of crystallization fails.

Mechanisms:

- low urine volume concentrates solutes;
- excess calcium, oxalate, uric acid or cystine increases supersaturation;
- low citrate removes an inhibitor of calcium stone formation;
- urinary pH changes solubility;
- infection with urease-positive bacteria alkalinizes urine and favors
  struvite;
- anatomic obstruction/stasis favors growth and infection.

| Mechanism | Stone route |
|---|---|
| Hypercalciuria / hypocitraturia / low volume | Calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate |
| Acidic urine + hyperuricemia/gout | Uric acid |
| Cystinuria | Cystine |
| Urease-positive infection | Struvite |
| Distal renal tubular acidosis | Calcium phosphate |
| Bowel disease/resection | Enteric hyperoxaluria -> calcium oxalate |

**Take-home:** urine pH is a discriminator: acidic favors uric acid/cystine;
alkaline favors phosphate/struvite.

### 2. A quien le da

| Pattern | Typical patient/context |
|---|---|
| Calcium oxalate | Most common; adult male; hypercalciuria, low urine volume, high sodium |
| Calcium phosphate | Distal RTA, hypercalcemia/hyperparathyroidism |
| Uric acid | Male, gout, hyperuricemia, acidic urine, metabolic syndrome |
| Struvite | Woman, recurrent UTI, Proteus/Klebsiella/Serratia, staghorn |
| Cystine | Young patient, family history, autosomal recessive cystinuria |
| High recurrence risk | Early onset, bilateral, solitary kidney, staghorn, rare type, recurrent |

**Take-home:** the context is often more important than frequency. Calcium
oxalate is most common, but gout + acidic urine is uric acid until proven
otherwise.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Presentation | Clue | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Classic renal colic | Sudden flank pain to groin, restless | Ureteral obstruction |
| Distal ureter/UVJ | Genital radiation, frequency, dysuria | Low stone |
| Hematuria | Micro or gross blood in urine | Supports stone |
| Nausea/vomiting/sweating | Autonomic response | Common in colic |
| Fever/chills | Infection | Emergency if obstructed |
| Anuria/AKI | Obstruction with renal risk | Urgent evaluation |
| Staghorn stone | Large branching renal pelvis stone | Usually struvite/infection |

**Take-home:** fever changes the game. Pain plus fever plus obstruction is not
"more severe colic"; it is infected obstruction.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

#### Bedside diagnosis

Start with the clinical pattern:

```text
flank pain -> groin/genitals
+ restlessness
+ nausea/vomiting
+ hematuria
= renal colic probable
```

Basic tests:

- urinalysis: hematuria, leukocyturia, nitrites, pH, crystals;
- urine culture if infection suspected;
- creatinine/eGFR;
- CBC/CRP if fever or systemic illness;
- pregnancy test when relevant;
- serum calcium if stone disease or recurrence evaluation.

#### Imaging

Local exam-safe framing:

| Test | What it gives | Main use |
|---|---|---|
| Ultrasound | hydronephrosis, renal/UVJ stone, no radiation | safe initial screen; pregnancy/children; local first-image stems |
| Non-contrast CT | size, location, density, alternative diagnosis | reference/confirmation; adult current route |
| KUB radiograph | radiopaque vs radiolucent follow-up | not enough to rule out uric acid stone |
| IVU | old morphology/function test | displaced by CT; avoid with creatinine >2, allergy, myeloma, dehydration |

Product modifier:

```text
If the exam asks "first urgent safe image" -> ultrasound can be correct locally.
If the exam asks "reference/confirmatory test" -> non-contrast CT.
If adult current guideline route is explicit -> urgent low-dose non-contrast CT.
If pregnancy/child -> ultrasound first.
```

**Take-home:** KUB negative does not rule out stone; uric acid can be
radiolucent. CT without contrast is the reference test.

### 2. Clasificacion

#### By stone type

| Type | pH | Radiology | Crystals/context | Treatment/prevention anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calcium oxalate | variable/neutral | radiopaque | most common, hypercalciuria, bipyramidal | fluids, low salt, thiazide/citrate if indicated |
| Calcium phosphate | alkaline | radiopaque | distal RTA, hypercalcemia | treat cause, thiazide when indicated |
| Struvite | alkaline | radiopaque/staghorn | Proteus, recurrent UTI, woman | remove stone, antibiotics, urease inhibitor selected |
| Uric acid | acidic | radiolucent | gout, hyperuricemia, KUB negative | alkalinize urine, allopurinol if hyperuricemia |
| Cystine | acidic | poorly radiopaque/radiolucent | young, family, hexagonal crystals | high diuresis, alkalinize >7.5, D-penicillamine if refractory |

#### By clinical risk

| Type | Criteria | Route |
|---|---|---|
| Uncomplicated | afebrile, stable, renal function OK, pain controlled | outpatient if small/likely to pass |
| Complicated | fever, sepsis, solitary kidney, anuria/AKI, pregnancy, uncontrolled pain, high-risk host | hospital/urology route |
| Obstructed infected system | obstruction + infection/sepsis | urgent decompression + antibiotics |

#### By size

| Size | Local exam route |
|---|---|
| <5 mm | observation + hydration + NSAID |
| 5-10 mm | MET, especially tamsulosin 0.4 mg/day for distal ureter |
| >10 mm | active intervention by site |
| >20 mm or staghorn | PCNL/NLPC |

**Take-home:** classify by chemistry to prevent recurrence, by complication to
avoid death, and by size/location to choose procedure.

### 3. Manejo

#### Acute uncomplicated renal colic

```text
assess red flags
-> analgesia
-> hydration without forced overhydration
-> urine/blood tests
-> image by context
-> decide observe/MET/procedure
```

Analgesia:

- first line: NSAID, local card uses ketorolac 30 mg IV/IM;
- if NSAID contraindicated or insufficient: IV paracetamol or opioid depending
  source/context;
- opioids are not first-line when NSAID is safe;
- avoid antispasmodics as core therapy.

Medical expulsive therapy:

- best exam overlap: distal ureteral stone 5-10 mm;
- tamsulosin 0.4 mg/day;
- control in 4-6 weeks in local card if stable.

#### Complicated colic / obstructed infection

Red flags:

- fever >38 C or sepsis;
- hypotension/tachycardia;
- solitary kidney;
- AKI/anuria;
- uncontrolled pain or vomiting;
- pregnancy;
- diabetes/high-risk host;
- large obstructing stone.

Route:

```text
do not discharge
-> cultures/labs and imaging
-> IV antibiotics if infection suspected
-> urgent urinary decompression
   ureteral stent or percutaneous nephrostomy
-> definitive stone treatment after infection/control
```

**Take-home:** infected obstruction is a drainage problem, not a tamsulosin
problem.

#### Active treatment by size/location

| Scenario | Preferred local-exam route |
|---|---|
| <5 mm uncomplicated | observation + analgesia |
| 5-10 mm distal ureter | tamsulosin/MET |
| 10-20 mm renal or proximal ureter | LEOC/SWL or URS depending site/context |
| distal/mid ureteral stone | URS especially useful |
| renal stone >2 cm or staghorn | PCNL/NLPC |
| failed minimally invasive options | surgery open/laparoscopic rare |

LEOC/SWL avoid in local table:

- pregnancy;
- active infection;
- distal obstruction below the stone;
- coagulopathy;
- aortic aneurysm;
- pacemaker in local card/source-lock pending.

#### Prevention and recurrence

Universal advice:

- increase fluid intake to raise urine volume;
- reduce sodium;
- maintain normal dietary calcium;
- avoid excess animal protein if uric acid/cystine risk;
- collect/analyze passed stone when possible;
- evaluate high-risk or recurrent stone formers.

Targeted prevention:

| Stone | Prevention |
|---|---|
| Calcium oxalate + hypercalciuria | thiazide after salt restriction |
| Calcium oxalate recurrent/hypocitraturia | potassium citrate |
| Enteric hyperoxaluria | low fat/low oxalate strategy, calcium with meals, selected cholestyramine |
| Uric acid | alkalinize urine, allopurinol if hyperuricemia |
| Cystine | urine volume >3 L/day, alkalinize >7.5, D-penicillamine if refractory |
| Struvite | infection control and complete removal; urease inhibitor selected |

**Take-home:** acute treatment removes pain/obstruction; prevention follows
stone chemistry.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Complication | Clue | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Obstructed pyelonephritis | fever + obstruction | sepsis risk; urgent drainage |
| Urosepsis | hypotension, tachycardia, fever | antibiotics + source control |
| AKI/anuria | creatinine rise, solitary kidney, bilateral obstruction | urgent decompression |
| Hydronephrosis | ultrasound/CT dilation | obstruction severity |
| Recurrent stones | repeated episodes | metabolic workup |
| Staghorn stone | branching renal pelvis stone | infection reservoir, renal damage |
| Renal scarring/loss | chronic obstruction/infection | long-term morbidity |

**Take-home:** the dangerous complication is a closed infected urinary system.

### 5. Seguimiento necesario

After outpatient colic:

- confirm symptom control;
- confirm stone passage or follow-up imaging if not seen;
- recheck renal function if obstruction, AKI risk or persistent symptoms;
- give return precautions: fever, uncontrolled pain, vomiting, anuria;
- retrieve stone for analysis when possible.

Metabolic evaluation is indicated with:

- early onset;
- recurrent stones;
- bilateral stones;
- solitary kidney;
- staghorn stone;
- nephrocalcinosis;
- rare stone type;
- high-risk occupational or medical context.

Follow-up prevention:

```text
stone analysis
-> serum calcium/basic labs
-> 24 h urine if high risk/recurrent
-> lifestyle
-> targeted medication
-> monitor recurrence and adverse effects
```

**Take-home:** a passed stone is not the end of the case if it is recurrent,
bilateral, early, rare or high risk.

### 6. Pronostico

Good prognosis:

- small distal stone;
- no fever;
- normal renal function;
- pain controlled;
- no solitary kidney/pregnancy/high-risk host;
- stone passes or is removed completely;
- recurrence prevention addressed.

Poor prognosis/risk:

- infected obstruction;
- delayed decompression;
- staghorn stone;
- recurrent stones without metabolic workup;
- solitary kidney obstruction;
- renal dysfunction;
- cystine/struvite/high-risk metabolic disease.

**Take-home:** prognosis is determined less by pain intensity and more by
infection, obstruction, renal function and recurrence risk.

## Cases at the end

### Case 1

Man with gout has renal colic. Urine pH is 5.0 and KUB does not show a stone.

Question: most likely stone?

Answer: uric acid. Acidic urine + gout + radiolucent/KUB-negative stone.

### Case 2

Woman with recurrent UTIs has a staghorn renal stone, alkaline urine and
Proteus culture.

Question: stone type?

Answer: struvite. Urease-positive infection alkalinizes urine.

### Case 3

Stable adult has a 7 mm distal ureteral stone, no fever, normal creatinine and
pain controlled with ketorolac.

Question: next treatment?

Answer: outpatient MET with tamsulosin plus analgesia and follow-up.

### Case 4

Woman with recurrent stones has fever 39.2 C, vomiting, flank pain, BP 90/60
and tachycardia.

Question: what is the priority?

Answer: obstructed infected system/sepsis risk. Admit, antibiotics and urgent
urinary decompression, not simple outpatient colic.

Litiasis renal se resuelve con una pregunta de ruta: ```text dolor tipo colico renal -> complicado o no complicado? -> que imagen necesito? -> que tipo de calculo parece? -> que tamano/localizacion tiene? -> pasa solo, necesita MET, procedimiento o drenaje urgente? ``` | Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada | |---|-

units.title: Nota - Apendicitis aguda
units.body:
# Nota - Apendicitis aguda

## Promesa de la nota

Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder reconocer apendicitis aguda, decidir
cuando operar sin imagen, cuando pedir imagen, como manejar apendicitis
complicada, que antibiotico usar y que trampas no caer en ENAM/Residentado.

## Take-home global

La pregunta real es:

```text
dolor RLQ
-> patron clasico o incierto?
-> paciente especial?
-> no complicada o complicada?
-> apendicectomia, imagen, antibioticos, drenaje o cirugia de emergencia?
```

## Como la preguntan

| Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada |
|---|---|---|---|
| Diagnostico clasico | Que tiene? | dolor periumbilical que migra a RLQ + anorexia + signos | apendicitis aguda |
| Siguiente paso | Imagen o cirugia? | Alvarado/riesgo + peritonismo + paciente especial | cirugia directa vs US/CT |
| Tratamiento a medida | No complicada vs complicada | perforacion, absceso, plastron, peritonitis | appy, antibiotics, drainage, laparotomy/laparoscopy |
| Antibioticos | Profilaxis o terapia? | no complicada vs complicada | cefazolin single dose vs gram-negative/anaerobe coverage |
| Complicaciones | Que puede salir mal? | perforacion, SSI, abscess, sepsis | most likely complication |
| Tumor trap | Appy or right hemicolectomy? | size/location/extension | local rule by tumor size/base |

## Gatillo de reconocimiento

Piensa en apendicitis aguda si el caso tiene:

- pain begins epigastric or periumbilical;
- pain migrates to right iliac fossa/RLQ within hours;
- anorexia;
- nausea/vomiting after the pain;
- low-grade fever;
- McBurney, Blumberg or Rovsing positive;
- leukocytosis with neutrophilia.

Piensa en complicated appendicitis si hay:

- diffuse peritonitis;
- perforation;
- abscess;
- phlegmon/plastron;
- sepsis or shock;
- long evolution with RLQ mass.

**Take-home:** migration is the story. Visceral pain starts central; parietal
peritoneal irritation localizes it to RLQ.

## Guion de la enfermedad

### 1. Por que da

Apendicitis usually begins with obstruction of the appendiceal lumen. This
raises intraluminal pressure, compromises venous drainage, promotes bacterial
proliferation and finally irritates the peritoneum.

| Step | What happens | Clinical clue |
|---|---|---|
| Luminal obstruction | mucus/pressure accumulate | vague visceral pain |
| Venous congestion | wall edema and ischemia | worsening pain |
| Bacterial proliferation | inflammatory response | fever, leukocytosis |
| Parietal irritation | local peritonism | RLQ pain, rebound |
| Progression | perforation/abscess/plastron/peritonitis | toxicity, mass, diffuse signs |

**Take-home:** the pain migrates because the inflammation moves from visceral
afferents to parietal peritoneum.

### 2. A quien le da

| Patient | Exam meaning |
|---|---|
| Young adult male | classic high-yield stem |
| Child/school-age patient | can progress faster and look toxic |
| Fertile woman | must consider pregnancy, ectopic, ovarian torsion, PID |
| Pregnant patient | symptoms/signs are less reliable; image route changes |
| Elderly patient | atypical presentation, higher perforation/neoplasm risk |
| Obese/immunosuppressed patient | lower exam reliability; CT threshold higher |
| Prior appendectomy | stump appendicitis remains possible |

**Take-home:** the same RLQ pain is a different decision in a young man, fertile
woman, pregnant patient or elderly patient.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Finding | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Periumbilical/epigastric pain -> RLQ | classic chronology |
| Anorexia | high-yield associated symptom |
| Vomiting after pain | supports appendicitis; vomiting before pain suggests another cause |
| McBurney | focal RLQ tenderness |
| Blumberg | rebound/peritoneal irritation |
| Rovsing | referred RLQ pain from LLQ pressure |
| Psoas | retrocecal appendix |
| Obturator | pelvic appendix |
| Leukocytosis/neutrophilia | supports but absence does not exclude |
| CRP elevation after 24-48 h | supports inflammation/progression |

**Take-home:** fever and leukocytosis help, but their absence does not safely
rule out appendicitis.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

Start with probability:

```text
classic migration + RLQ peritonism + leukocytosis
-> high probability

RLQ pain without full pattern or special patient
-> intermediate/uncertain probability

diffuse peritonitis or shock
-> source-control emergency
```

Alvarado local rule:

| Score | Local route |
|---|---|
| <=4 | low probability: observation or discharge with safety net |
| 5-6 | indeterminate: imaging |
| 7-8 | high probability: surgery or confirmatory imaging by context |
| 9-10 | very high probability: surgery without further studies |

ENAM/MINSA product rule:

```text
classic case + Alvarado >=7 or clear peritoneal signs
-> urgent appendectomy
-> do not delay with CT as first step
```

Current-guideline modifier:

- WSES 2025 favors clinical risk scores plus imaging to reduce negative
  appendectomy.
- Therefore, for publication we keep the conflict visible:
  - local exam answer: direct surgery in high-certainty classic case;
  - current broader care: risk-based imaging when uncertainty or special
    population exists.

**Take-home:** in ENAM, "classic high-certainty appendicitis" is a surgical
answer; "doubtful/special patient" is an imaging or pregnancy-aware answer.

### 2. Clasificacion

| Form | Findings | Initial route |
|---|---|---|
| Uncomplicated | no perforation, no abscess, no plastron, no diffuse peritonitis | urgent appendectomy, lap preferred |
| Plastron/phlegmon | RLQ inflammatory mass, >5 days, stable, no collection | conservative antibiotics/observation |
| Abscess | localized collection, local card uses >5 cm for drainage | percutaneous drainage + antibiotics |
| Generalized peritonitis | free perforation/diffuse contamination | resuscitation + antibiotics + emergency surgery |
| Stump appendicitis | classic symptoms after prior appendectomy | diagnose and treat as appendicitis |
| Appendiceal tumor found | size/base/mesoappendix decides extent | appendectomy vs right hemicolectomy by rule |

**Take-home:** "complicated" is not one bucket. Plastron, abscess and
peritonitis have different first moves.

### 3. Manejo

#### High-certainty uncomplicated appendicitis

Local exam route:

```text
classic case / Alvarado high / peritonism
-> fluids, analgesia, NPO
-> preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis
-> urgent appendectomy
-> laparoscopy preferred if available
```

Preferred operation:

- laparoscopic appendectomy;
- open McBurney/Rocky-Davis if unstable, fecal peritonitis with shock, or
  resources limited.

Current modifier:

- WSES 2025 says appendectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis can be delayed
  within 24 h without increased adverse outcomes.
- This does not mean ignore surgery; it means short in-hospital delay for safe
  logistics is acceptable.

#### Diagnostic uncertainty

```text
Alvarado 5-6 / atypical / older / obese / immunosuppressed
-> labs + imaging
-> CT abdomen with contrast in adult if feasible
```

Special populations:

- child: ultrasound first;
- fertile woman: pregnancy test and gynecologic differential;
- pregnant: ultrasound first; MRI if ultrasound inconclusive and available;
- if progressive pain persists after negative studies, surgical/laparoscopic
  evaluation may still be required.

#### Antibiotics-only option

Modern evidence allows selected nonoperative antibiotics for uncomplicated
appendicitis, but this is not the default ENAM answer.

Use as current modifier when:

- CT-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis;
- no appendicolith/fecalith if source requires;
- stable patient;
- reliable follow-up;
- shared decision-making;
- no diffuse peritonitis, abscess or perforation.

ENAM-safe default:

```text
uncomplicated classic appendicitis -> appendectomy
```

#### Plastron/phlegmon

Local route:

```text
>5 days RLQ pain + stable + inflammatory mass + no abscess/peritonitis
-> hospital observation
-> antibiotics
-> analgesia/fluids
-> interval appendectomy local 6-8 weeks
```

Trap:

- urgent operation in stable plastron increases morbidity.

#### Abscess

Local route:

```text
localized abscess >5 cm
-> image-guided percutaneous drainage
-> antibiotics covering gram-negatives + anaerobes
-> interval/follow-up plan
```

If drainage is impossible or the patient deteriorates:

- surgery/source control.

#### Peritonitis or sepsis

```text
diffuse peritonitis / shock / free perforation
-> resuscitation
-> broad antibiotics
-> emergency surgery
-> washout/source control
```

**Take-home:** treatment follows anatomy: inflamed appendix gets appy; stable
plastron gets conservative route; drainable abscess gets drainage; diffuse
peritonitis gets emergency surgery.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Complication | High-yield clue | Exam meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Perforation | delayed diagnosis, >24-48 h, worsening toxicity | most frequent untreated complication |
| Abscess | localized collection after perforation | drain if large/local rule >5 cm |
| Plastron/phlegmon | inflammatory mass without collection | conservative route |
| Generalized peritonitis | diffuse rebound/rigidity, sepsis | emergency surgery |
| Surgical site infection | post-appendectomy wound infection | most frequent post-op complication |
| Stump abscess/stump appendicitis | symptoms after prior appendectomy | do not dismiss |
| Fistula | rare, severe complicated context | source-control concern |

**Take-home:** perforation is the main natural-history complication; wound
infection is the main postoperative complication.

### 5. Seguimiento necesario

After uncomplicated appendectomy:

- monitor pain, fever, oral tolerance and wound;
- no postoperative antibiotics if source-control and no complication;
- return precautions for fever, wound infection, worsening abdominal pain.

After complicated appendicitis:

- monitor fever, leukocytes/CRP if used locally, pain and oral tolerance;
- ensure source control;
- short antibiotic course after adequate source control in current guideline
  framing, local duration source-lock pending;
- assess abscess resolution if drained;
- plan interval/follow-up strategy when treated nonoperatively.

After abscess/plastron nonoperative management:

- outpatient follow-up;
- interval appendectomy per local card 6-8 weeks, source-lock pending;
- current WSES 2025 stresses follow-up after abscess NOM to detect neoplasm,
  especially in older adults or atypical course.

**Take-home:** follow-up after abscess is not bureaucracy; it protects against
recurrence and missed neoplasm.

### 6. Pronostico

Good prognosis:

- early diagnosis;
- uncomplicated disease;
- laparoscopic appendectomy;
- adequate prophylaxis;
- no delay beyond safe in-hospital window;
- no perforation or abscess.

Bad prognosis/risk:

- delayed presentation;
- elderly, very young, pregnant or immunosuppressed patient;
- perforation;
- abscess or generalized peritonitis;
- sepsis/shock;
- inadequate anaerobe coverage;
- missed gynecologic/obstetric diagnosis in fertile woman.

**Take-home:** prognosis worsens when inflammation escapes the appendix:
perforation, abscess, peritonitis and sepsis change the whole route.

## Cases at the end

### Case 1

Young man with periumbilical pain that migrates to RLQ, anorexia, nausea after
pain, fever 38 C, McBurney and Blumberg positive, leukocytosis.

Question: next step?

Answer: urgent appendectomy in the local ENAM/MINSA frame, not CT first.

### Case 2

Fertile woman with RLQ pain, doubtful McBurney, normal CBC and unknown last
menstrual period.

Question: first diagnostic priority?

Answer: pregnancy/gynecologic-aware evaluation, including pregnancy test and
ultrasound route, not blind CT first.

### Case 3

Stable patient with 10 days RLQ pain, fever history, tolerates oral intake and
palpable RLQ mass without diffuse peritonitis.

Question: likely form and management?

Answer: appendiceal plastron/phlegmon; conservative hospital management with
antibiotics/observation and interval plan.

### Case 4

After appendectomy for complicated appendicitis, a regimen of cefazolin alone
is proposed.

Question: why is it wrong?

Answer: complicated appendicitis needs gram-negative and anaerobe coverage;
cefazolin alone does not cover the anaerobic component adequately.
units.example: Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder reconocer apendicitis aguda, decidir cuando operar sin imagen, cuando pedir imagen, como manejar apendicitis complicada, que antibiotico usar y que trampas no caer en ENAM/Residentado. La pregunta real es: ```text dolor RLQ -> patron clasico o incierto? -> paciente especial? -> no complicada o complicada? -> apendicectomia, imagen, antibioticos, drenaje o cirugia de emergencia? ``` | Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada | |---|---|---|---| | Diagnostico clasico | Que tiene? | dolor periumbilical que migra a RLQ + anorexia + signo

units.title: Nota - Neumonia
units.body:
# Nota - Neumonia

## Promesa de la nota

Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder reconocer neumonia, confirmar el diagnostico
en el examen, clasificarla por escenario, estratificar severidad, elegir manejo
empirico inicial y separar verdad de examen de verdad clinica actual.

## Take-home global

La pregunta real no es "que antibiotico es para neumonia". La pregunta real es:

```text
tiene neumonia?
-> donde la adquirio?
-> que tan grave esta?
-> que germen o riesgo cambia la cobertura?
-> que hago ahora y que reevalua a las 48-72 h?
```

## Como la preguntan

| Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada |
|---|---|---|---|
| Diagnostico clasico | Que tiene o que lo confirma? | sindrome infeccioso respiratorio + infiltrado/focalidad | Rx torax confirma en examen |
| Agente probable | Quien es el culpable? | lobar vs atipica, edad, alcohol, post-flu, COPD, VIH | S pneumoniae default; modifiers by clue |
| Severidad | Ambulatorio, hospital o UCI? | CURB-65/PSI, hipoxemia, shock, multilobar, confusion | site-of-care route |
| Tratamiento | Que antibiotico empirico? | outpatient vs ward vs ICU; comorbidity; resistant risk | amox/doxy/macrolide modifier; ceftriaxone+azithro; broad only by risk |
| Nosocomial/VAP | CAP, HAP or VAP? | >48 h hospital or >48 h intubation | HAP/VAP route, cultures and local antibiogram |
| Inmunocompromiso | Es PCP u oportunista? | CD4 <200, dry cough, hypoxemia, bilateral pattern | TMP-SMX +/- steroids |
| Complicacion | Por que empeora? | effusion, empyema, abscess, ARDS, sepsis | image/culture/source control by complication |

## Gatillo de reconocimiento

Piensa en neumonia si el stem tiene:

- fever or chills;
- cough with purulent, rusty or dry sputum by phenotype;
- dyspnea or pleuritic chest pain;
- focal crackles, bronchial breath sounds, increased vocal fremitus or dullness;
- leukocytosis or inflammatory markers;
- new infiltrate on chest radiograph.

The minimum exam chain is:

```text
fever/cough/dyspnea + focal chest finding
-> chest radiograph
-> infiltrate/consolidation confirms pneumonia in the stem
```

**Take-home:** symptoms suggest pneumonia; the infiltrate makes the exam answer
stick.

## Guion de la enfermedad

### 1. Por que da

Neumonia is infection of the lower respiratory tract with inflammation in alveoli
or interstitium. In bacterial lobar pneumonia, alveoli fill with inflammatory
exudate. That produces consolidation, impaired gas exchange and shunt/VQ
mismatch. In atypical pneumonia, the pattern is often more interstitial or
patchy, so dry cough and systemic symptoms can dominate.

| Mechanism | What happens | Clinical clue |
|---|---|---|
| Alveolar exudate | airspace fills with neutrophils/protein/pathogen | consolidation, bronchial breath sounds, focal crackles |
| VQ mismatch/shunt | perfused alveoli are poorly ventilated | hypoxemia, tachypnea, low SatO2 |
| Pleural irritation | inflammation reaches pleura | pleuritic pain, friction rub |
| Systemic inflammation | cytokines and bacteremia risk | fever, chills, confusion, hypotension |
| Necrosis/abscess | tissue destruction or obstruction | cavity, foul sputum, persistent fever |

**Take-home:** focal consolidation explains the classic exam signs; gas exchange
failure explains why oxygenation can be more important than the cough.

### 2. A quien le da

| Patient/context | Exam meaning |
|---|---|
| Young healthy adult | classic CAP; pneumococcus or atypical depending pattern |
| Older adult | higher risk, atypical presentation, comorbidity and severe disease |
| COPD/structural lung disease | H influenzae, Moraxella, S pneumoniae; Pseudomonas risk if severe/bronchiectasis/recent antibiotics |
| Diabetes/HTN/older age | still does not erase S pneumoniae in lobar CAP stems |
| Alcohol use/aspiration risk | Klebsiella/anaerobe local framing, aspiration/abscess modifier |
| Post-influenza | S aureus/MRSA risk, necrotizing pattern |
| Recent hospital/IV antibiotics | resistant pathogen risk, especially severe CAP |
| Hospital >48 h | HAP/NIH |
| Mechanical ventilation >48 h | VAP/NAVM |
| HIV CD4 <200 or major immunosuppression | PCP/opportunistic infection route |

**Take-home:** the host changes the pathogen list, but a lobar CAP stem still
often wants pneumococcus unless a stronger clue appears.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Pattern | Findings | Most likely thought |
|---|---|---|
| Typical lobar CAP | acute fever, chills, productive/rusty sputum, pleuritic pain, focal consolidation | S pneumoniae |
| Atypical CAP | insidious fever, dry cough, headache/myalgia, patchy/bilateral infiltrates | Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila, Legionella |
| Legionella | pneumonia plus diarrhea, confusion, hyponatremia, water/AC exposure | macrolide or respiratory FQ |
| Post-influenza necrotizing | flu then severe pneumonia/cavitation/hemoptysis | S aureus/MRSA risk |
| Aspiration/abscess | altered consciousness/dysphagia/tumor, foul sputum, dependent infiltrate or cavity | aspiration pneumonia/abscess |
| HAP/VAP | new infiltrate after hospital/ventilator exposure plus fever, leukocytosis, purulent secretions | resistant hospital flora |
| PCP | HIV/CD4 <200, progressive dyspnea, dry cough, hypoxemia, bilateral ground-glass/interstitial | Pneumocystis jirovecii |

**Take-home:** add the nonpulmonary clues. Diarrhea plus hyponatremia is not
"weird pneumonia"; it is Legionella until proven otherwise.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

#### First move in an exam stem

```text
suspected pneumonia
-> chest radiograph
-> infiltrate/consolidation confirms the clinical suspicion
```

Local Residentado explicitly keyed Rx torax as the exam of choice to confirm a
case with fever, dry cough, pleuritic pain, alcohol use and focal lung findings.

#### What not to use as first confirmation

| Test | Use | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| Sputum culture | severe CAP, MRSA/Pseudomonas risk, HAP/VAP, failure | not routine outpatient confirmation |
| Blood cultures | severe CAP or resistant-risk inpatient CAP | not routine outpatient/nonsevere ward CAP |
| Procalcitonin | may support probability/stewardship in context | do not withhold antibiotics solely because it is low |
| CT chest | complication, alternative diagnosis, nonresolving disease, immunosuppressed nuance | not first exam answer for routine CAP |
| Urinary Legionella antigen | severe CAP, outbreak/travel/water/Legionella clues | not routine for all CAP |
| MRSA nasal PCR | helps deescalate/avoid MRSA coverage in some settings | positive result still needs culture/context |

**Take-home:** Rx confirms the common stem; cultures are for severe, resistant,
hospital or failing disease.

### 2. Clasificacion

| Type | Definition | Usual exam implication |
|---|---|---|
| CAP/NAC | outside hospital or <48 h after admission | community pathogens, route by severity |
| HAP/NIH | >=48 h after admission, not ventilated | hospital flora, culture and antibiogram logic |
| VAP/NAV | >=48 h after intubation/mechanical ventilation | Pseudomonas/MRSA/Acinetobacter risk, ICU logic |
| Aspiration | inhaled oropharyngeal/gastric material | distinguish pneumonitis, pneumonia and abscess |
| Atypical | Mycoplasma/Chlamydophila/Legionella pattern | beta-lactam alone may miss atypicals |
| Opportunistic | immunocompromised host | PCP/CMV/fungal route |
| Severe CAP | one ATS/IDSA major or >=3 minor criteria | ICU-level decision |

**Take-home:** classify by where and in whom it happened. That is what makes the
antibiotic answer defensible.

### 3. Severidad and site of care

#### CURB-65

| Item | Point |
|---|---|
| Confusion | 1 |
| Urea >42 mg/dL or BUN equivalent high | 1 |
| Respiratory rate >=30/min | 1 |
| Blood pressure SBP <90 or DBP <=60 | 1 |
| Age >=65 | 1 |

Local route:

| Score | Exam route |
|---|---|
| 0-1 | outpatient if no red flags |
| 2 | consider admission |
| >=3 | severe/high-risk; historical Residentado item keyed ICU threshold |
| 4-5 | ICU very likely in local card logic |

Current modifier:

- ATS/IDSA adult CAP prefers PSI over CURB-65 for hospitalization decisions.
- ICU intensity should use major/minor severe CAP criteria plus clinical
  judgment.

#### ATS/IDSA severe CAP criteria

Major criteria:

- invasive mechanical ventilation;
- septic shock requiring vasopressors.

Minor criteria:

- RR >=30/min;
- P/F <=250;
- multilobar infiltrates;
- confusion/disorientation;
- BUN >=20 mg/dL;
- leukopenia;
- thrombocytopenia;
- hypothermia;
- hypotension requiring aggressive fluids.

Severe CAP = one major criterion or at least three minor criteria.

**Take-home:** scores guide site. Hypoxemia, shock, mental status and work of
breathing can override the spreadsheet.

### 4. Manejo empirico

#### CAP outpatient

| Situation | Current/teaching route | Local exam modifier |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy adult, no comorbidity | amoxicillin or doxycycline | 2024 RM key used doxycycline |
| Healthy adult, atypical phenotype | doxycycline or macrolide if resistance low | 2019 RM key used clarithromycin |
| Comorbidities or recent antibiotics | amoxicillin-clavulanate plus macrolide/doxy, or respiratory FQ | ENAM card lists amox-clav |
| Penicillin allergy/selected context | doxy, macrolide, respiratory FQ depending severity/resistance | source-lock local policy |

Do not teach macrolide monotherapy as universal. Current adult CAP guidance
allows it only when local pneumococcal macrolide resistance is sufficiently low.

#### CAP ward

Local exam anchor:

```text
hospitalized CAP / ward
-> ceftriaxone + azithromycin
```

Other current accepted route:

- beta-lactam plus macrolide; or
- respiratory fluoroquinolone when appropriate.

#### CAP ICU/severe

```text
severe CAP
-> beta-lactam + macrolide
   or beta-lactam + respiratory fluoroquinolone
-> if MRSA/Pseudomonas risk, add targeted empiric coverage
-> obtain cultures and deescalate at 48 h if negative/improving
```

#### MRSA/Pseudomonas risk

Strong/current risk factors:

- prior respiratory isolation or infection with MRSA or Pseudomonas;
- recent hospitalization plus IV/parenteral antibiotics, especially in severe
  CAP;
- structural lung disease/recent antibiotics can raise concern locally but needs
  context and local antibiogram.

Avoid the outdated shortcut:

```text
old HCAP label
-> automatic broad coverage
```

#### HAP/VAP

```text
HAP/VAP suspected
-> culture respiratory sample when feasible
-> empiric active coverage against S aureus and gram-negative pathogens
-> add MRSA or dual antipseudomonal coverage by local resistance/risk/severity
-> deescalate when cultures return
-> typical duration around 7 days if responding
```

**Take-home:** broad therapy is a bridge, not a destination.

### 5. Complicaciones

| Complication | Clue | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Parapneumonic effusion | pleural fluid with pneumonia | ultrasound/diagnostic thoracentesis if significant |
| Empyema | pus/loculated infected pleural fluid | drainage plus antibiotics |
| Lung abscess | cavity, air-fluid level, foul sputum, obstruction/aspiration | anaerobic/source-control route; source-lock local agent key |
| Necrotizing pneumonia | post-flu, severe toxicity, cavitation | think S aureus/MRSA |
| ARDS | bilateral infiltrates, severe hypoxemia, P/F low | ventilatory/ICU management |
| Sepsis/shock | hypotension, lactate, organ dysfunction | resuscitation, cultures, timely antibiotics |
| Respiratory failure | low SatO2, high work of breathing, altered mentation | oxygen, HFNC/VMNI/intubation by context |

**Take-home:** persistent fever, hypoxemia or nonresolution means the question
may have moved from "which antibiotic" to "what complication/source control".

### 6. Seguimiento

Use clinical stability:

- temperature improving;
- heart rate improving;
- respiratory rate improving;
- blood pressure stable;
- oxygen saturation adequate;
- able to eat;
- normal mentation.

CAP antibiotics should generally continue until clinical stability and at least
5 total days. MRSA/Pseudomonas CAP and HAP/VAP often use about 7 days when
responding, with local/infectious-disease adjustment.

Repeat chest imaging is not routine if symptoms resolve within 5-7 days. Consider
follow-up imaging when:

- symptoms persist or worsen;
- older age and smoking/cancer risk;
- recurrent pneumonia in the same lobe;
- suspected obstruction, abscess or empyema;
- immunosuppressed host or unusual pathogen.

**Take-home:** reassess at 48-72 h. Improvement means narrow/complete; failure
means complication, wrong bug, wrong host or wrong diagnosis.

### 7. Pronostico and prevention

Bad prognosis signals:

- multilobar infiltrates;
- hypoxemia or P/F low;
- shock or need for vasopressors;
- confusion;
- renal dysfunction/uremia;
- leukopenia or thrombocytopenia;
- older age/comorbidity;
- resistant pathogens;
- delayed appropriate therapy.

Prevention boundaries:

- influenza vaccination reduces influenza-associated pneumonia burden;
- pneumococcal vaccination matters, but local Peru schedule must be source-locked
  before final public content;
- aspiration prevention in dysphagia/altered mental status is a systems and
  bedside intervention;
- VAP/NAVM prevention is bundle based: head elevation, oral care, sedation/
  extubation readiness, ventilator-day reduction and infection-control practice.

**Take-home:** mortality is driven less by cough and more by oxygenation,
sepsis, host vulnerability and whether empiric therapy fits the setting.

## One-page algorithm

```text
Suspected pneumonia
|
+-- no infiltrate/focality and mild viral syndrome?
|   -> consider bronchitis/viral URI/COPD/CHF; safety-net
|
+-- infiltrate or focal consolidation present
    -> classify setting:
       CAP / HAP / VAP / aspiration / immunosuppressed
    -> assess severity:
       PSI/CURB-65 + oxygen + BP + mental status + multilobar
    -> route:
       outpatient stable -> amoxicillin or doxy (macrolide only if resistance low)
       ward CAP -> ceftriaxone + azithro local anchor
       severe CAP -> beta-lactam + macrolide/FQ, cultures
       MRSA/Pseudomonas risk -> add targeted empiric coverage, deescalate
       HAP/VAP -> culture, antibiogram, anti-S aureus + gram-negative strategy
       PCP -> TMP-SMX 21 days +/- steroids if hypoxemic
    -> reassess 48-72 h:
       improving -> narrow and complete minimum duration
       failing -> complication, resistant bug, wrong diagnosis, obstruction
```

## Exam red flags

- If the stem asks "examen de eleccion para confirmar" in typical CAP, answer
  Rx torax.
- If the stem says lobar consolidation and asks agent, answer S pneumoniae unless
  a stronger clue appears.
- If the stem says diarrhea + hyponatremia, think Legionella.
- If the stem says post-influenza and necrotizing/cavitary, think S aureus/MRSA.
- If the stem says ward CAP and asks empiric therapy, local anchor is
  ceftriaxone + azithromycin.
- If the stem says CURB-65 and asks severe/ICU historical threshold, remember
  >=3; if it asks modern ICU criteria, use severe CAP major/minor criteria.
- If the stem says VM >=48 h plus new infiltrate plus fever/leukocytosis/
  purulence, think VAP/NAVM.
- If the stem says HIV CD4 <200, dry cough, progressive dyspnea and bilateral
  interstitial/ground-glass pattern, think PCP and TMP-SMX.

## What stays source-locked

- Exact antibiotic doses/durations for local manuals.
- Local macrolide resistance assumption.
- Whether a product should teach clarithromycin as historical exam key or
  relegate it to legacy trap.
- Cavitary/fetid pneumonia key that selected S aureus over anaerobes in one
  Residentado item.
- Adult vaccination schedule in Peru versus CDC US recommendations.
- HAP/VAP recommendations after the expected 2026 update.

La pregunta real no es "que antibiotico es para neumonia". La pregunta real es: ```text tiene neumonia? -> donde la adquirio? -> que tan grave esta? -> que germen o riesgo cambia la cobertura? -> que hago ahora y que reevalua a las 48-72 h? ``` | Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada | |---|---|---|---| | Diagnostico clasico | Que tiene o

units.title: Nota - Traumatismos oculares
units.body:
# Nota - Traumatismos oculares

## Promesa de la nota

Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder ordenar el manejo inicial de trauma ocular,
reconocer lesiones que amenazan vision, elegir la prueba inicial correcta, y
separar abrasion simple de quemadura quimica, globo abierto, hifema o fractura
orbitaria.

## Take-home global

La pregunta real no es "que lesion tiene el ojo". La pregunta real es:

```text
hay algo que pueda destruir vision en minutos o empeorar con mi examen?
```

Por eso el algoritmo empieza con peligro:

```text
quimico -> irrigar
globo abierto -> proteger sin presion
superficie -> fluoresceina/Seidel
camara anterior -> hifema/IOP
orbita -> CT
```

## Como la preguntan

| Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quemadura quimica | Cual es el primer manejo? | acido/alcali/lejia/cemento en ojo | irrigacion inmediata y abundante |
| Globo abierto | Que no debes hacer? | herida penetrante, Seidel, pupila irregular, atalamia | no presion; escudo rigido; CT/oftalmologia |
| Cuerpo extrano intraocular | Que imagen usar? | metal/alta velocidad/penetrante | CT orbitaria; no RM si metal |
| Erosion corneal | Como detectarla? | dolor, lagrimeo, fotofobia, trauma superficial | fluoresceina |
| Seidel positivo | Que significa? | fluoresceina diluida por fuga acuosa | perforacion/open globe hasta demostrar lo contrario |
| Hifema | Que vigilar? | sangre en camara anterior tras golpe | rebleeding, IOP, glaucoma, corneal staining |
| Blow-out | Que patron diagnostica? | diplopia vertical, limitacion al elevar mirada, enoftalmos | fractura de piso orbitario; CT |
| Medial wall exception | Que clave historica recuerda? | dolor con movimiento horizontal | fractura de pared medial en RM 2019 |

## Algoritmo del primer minuto

```text
1. Pregunta: hay quimico?
   - si: irrigar ahora.
   - no esperes historia completa.

2. Pregunta: el globo podria estar abierto?
   - si: escudo rigido, no presion, no tonometria, no US con presion.
   - CT si IOFB/fractura; oftalmologia urgente.

3. Si el globo parece cerrado:
   - agudeza visual si es posible.
   - fluoresceina para abrasion o Seidel.
   - evertir parpados si sospecha cuerpo extrano.

4. Si hay sangre en camara anterior:
   - hifema: cabeza elevada, escudo, evitar NSAIDs/ASA, vigilar IOP.

5. Si hay diplopia, enoftalmos, enfisema o hipoestesia:
   - sospecha fractura orbitaria.
   - CT orbitas.
```

**Take-home:** en trauma ocular, la primera decision es no hacer dano mientras
proteges vision.

## Guion del trauma ocular

### 1. Por que da

El ojo se lesiona por cuatro mecanismos grandes:

| Mecanismo | Que pasa | Lesion que activa |
|---|---|---|
| Quimico | acido/alcali rompe epitelio, cornea y limbo | quemadura quimica |
| Cortante/penetrante | pared ocular se abre o entra cuerpo extrano | globo abierto, IOFB, endoftalmitis |
| Superficial | epitelio corneal se pierde o queda cuerpo extrano | abrasion, erosion, rust ring |
| Contuso | golpe transmite energia a camara anterior u orbita | hifema, blow-out, retinal injury |

El punto mecanistico mas preguntable:

```text
alcali -> necrosis licuefactiva -> penetracion profunda -> peor que acido
```

El acido puede coagular proteinas y limitar algo la penetracion; el alcali
puede atravesar tejidos con mas rapidez. Por eso el manejo no espera.

**Take-home:** el mecanismo predice el peligro: quimico destruye, penetrante
extruye, superficial se marca con fluoresceina, contuso sangra o fractura.

### 2. A quien le da

| Contexto | Lesion probable | Clave de examen |
|---|---|---|
| Lejia, acido, alcali, cemento, limpiador | quemadura quimica | irrigar primero |
| Martilleo metal-metal, explosion, vidrio | IOFB/open globe | CT; no RM si metal |
| Rama, fingernail, polvo, lente de contacto, metal superficial | abrasion/cuerpo extrano | fluoresceina y eversion palpebral |
| Punetazo, pelota, caida | hifema o blow-out | camara anterior u orbita |
| Nino con trauma orbitario y nauseas/bradicardia | trapdoor fracture | entrapment urgente |
| Paciente con anticoagulantes o trastorno hematologico | hifema complicado | mas riesgo de sangrado/IOP |

**Take-home:** ocupacion y mecanismo importan mas que memorizar listas de
sintomas.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Lesion | Presentacion frecuente | Hallazgo que cambia conducta |
|---|---|---|
| Quemadura quimica | dolor intenso, blefaroespasmo, ojo rojo, cornea opaca | pH anormal o limbal ischemia |
| Globo abierto | dolor, baja vision, herida visible, pupila irregular, atalamia | no presion, no tonometria |
| IOFB | antecedente alta velocidad, dolor variable, vision baja | CT; RM prohibida si metal |
| Abrasion corneal | dolor, lagrimeo, fotofobia, sensacion de cuerpo extrano | fluoresceina positiva sin fuga |
| Seidel positivo | fluoresceina diluida/flujo acuoso | perforacion hasta demostrar lo contrario |
| Hifema | sangre visible en camara anterior, vision borrosa, fotofobia | IOP/rebleeding |
| Blow-out piso orbitario | diplopia vertical, limitacion de elevacion, enoftalmos/hipoglobus | CT; entrapment |
| Pared medial | dolor o diplopia horizontal en clave historica | separar de piso orbitario |

**Take-home:** no todos los ojos rojos post-trauma son abrasiones. La fuga,
la sangre, el pH y la diplopia son cambios de carril.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

#### Quemadura quimica

Diagnostico y manejo empiezan juntos:

```text
exposicion quimica
-> irrigacion inmediata
-> retirar particulas si es seguro
-> pH con tira
-> continuar hasta pH fisiologico y estable
-> oftalmologia
```

No esperes a clasificar gravedad antes de irrigar.

#### Globo abierto

Sospecha si hay:

- traumatismo penetrante;
- cuerpo extrano de alta velocidad;
- herida corneal/escleral;
- pupila irregular o en pico;
- camara anterior plana o muy superficial;
- uvea visible;
- hipotonia ocular;
- Seidel positivo;
- disminucion marcada de agudeza visual.

Conducta:

```text
escudo rigido
no presion
no parche compresivo
no tonometria
no ultrasound con presion
CT orbitas si IOFB/fractura
NPO + analgesia/antiemetico + antibiotico/tetano segun protocolo
oftalmologia urgente
```

#### Abrasion y cuerpo extrano superficial

Usa fluoresceina cuando el mecanismo parece superficial y el globo parece
cerrado.

```text
fluoresceina uptake
-> defecto epitelial

fluoresceina diluida en corriente
-> Seidel positivo
-> fuga acuosa/open globe
```

Evertir parpados es obligatorio si hay sensacion persistente de cuerpo extrano
o lineas verticales de abrasion.

#### Hifema

Diagnostico: sangre en camara anterior luego de trauma contuso.

Buscar:

- nivel de sangre visible;
- dolor/fotofobia;
- vision borrosa;
- IOP elevada cuando medir sea seguro;
- lesiones asociadas.

#### Fractura orbitaria

Sospecha blow-out de piso si:

- diplopia vertical;
- limitacion para mirar arriba;
- enoftalmos o hipoglobus;
- dolor con movimiento ocular;
- enfisema/crepito orbital;
- hipoestesia infraorbitaria.

Prueba:

```text
CT orbitas
```

**Take-home:** fluoresceina no reemplaza CT cuando hay IOFB/fractura, y CT no
reemplaza irrigacion cuando hay quimico.

### 2. Clasificacion

| Clase | Subclase util | Que cambia |
|---|---|---|
| Quimica | acido vs alcali; leve/moderada/severa | urgencia de irrigacion, limbo, pronostico |
| Mecanica abierta | penetrante, perforante, IOFB | no presion, CT, antibioticos, cirugia |
| Mecanica cerrada | abrasion, hifema, contusion, retina | fluoresceina, IOP, seguimiento |
| Superficial | abrasion simple, cuerpo extrano, rust ring | remocion, antibiotico topico, control |
| Orbitaria | piso, pared medial, trapdoor | CT, entrapment, cirugia urgente vs diferida |

**Take-home:** la palabra "trauma" no basta. La clasificacion es abierta vs
cerrada, quimica vs mecanica, superficie vs camara vs orbita.

### 3. Manejo

#### Quemadura quimica

Primero:

```text
irrigacion abundante inmediata
```

Luego:

- retirar particulas retenidas en fornices si es seguro;
- medir pH;
- continuar irrigando hasta pH fisiologico;
- analgesia y soporte;
- evaluacion oftalmologica;
- tratamiento antiinflamatorio/antibiotico/cicloplejico segun especialista y
  severidad.

Frase de examen:

```text
lejia en ojo -> lavado ocular inmediato
```

#### Globo abierto / IOFB

Manejo inicial:

- escudo rigido;
- no presionar el ojo;
- no parche compresivo;
- no intentar retirar cuerpo extrano incrustado;
- evitar tonometria;
- evitar ultrasound si sospecha ruptura;
- CT orbitas;
- NPO;
- analgesia y antiemetico;
- antibioticos sistemicos y tetanos segun protocolo;
- oftalmologia para cierre quirurgico.

Frase de examen:

```text
herida penetrante + pupila irregular/Seidel -> proteger, no manipular
```

#### Abrasion/cuerpo extrano superficial

Si no hay signos de globo abierto:

- medir agudeza visual cuando sea posible;
- fluoresceina;
- evertir parpados;
- retirar cuerpo extrano superficial si se cuenta con tecnica segura;
- antibiotico topico segun riesgo;
- analgesia;
- evitar lente de contacto hasta curacion;
- control si lesion central, grande, contact lens, infeccion, vegetales/sucio,
  disminucion visual o dolor persistente.

Patching/occlusion:

- puede aparecer en fuentes locales antiguas para erosiones simples;
- evitarlo si hay contacto lens, agente sucio/vegetal, sospecha infeccion o
  perforacion;
- requiere decision editorial con fuente local antes de publicarlo como regla
  general.

#### Hifema

Manejo inicial:

- escudo ocular;
- reposo relativo;
- cabeza elevada;
- evitar aspirina/NSAIDs/anticoagulantes si es posible y seguro;
- controlar IOP;
- cicloplejico/topico antiinflamatorio segun oftalmologia;
- seguimiento estrecho los primeros dias.

Complicacion mas examinable:

```text
rebleeding day 3-5
```

#### Fractura orbitaria

Manejo:

- CT orbitas;
- evitar sonarse la nariz si hay enfisema orbital;
- analgesia y soporte;
- valorar diplopia, enoftalmos, atrapamiento muscular y nervio optico;
- urgencia si hay trapdoor pediatrico, oculocardiac reflex, entrapment severo,
  nausea/vomitos/bradicardia o compromiso visual;
- reparacion diferida si persisten diplopia/enophthalmos/indicaciones despues
  de bajar edema, segun especialista.

**Take-home:** cada lesion tiene un "no hacer": no retrasar irrigacion, no
presionar globo abierto, no llamar simple a un Seidel positivo, no olvidar IOP
en hifema, no perder trapdoor pediatrico.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Lesion | Complicacion |
|---|---|
| Quemadura quimica | opacidad corneal, simblefaron, glaucoma, limbal stem cell failure, perforacion |
| Globo abierto | endoftalmitis, extrusion, retinal detachment, vision loss |
| IOFB | infeccion, toxicidad metalica, retinal injury |
| Abrasion/cuerpo extrano | ulcera, queratitis infecciosa, recurrent erosion, rust ring |
| Hifema | rebleeding, glaucoma secundario, corneal blood staining |
| Blow-out | diplopia persistente, enoftalmos, atrapamiento muscular, oculocardiac reflex |

**Take-home:** la complicacion que mata la respuesta suele estar en la opcion
que "suena rutinaria": parche, tonometria, demora, RM, o NSAID.

### 5. Seguimiento

| Escenario | Seguimiento minimo conceptual |
|---|---|
| Quemadura quimica | pH estable, cornea/limbo, IOP, oftalmologia |
| Globo abierto | cirugia, antibioticos, signos de endoftalmitis, retina |
| Abrasion simple | revaluar si central/grande, dolor persistente o no mejora |
| Contact lens abrasion | vigilancia de queratitis por Pseudomonas y no patching |
| Hifema | IOP y rebleeding durante primeros dias |
| Fractura orbitaria | diplopia/enoftalmos despues de edema, entrapment, vision |

**Take-home:** el alta sin red flags es parte del manejo. El ojo traumatico que
no mejora rapido vuelve.

### 6. Pronostico

Buen pronostico:

- abrasion pequena, periferica, sin infeccion;
- cuerpo extrano superficial removido sin rust ring importante;
- hifema pequeno sin IOP elevada;
- fractura orbitaria sin entrapment ni diplopia persistente.

Mal pronostico:

- quemadura por alcali con limbal ischemia;
- globo abierto con baja vision inicial o IOFB;
- endoftalmitis;
- hifema total o con IOP elevada;
- pediatric trapdoor no reconocido;
- retinal detachment or optic nerve injury.

**Take-home:** la vision se salva por tiempo y por no hacer dano. Trauma ocular
es una nota de secuencia.

## Tabla rapida de decisiones

| Si el stem dice... | Responde mentalmente... |
|---|---|
| Lejia/alcali/acido en ojo | irrigar ya |
| Dolor + fluoresceina capta | abrasion |
| Fluoresceina se diluye en flujo | Seidel positivo/open globe |
| Penetrante + metal | CT, no RM |
| Pupila en pico/atalamia | open globe, no presion |
| Sangre en camara anterior | hifema, cabeza elevada y IOP |
| Diplopia vertical + enoftalmos | fractura de piso orbitario |
| Dolor horizontal local RM | pared medial, key historica |
| Nino con nausea/bradicardia tras trauma orbital | trapdoor urgente |

## Frase final

```text
El ojo traumatico se resuelve por prioridad:
irrigar lo quimico,
proteger lo abierto,
tenir la superficie,
vigilar la sangre,
tomografiar la orbita.
```
units.example: Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder ordenar el manejo inicial de trauma ocular, reconocer lesiones que amenazan vision, elegir la prueba inicial correcta, y separar abrasion simple de quemadura quimica, globo abierto, hifema o fractura orbitaria. La pregunta real no es "que lesion tiene el ojo". La pregunta real es: ```text hay algo que pueda destruir vision en minutos o empeorar con mi examen? ``` Por eso el algoritmo empieza con peligro: ```text quimico -> irrigar globo abierto -> proteger sin presion superficie -> fluoresceina/Seidel camara anterior -> hifema/IOP orbita -> CT ``` | Fenoti

units.title: Nota - Falla Respiratoria
units.body:
# Nota - Falla Respiratoria

## Promesa de la nota

Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder interpretar una gasometria, clasificar
falla respiratoria tipo I o II, explicar el mecanismo de hipoxemia, diagnosticar
SDRA por criterios de Berlin, y elegir entre oxigeno, HFNC, VMNI o VMI segun el
peligro fisiologico.

## Take-home global

La pregunta real no es "esta disneico?". La pregunta real es:

```text
esta fallando la oxigenacion, la ventilacion o ambas?
```

Y se resuelve asi:

```text
PaO2 -> oxigenacion
PaCO2 -> ventilacion
pH -> agudeza y peligro
D(A-a)O2 -> mecanismo
PaO2/FIO2 -> severidad en SDRA
estado mental/fatiga -> soporte ventilatorio
```

## Como la preguntan

| Fenotipo | Pregunta real | Dato que decide | Respuesta esperada |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tipo I vs II | Como clasificas la falla? | PaO2 y PaCO2 | tipo I si hipoxemia sin hipercapnia; tipo II si hipercapnia |
| Mecanismo | Por que esta hipoxemico? | D(A-a), O2 response, contexto | shunt, V/Q, difusion, hipoventilacion, CO |
| SDRA | Cumple criterios y que severidad? | inicio, bilateralidad, no cardiogenico, PaFI | Berlin leve/moderado/grave |
| Soporte inicial | Que hago ahora? | PaFI, trabajo respiratorio, mental status | O2/HFNC/NIV/VMI |
| COPD hipercapnico | NIV o intubacion? | pH, PaCO2, cooperacion, contraindicaciones | VMNI si acidosis y candidato |
| CO/incendio | Por que PaO2 normal no tranquiliza? | carboxihemoglobina | 100% O2, COHgb |
| Neumotorax pequeno | Que manejo historico? | post-CVC <10%, estable | oxigeno complementario local key |

## Algoritmo de 30 segundos

```text
1. Leer PaO2:
   - <60 en aire ambiente = falla respiratoria.

2. Leer PaCO2:
   - >50 = tipo II / ventilatoria.
   - normal o baja = tipo I / hipoxemica.

3. Leer pH:
   - acidemia = hipercapnia aguda o descompensada.

4. Calcular D(A-a)O2 si el stem lo pide:
   - normal = hipoventilacion pura o bajo FiO2.
   - alto = shunt, V/Q o difusion.

5. Calcular PaFI si hay FIO2:
   - 201-300 leve.
   - 101-200 moderado.
   - <=100 grave.

6. Elegir soporte:
   - COPD acidosis candidato = VMNI.
   - SDRA grave/fatiga/bajo GCS = VMI.
```

**Take-home:** el examen de falla respiratoria premia leer gases en orden, no
recordar un dispositivo suelto.

## Guion de la enfermedad

### 1. Por que da

Falla respiratoria ocurre cuando el sistema respiratorio no puede mantener
oxigenacion, ventilacion o ambas. El problema puede estar en el alveolo, la
perfusion, la membrana, el centro respiratorio, los musculos, la caja toracica
o la hemoglobina.

| Funcion que falla | Variable | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Oxigenacion | PaO2 baja | hipoxemia, tipo I |
| Ventilacion | PaCO2 alta | hipercapnia, tipo II |
| Intercambio alveolocapilar | D(A-a)O2 alta | shunt, V/Q, difusion |
| Bomba respiratoria | PaCO2 alta + A-a normal | hipoventilacion pura |
| Transporte de O2 | COHgb alta | PaO2 normal puede enganchar |

El concepto preguntable:

```text
PaO2 mide oxigeno disuelto.
SpO2 estima saturacion de hemoglobina.
Contenido arterial de O2 depende sobre todo de hemoglobina y saturacion.
```

Por eso CO puede generar hipoxia tisular con PaO2 normal.

**Take-home:** PaO2, PaCO2 y contenido de oxigeno no son lo mismo. Esa
diferencia explica varias trampas.

### 2. A quien le da

| Contexto | Ruta probable |
|---|---|
| Neumonia, atelectasia, edema, SDRA | tipo I por shunt/VQ |
| EPOC agudizado | tipo II o mixto, VMNI si candidato |
| Opioides/sedantes | hipoventilacion pura, CO2 alto y A-a normal |
| Neuromuscular, miastenia, Guillain-Barre | bomba falla antes que Rx impresione |
| Sepsis, pancreatitis, trauma, aspiracion | SDRA |
| Incendio/humo/generador | CO, inhalacion, cianuro, lesion de via aerea |
| CVC subclavio, trauma, espontaneo | neumotorax |
| Embarazo/obstetricia severa | complicacion respiratoria, derivacion/soporte |

**Take-home:** el contexto te dice si el problema es pulmon, bomba,
hemoglobina, pleura o injuria sistemica.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Patron | Hallazgos | Piensa |
|---|---|---|
| Tipo I | PaO2 baja, PaCO2 normal/baja, taquipnea | intercambio falla |
| Tipo II | PaO2 baja + PaCO2 alta, pH bajo si aguda | ventilacion falla |
| Hipoventilacion pura | bradipnea/somnolencia, CO2 alto, A-a normal | opioide, CNS, NM |
| SDRA | bilateral infiltrates, PaFI <=300, no edema cardiogenico | shunt, baja compliance |
| CO poisoning | incendio, headache/confusion, PaO2 normal posible | COHgb |
| COPD acidotico | disnea, wheeze, CO2 alto, pH bajo | VMNI si candidato |
| Fatiga respiratoria | FR alta luego baja, tiraje, altered mental status | intubacion |

**Take-home:** trabajo respiratorio y estado mental pesan tanto como la
saturacion.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

#### Definicion local de examen

Respirando aire ambiente a nivel del mar:

```text
PaO2 <60 mmHg and/or PaCO2 >50 mmHg
```

#### Tipo I vs tipo II

| Tipo | Gasometria | Mecanismo primario |
|---|---|---|
| Tipo I / hipoxemica | PaO2 <60, PaCO2 normal o baja | intercambio: shunt, V/Q, difusion |
| Tipo II / hipercapnica | PaO2 <60 + PaCO2 >50 | ventilacion alveolar insuficiente |
| Mixta | PaO2 baja + PaCO2 alta + A-a alta | bomba y pulmon a la vez |

#### D(A-a)O2

Formula local rapida en aire ambiente:

```text
PAO2 = 150 - 1.25 x PaCO2
D(A-a)O2 = PAO2 - PaO2
```

Interpretacion:

| Gradiente | Significado |
|---|---|
| normal | hipoventilacion pura o baja FiO2 |
| alto | V/Q, shunt o difusion |

Ejemplo local:

```text
sobredosis de heroina + respiraciones bajas
-> CO2 elevado
-> D(A-a)O2 normal
-> hipoventilacion pura
```

#### PaO2/FIO2

```text
PaFI = PaO2 / FIO2
```

Si FIO2 = 50%, usa 0.50, no 50.

**Take-home:** primero clasificas, luego explicas. No al reves.

### 2. Clasificacion

#### Mecanismos de hipoxemia

| Mecanismo | D(A-a)O2 | PaCO2 | Responde a O2 | Ejemplo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hipoventilacion | normal | alta | si | opioides, NM |
| V/Q mismatch | alta | variable | si/parcial | COPD, asma, TEP |
| Shunt | alta | normal/baja | pobre | SDRA, neumonia, atelectasia |
| Difusion | alta | normal/baja | si | intersticial, enfisema |
| Baja FiO2 | normal | baja/normal | si | altura |
| Dyshemoglobin | variable | no explica todo | PaO2 puede ser normal | CO |

#### SDRA Berlin

Los cuatro criterios:

1. Inicio dentro de 1 semana de injuria conocida o empeoramiento respiratorio.
2. Opacidades bilaterales en Rx o CT no explicadas por derrame, colapso o
   nodulos.
3. Edema no explicado por falla cardiaca o sobrecarga de volumen.
4. PaO2/FIO2 con PEEP >=5:

| Severidad | PaO2/FIO2 |
|---|---|
| Leve | 201-300 |
| Moderado | 101-200 |
| Grave | <=100 |

Current modifier:

- La definicion global 2024 propone expandir Berlin usando SpO2/FIO2, HFNO y
  ultrasonido pulmonar en ciertos contextos.
- Para ENAM/RM, usar Berlin salvo que la pregunta indique otra norma.

**Take-home:** Berlin es el idioma del examen; global 2024 es el idioma actual
que debe aparecer como modificador, no como sustitucion silenciosa.

### 3. Manejo

#### Oxigeno

Regla actual de seguridad:

| Paciente | Target conceptual |
|---|---|
| Acutely ill sin riesgo hipercapnico | SpO2 94-98% |
| COPD o riesgo de falla hipercapnica | SpO2 88-92% hasta ABG |
| CO poisoning sospechado | 100% O2 mientras se confirma/descarta |
| ENCAPS referencia | Sat <90% con O2 o RR >30 persistente = referencia |

No conviertas "dar oxigeno" en "dar FiO2 100% para siempre". Oxigeno se titula,
excepto en situaciones especiales como CO.

#### HFNC

Uso conceptual:

- acute hypoxemic respiratory failure sin cardiogenic edema ni COPD
  exacerbation puede beneficiarse de HFNC frente a oxigeno convencional.
- necesita monitorizacion estrecha.
- si falla o hay fatiga/altered mental status, no debe retrasar intubacion.

#### VMNI / NIV

La indicacion clasica:

```text
COPD agudizado + PaCO2 alta + pH <=7.35 + paciente cooperador
-> BiPAP / VMNI
```

Tambien puede usarse en edema pulmonar cardiogenico si el paciente es candidato.

No usar o tener umbral bajo de intubacion si:

- paro respiratorio;
- bajo nivel de conciencia grave;
- shock/inestabilidad;
- vomitos o alto riesgo de aspiracion;
- trauma facial;
- obstruccion de via aerea superior;
- secreciones que no puede manejar;
- falla de VMNI;
- SDRA grave con PaFI muy bajo y alto trabajo respiratorio.

#### VMI / intubacion

Indicar si:

- GCS bajo, coma, estupor o no protege via aerea;
- fatiga o trabajo respiratorio extremo;
- FR >30 persistente o bradipnea peligrosa;
- SatO2 <90 con O2 o PaO2 <60 pese a soporte;
- PaO2/FIO2 <200 con deterioro, y muy especialmente PaFI 100;
- hipercapnia progresiva con pH <7.25;
- contraindica o fracasa VMNI.

#### SDRA

Manejo central:

```text
VMI protectora
-> Vt bajo por peso ideal/predicho
-> plateau <30 cmH2O
-> PEEP adecuada
-> FiO2 minima para target
-> prone si grave/moderado-severo
-> tratar causa
```

Local exam anchor:

```text
pancreatitis + bilateral infiltrates + PaFI 100
-> VMI
```

Current modifier:

- ATS 2024 sugiere corticoides en ARDS de forma condicional.
- ATS 2024 sugiere VV-ECMO en pacientes seleccionados con SDRA severo.
- ATS 2024 sugiere bloqueadores neuromusculares en SDRA temprano severo.
- ATS 2024 sugiere PEEP mas alta sin maniobras prolongadas de reclutamiento en
  SDRA moderado-severo.

Como el CTO local dice "no corticoides rutinarios", esta seccion queda
source-locked para manual.

#### CO poisoning

Claves:

```text
incendio + sintomas + SpO2 baja o discordante + PaO2 normal posible
-> COHgb
-> 100% oxygen
```

No confies en pulsioximetria convencional. CO forma carboxihemoglobina y puede
hacer que el contenido de oxigeno sea bajo aunque la PaO2 sea normal.

#### Neumotorax pequeno local

Local item:

```text
post-CVC subclavio + neumotorax <10% + estable
-> oxigeno complementario
```

No generalizar:

- tension pneumothorax = descompresion urgente.
- grande/sintomatico/inestable = drenaje segun protocolo.

**Take-home:** el dispositivo correcto es consecuencia de la fisiologia y del
riesgo de fatiga, no una preferencia de estilo.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Problema | Complicacion |
|---|---|
| Hipoxemia sostenida | arritmias, isquemia, encefalopatia, paro |
| Hipercapnia aguda | acidosis, somnolencia, coma, paro |
| SDRA | VILI, barotrauma, shock, fibrosis, muerte |
| VMNI mal indicada | aspiracion, retraso de intubacion |
| Oxigeno liberal | hiperoxia, retencion CO2 en susceptibles |
| CO poisoning | dano neurologico tardio, lesion cardiaca |
| Neumotorax | tension, colapso, deterioro hemodinamico |

**Take-home:** la falla respiratoria mata por gases, fatiga y decisiones
tardias.

### 5. Seguimiento

| Escenario | Monitorizacion |
|---|---|
| Oxigeno suplementario | SpO2, FR, trabajo respiratorio, target |
| Riesgo hipercapnico | ABG/VBG segun protocolo, PaCO2, pH |
| VMNI | respuesta clinica y ABG temprana, tolerancia, fuga, mental status |
| VMI/SDRA | PaFI, plateau, PEEP/FIO2, sincronia, barotrauma |
| CO poisoning | COHgb, neuro, ECG/troponina si severo, seguimiento neuro |
| Neumotorax pequeno | sintomas, imagen de control segun protocolo |
| Referencia ENCAPS | SatO2, FR, posicion Fowler, traslado monitorizado |

**Take-home:** si el soporte no baja trabajo respiratorio ni corrige gases,
hay que escalar.

### 6. Pronostico

Mejor pronostico:

- hipoventilacion reversible;
- COPD con acidosis moderada que responde a VMNI;
- causa tratable sin shock;
- SDRA leve/moderado que mejora con soporte temprano.

Peor pronostico:

- PaFI <=100;
- shock/sepsis persistente;
- bajo nivel de conciencia;
- retraso de intubacion cuando la VMNI falla;
- hipercapnia con acidemia severa;
- CO con perdida de conciencia, acidosis, embarazo o compromiso cardiaco;
- barotrauma o VILI.

**Take-home:** el numero no reemplaza al paciente: gases, tendencia y fatiga
mandan juntos.

## Tabla rapida de decisiones

| Si el stem dice... | Responde mentalmente... |
|---|---|
| PaO2 55, PaCO2 35 | tipo I |
| PaO2 55, PaCO2 60 | tipo II |
| CO2 alto + A-a normal | hipoventilacion pura |
| heroina + bradipnea | CO2 elevado, A-a normal |
| incendio + PaO2 normal + SpO2 baja | COHgb/carboxihemoglobina |
| pancreatitis + bilateral infiltrates + PaFI 100 | SDRA grave, VMI |
| COPD + pH 7.28 + CO2 alto + despierto | VMNI/BiPAP |
| GCS bajo o fatiga | intubacion |
| shunt | mala respuesta a O2 |
| post-CVC neumotorax <10% estable | oxigeno local key |

## Frase final

```text
Falla respiratoria se resuelve leyendo:
O2 para oxigenacion,
CO2 para ventilacion,
A-a para mecanismo,
PaFI para SDRA,
y fatiga para intubar.
```
units.example: Al terminar, el estudiante debe poder interpretar una gasometria, clasificar falla respiratoria tipo I o II, explicar el mecanismo de hipoxemia, diagnosticar SDRA por criterios de Berlin, y elegir entre oxigeno, HFNC, VMNI o VMI segun el peligro fisiologico. La pregunta real no es "esta disneico?". La pregunta real es: ```text esta fallando la oxigenacion, la ventilacion o ambas? ``` Y se resuelve asi: ```text PaO2 -> oxigenacion PaCO2 -> ventilacion pH -> agudeza y peligro D(A-a)O2 -> mecanismo PaO2/FIO2 -> severidad en SDRA estado mental/fatiga -> soporte ventilatorio ``` | Fenotipo | Pregun
