units.title: Cardiopatia isquemica
units.body:
# Cardiopatia isquemica

## Uso de esta nota

Esta es una nota de enfermedad/condicion para aprendizaje USAMEDIC. Sirve para
estudiantes y como ground truth interno de clases/manuales, pero queda en
`qa_pending` porque mezcla verdad local de examen con guias cardiologicas
actuales.

Modelo nuclear:

`dolor toracico -> ECG -> STEMI/NSTE/chronic -> troponina -> riesgo -> reperfusion`.

---

# Guion de la enfermedad

## 1. Por que da

Cardiopatia isquemica ocurre cuando el miocardio recibe menos oxigeno del que
necesita. La causa mas comun es aterosclerosis coronaria.

Mecanismos principales:

| Mecanismo | Resultado clinico |
|---|---|
| Estenosis fija coronaria | Angina estable con esfuerzo. |
| Ruptura/erosion de placa + trombo no oclusivo | SCASEST: angina inestable o NSTEMI. |
| Ruptura/erosion de placa + trombo oclusivo | SCACEST/STEMI con necrosis transmural. |
| Espasmo coronario | Angina vasoespastica/Prinzmetal. |
| Disfuncion microvascular | INOCA/angina microvascular. |
| Demanda aumentada o oferta reducida sin ruptura de placa | MI tipo 2 o lesion miocardica. |

La placa vulnerable tiene capa fibrosa delgada, nucleo lipidico abundante e
inflamacion. Cuando se rompe o erosiona, expone material trombogenico, activa
plaquetas y genera trombo.

Cadena del SCA:

```text
placa vulnerable
  -> ruptura/erosion
  -> activacion plaquetaria + trombina
  -> trombo
  -> oclusion parcial = SCASEST
  -> oclusion completa = SCACEST
```

Take-home: la misma placa puede dar angina inestable, NSTEMI o STEMI; la
diferencia de examen la ponen ECG, troponina y grado de oclusion.

## 2. A quien le da

Perfil clasico:

- Hombre mayor de 45-50 anos.
- Mujer postmenopausica o diabetica.
- HTA.
- Diabetes mellitus.
- Tabaquismo.
- Dislipidemia.
- Obesidad y sedentarismo.
- Enfermedad renal cronica.
- Historia familiar de enfermedad coronaria precoz.
- Enfermedad cardiovascular previa.

Grupos donde la presentacion puede ser atipica:

| Grupo | Presentacion que no debes perder |
|---|---|
| Diabeticos | Disnea, nauseas, sudoracion, debilidad, dolor minimo. |
| Mujeres | Dolor epigastrico, disnea, fatiga, sintomas menos clasicos. |
| Ancianos | Sincope, delirium, disnea, caida funcional. |
| ERC | Troponina basal puede estar elevada; importa cambio dinamico y contexto. |

Take-home: el examen ama al varon hipertenso/fumador con dolor opresivo, pero
la clinica peligrosa esta en diabeticos, mujeres, ancianos y ERC.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Dolor anginoso tipico

Tres datos:

1. Dolor retroesternal opresivo.
2. Desencadenado por esfuerzo o estres/frio.
3. Alivia con reposo o nitroglicerina.

Si tiene los tres: angina tipica.
Si tiene dos: angina atipica.
Si tiene uno o ninguno: dolor no anginoso.

### Fenotipos clinicos de examen

| Fenotipo | Dolor | ECG | Troponina | Clave |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Angina estable | Esfuerzo, predecible, dura minutos, alivia con reposo/nitro. | Normal o cambios de isquemia con esfuerzo. | Normal. | Estenosis fija. |
| Angina inestable | Reposo, reciente, progresiva o mas intensa. | ST bajo/T invertida o normal. | Normal. | ACS sin necrosis. |
| NSTEMI | Dolor ACS. | ST bajo/T invertida o normal. | Elevada con dinamica. | Necrosis subendocardica. |
| STEMI | Dolor >20 min, vegetativo, no cede. | ST elevado territorial o equivalente. | Sube, pero no esperar para reperfundir. | Oclusion coronaria. |
| Prinzmetal | Reposo/nocturno, episodico. | ST elevado transitorio durante dolor. | Usualmente normal. | Espasmo. |
| Tipo 2 MI | Dolor o disnea en anemia/sepsis/shock/taquiarritmia. | Variable. | Elevada con dinamica. | Oferta-demanda, no placa rota. |

Take-home: el primer filtro no es la troponina; es si el ECG ya te obliga a
reperfundir.

---

# Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Primer movimiento ante dolor toracico

```text
dolor toracico sospechoso
  -> evaluar estabilidad
  -> ECG en menos de 10 min
  -> monitor/desfibrilador si alto riesgo
  -> acceso IV y signos vitales
  -> troponina seriada si no hay STEMI claro
```

No esperes troponina si el ECG muestra STEMI claro.

### Criterio operativo de infarto

Infarto de miocardio requiere:

1. Troponina cardiaca con elevacion y/o descenso, con al menos un valor sobre
   el percentil 99.
2. Evidencia de isquemia: sintomas, ECG, imagen o trombo coronario.

Regla fina: troponina alta sin clinica isquemica puede ser lesion miocardica o
MI tipo 2, no automaticamente NSTEMI tipo 1.

### Troponina

| Dato | Uso |
|---|---|
| Troponina T/I | Marcador mas sensible y especifico de necrosis miocardica. |
| Inicio clasico de elevacion | 3-4 h despues de sintomas en examenes tradicionales. |
| Duracion | Puede permanecer elevada hasta 1-2 semanas. |
| CK-MB | Menos especifica; puede ayudar si sospecha reinfarto. |
| High-sensitivity troponin | Permite protocolos mas tempranos; requiere contexto clinico. |

### ECG de STEMI

Criterio local clasico:

- ST elevado persistente >=1 mm en al menos 2 derivaciones contiguas.
- En V7-V9 o V3R/V4R, umbral menor local: >=0.5 mm.
- BRCIHH/BCRIHH nuevo con dolor toracico se maneja como STEMI en framing
  clasico de examen, aunque la practica moderna exige interpretacion contextual.

### ECG por territorio

| Territorio | Derivaciones | Arteria probable | Pista de examen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anterior | V1-V4/V5 | Descendente anterior | Infarto grande, peor pronostico. |
| Lateral | I, aVL, V5-V6 | Circunfleja/diagonal | Puede ser sutil. |
| Inferior | II, III, aVF | Coronaria derecha mas frecuente | Buscar VD con V3R/V4R. |
| Posterior | ST bajo V1-V2; ST alto V7-V9 | Circunfleja o derecha | Imagen especular. |
| Ventriculo derecho | V3R/V4R | Coronaria derecha | Hipotension + pulmones limpios. |

### Diagnostico de angina estable

La angina estable es clinica cuando el patron es tipico. Luego se estratifica:

- ECG basal.
- Prueba funcional si probabilidad intermedia y paciente puede ejercitar.
- Eco de estres, perfusion miocardica o imagen coronaria segun disponibilidad.
- Coronariografia si alto riesgo, mala respuesta al tratamiento o datos de mal
  pronostico.

Take-home: ECG primero; troponina confirma necrosis, pero no debe retrasar la
reperfusion en STEMI.

## 2. Clasificacion

### Clasificacion grande

| Grupo | Entidades |
|---|---|
| Sindromes coronarios cronicos | Angina estable, isquemia silente, angina microvascular/INOCA. |
| ACS sin elevacion ST | Angina inestable, NSTEMI. |
| ACS con elevacion ST | STEMI/SCACEST. |
| Vasoespastica | Angina de Prinzmetal. |
| No tipo 1 | MI tipo 2, lesion miocardica no isquemica. |

### Angina estable vs inestable

| Rasgo | Estable | Inestable |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | Esfuerzo, frio, estres. | Reposo o menor esfuerzo. |
| Curso | Predecible. | Nuevo, progresivo o crescendo. |
| Duracion | Minutos, <20 min. | Mas prolongado o recurrente. |
| Troponina | Normal. | Normal. |
| Riesgo | Cronico. | ACS. |

### NSTEMI vs angina inestable

La diferencia es troponina:

- Troponina elevada con dinamica: NSTEMI.
- Troponina normal: angina inestable.

El ECG puede ser igual en ambos: ST bajo, T invertida o incluso normal.

### Riesgo en NSTE-ACS

| Riesgo | Criterios locales | Conducta |
|---|---|---|
| Muy alto | Shock, IC aguda, arritmias malignas, dolor refractario, cambios ECG dinamicos recurrentes. | Coronariografia urgente <2 h. |
| Alto | NSTEMI confirmado, cambios dinamicos ST/T, troponina positiva, GRACE >140. | Estrategia invasiva precoz <24 h. |
| Intermedio/bajo | Sin criterios previos. | Prueba de isquemia o coronariografia diferida/selectiva. |

### Fenotipos ENAM/Residentado

| Fenotipo | Que suelen pedir |
|---|---|
| P01 | Reconocer angina estable, IAMCEST, IAMSEST, Prinzmetal. |
| P09 | Tratamiento segun escenario: antiagregacion, reperfusion, antianginoso, VD, Prinzmetal. |
| P03 | Siguiente paso: ECG, PCI, fibrinolisis, rescate, coronariografia. |
| P18 | Interpretar ECG, territorio, troponina, aneurisma ventricular. |
| E10.M02 | Prueba inicial: ECG en dolor toracico. |
| E06.M04 | Complicacion: shock, insuficiencia cardiaca, ruptura, VD. |

Take-home: estable/inestable se separa por curso; NSTEMI/angina inestable se
separa por troponina; STEMI se separa por ECG y tiempo.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Manejo inicial de sospecha de ACS

| Paso | Conducta |
|---|---|
| 1 | Monitorizacion, desfibrilador disponible, 2 vias si critico. |
| 2 | ECG en <10 min; repetir si persiste sospecha. |
| 3 | AAS carga si no hay alergia/contraindicacion. |
| 4 | Oxigeno solo si SatO2 <90%, dificultad respiratoria o hipoxemia. |
| 5 | Nitrato si dolor/HTA y no hay hipotension, sospecha de VD o uso reciente de PDE5. |
| 6 | Estatina de alta intensidad desde fase aguda. |
| 7 | Anticoagulacion parenteral si ACS. |
| 8 | Elegir ruta: STEMI reperfusion, NSTE invasiva segun riesgo, cronico tratamiento medico. |

Morfina: usar si dolor intenso refractario; no como rutina automatica.

### B. STEMI / SCACEST

Pregunta clave: puede recibir PCI primaria a tiempo?

| Escenario | Conducta |
|---|---|
| PCI primaria disponible en ventana local <2 h | PCI primaria con stent, ideal puerta-balon rapido. |
| PCI no disponible en ventana local y sintomas <12 h | Fibrinolisis si no hay contraindicaciones. |
| Fibrinolisis exitosa | Coronariografia 2-24 h. |
| Fibrinolisis fallida | PCI de rescate urgente. |
| Shock cardiogenico | Revascularizacion urgente de vaso culpable; soporte vasoactivo/inotropico. |

Fibrinolisis exitosa:

- Dolor mejora.
- ST baja >=50% a los 60-90 min.
- Puede aparecer arritmia de reperfusion.

Contraindicaciones absolutas clasicas de fibrinolisis:

- Hemorragia activa.
- Hemorragia intracraneal previa.
- Ictus isquemico reciente.
- Lesion cerebral estructural.
- Trauma grave o cirugia mayor reciente.
- Sospecha de diseccion aortica.

Tratamiento concomitante local:

| Farmaco | Regla local |
|---|---|
| AAS | 150-300 mg carga, luego 100 mg/dia indefinido. |
| P2Y12 | Ticagrelor, prasugrel o clopidogrel segun estrategia, riesgo y disponibilidad. |
| Heparina | Acompana reperfusion/PCI segun protocolo. |
| Estatina | Alta intensidad desde el primer dia. |
| IECA/ARA-II | Temprano si IAM extenso, FEVI baja, DM, HTA o ERC si tolera. |
| Beta-bloqueador | Cuando estable; evitar en IC aguda, shock, bradicardia, bloqueo, hipotension. |
| Antagonista mineralocorticoide | FEVI <40% + IC o DM si K/funcion renal lo permiten. |

Tenecteplasa local CTO:

| Peso | Dosis |
|---|---|
| <60 kg | 30 mg IV bolo |
| 60-69 kg | 35 mg IV bolo |
| 70-79 kg | 40 mg IV bolo |
| 80-89 kg | 45 mg IV bolo |
| >=90 kg | 50 mg IV bolo maximo |

Take-home: STEMI no es una "troponina positiva"; es una arteria que se esta
cerrando y necesita reperfusion.

### C. NSTE-ACS: NSTEMI / angina inestable

Ruta:

```text
sin ST elevado
  -> troponina seriada + ECG seriado
  -> clasificar riesgo
  -> anticoagular + antiagregar
  -> estrategia invasiva segun riesgo
```

Antiagregacion:

| Farmaco | Dosis local |
|---|---|
| AAS | 150-300 mg carga; 100 mg/dia mantenimiento. |
| Ticagrelor | 180 mg carga; 90 mg cada 12 h. |
| Prasugrel | 60 mg carga; 10 mg cada 24 h; evitar si ictus previo. |
| Clopidogrel | 600 mg carga; 75 mg cada 24 h; opcion si alto sangrado/disponibilidad. |

Punto fino actual: si NSTE-ACS ira a estrategia invasiva, el momento de P2Y12
puede depender de si se conoce anatomia, riesgo de sangrado, posibilidad de
CABG y demora a angiografia. Por eso esta parte queda source-lock.

Anticoagulacion local:

| Farmaco | Uso |
|---|---|
| Fondaparinux | Preferido local si angiografia no precoz o manejo conservador. |
| Enoxaparina | Alternativa habitual. |
| Heparina no fraccionada | Durante PCI o si se requiere control rapido. |
| Bivalirudina | Alternativa en PCI con alto riesgo hemorragico. |

Duracion DAPT:

- Default tras ACS: 12 meses si no hay alto riesgo de sangrado.
- Puede acortarse o modificarse si riesgo hemorragico alto, necesidad de
  anticoagulacion o decisiones post-PCI.

Take-home: NSTE-ACS no siempre va al cath lab igual de rapido; el riesgo manda
el reloj.

### D. Angina estable / enfermedad coronaria cronica

Objetivos:

1. Reducir eventos cardiovasculares.
2. Controlar sintomas.
3. Identificar pacientes que necesitan revascularizacion.

Medidas de pronostico:

| Intervencion | Uso |
|---|---|
| Cese de tabaco | Prioridad maxima. |
| Actividad fisica/cardiorehabilitacion | Reduce eventos y mejora calidad de vida. |
| Estatina alta intensidad | LDL objetivo local/ESC: <55 mg/dL en muy alto riesgo. |
| AAS | Prevencion secundaria si enfermedad coronaria establecida y bajo riesgo de sangrado. |
| IECA/ARA-II | Post-IAM, HTA, DM, ERC, FEVI baja. |
| Control HTA/DM/peso | Base de prevencion secundaria. |

Antianginosos:

| Situacion | Opcion |
|---|---|
| Examen clasico | Beta-bloqueador como eleccion. |
| Guia moderna CCD | Beta-bloqueador o calcioantagonista como primera linea antianginosa. |
| Crisis | Nitrato sublingual. |
| Prinzmetal | Calcioantagonista +/- nitrato; evitar beta-bloqueador. |
| Angina + HTA en ENCAPS | Amlodipino/BCC es opcion util. |

Revascularizacion:

| Anatomia/escenario | Preferencia clasica |
|---|---|
| 1-2 vasos | PCI con stent farmacoactivo si sintomas o isquemia significativa. |
| 3 vasos | CABG o decision Heart Team segun complejidad. |
| Tronco coronario izquierdo | CABG o PCI seleccionada segun anatomia. |
| Diabetico multivaso | CABG favorecida, sobre todo si FEVI reducida. |
| Mala respuesta a tratamiento medico | Coronariografia y evaluar revascularizacion. |

Take-home: en cronico, las estatinas y factores de riesgo salvan pronostico; los
antianginosos mejoran sintomas; revascularizar depende de anatomia, riesgo y
sintomas.

### E. Prinzmetal

Datos clave:

- Dolor en reposo, a menudo nocturno.
- ST elevado transitorio durante el episodio.
- Coronarias sin ateromatosis significativa o con espasmo.
- Puede asociarse a vasorreactividad como Raynaud/migrana.

Manejo:

- Calcioantagonistas.
- Nitratos.
- Evitar tabaco/cocaina.
- Evitar beta-bloqueadores no selectivos o uso reflejo de beta-bloqueador.

Take-home: Prinzmetal se parece a STEMI en el ST, pero la pelicula es episodica
y vasoespastica.

## 4. Complicaciones

| Complicacion | Pista | Conducta/idea |
|---|---|---|
| Fibrilacion ventricular | Muerte subito temprana. | Desfibrilacion/RCP. |
| Insuficiencia cardiaca | S3, disnea, congestiones, bajo gasto. | Diureticos/vasodilatadores si tolera, soporte y revascularizacion si ACS. |
| Shock cardiogenico | Hipotension, piel fria, oliguria, lactato alto. | Revascularizacion urgente + soporte; local exam puede pedir dobutamina. |
| Infarto de VD | Inferior + hipotension + JVD + pulmones limpios. | Fluidos; no nitratos, no diureticos. |
| Ruptura papilar | Soplo sistolico nuevo + edema pulmonar agudo. | Cirugia urgente. |
| CIV post-IAM | Soplo sistolico nuevo + shock/EAP. | Cirugia urgente. |
| Ruptura pared libre | Taponamiento, PEA. | Catastrofico; cirugia si posible. |
| Bloqueo AV completo | Mas en IAM inferior. | Atropina/marcapasos segun estabilidad. |
| Aneurisma ventricular | ST persistente semanas + ondas Q. | Riesgo de trombo, IC, arritmia. |
| Pericarditis post-IAM | Dolor pleuritico/posicional. | Diferenciar de reinfarto. |

Take-home: despues del IAM, un soplo nuevo o hipotension no explicada es una
complicacion hasta demostrar lo contrario.

## 5. Seguimiento

### Al alta o despues de estabilizar

| Area | Que revisar |
|---|---|
| FEVI | Ecocardiografia; define IC, DAI futuro y farmacos. |
| Lipidos | Perfil lipidico 4-8 semanas tras iniciar/ajustar tratamiento. |
| Rehabilitacion | Cardiorehabilitacion presencial o domiciliaria si no puede asistir. |
| Antiagregacion | Duracion y sangrado; DAPT default 12 meses post-ACS si bajo riesgo. |
| Presion/DM/tabaco | Control intensivo de riesgo. |
| Sintomas | Angina residual, disnea, palpitaciones, sincope. |
| Adherencia | Estatina, antiagregantes, IECA/ARA-II, beta-bloqueador si indicado. |
| Seguridad | Sangrado, hipotension, bradicardia, funcion renal, potasio. |

### Prevencion secundaria basica

- No fumar.
- Ejercicio y rehabilitacion.
- Dieta cardioprotectora.
- Control de PA.
- Control de DM.
- Estatina de alta intensidad.
- Antiagregacion segun indicacion.
- Manejar depresion/ansiedad post-IAM si aparece.

Take-home: el seguimiento no es "control en consultorio"; es cerrar la fuga de
reinfarto: LDL, tabaco, PA, DM, FEVI, rehabilitacion y adherencia.

## 6. Pronostico

Mal pronostico si:

- STEMI anterior extenso.
- Shock cardiogenico.
- FEVI baja.
- Diabetes o ERC.
- Edad avanzada.
- Reperfusion tardia o fallida.
- Arritmias malignas.
- Complicacion mecanica.
- Multivaso o tronco coronario izquierdo.
- Mala adherencia a prevencion secundaria.

Perlas locales:

- FV primaria: causa principal de muerte extrahospitalaria.
- Shock cardiogenico: gran causa de muerte hospitalaria.
- PCR en adulto: causa frecuente cardiovascular/cardiopatia isquemica.
- Post-resucitacion con STEMI: estudiar causa coronaria y considerar
  coronariografia.

Take-home: lo que mas cambia pronostico en el examen es tiempo a reperfusion;
lo que mas cambia pronostico despues es prevencion secundaria real.

---

# Algorithm card

## Dolor toracico en una linea

```text
ECG en 10 min
  -> ST elevado = reperfusion
  -> sin ST elevado = troponina seriada + riesgo
  -> esfuerzo predecible = cronico/estable
```

## Tratamiento en una linea

| Fenotipo | Movimiento |
|---|---|
| Stable angina | Antianginoso + prevencion secundaria + prueba/riesgo. |
| Unstable angina | ACS sin necrosis: DAPT/anticoag + estratificar. |
| NSTEMI | ACS con necrosis: DAPT/anticoag + invasiva segun riesgo. |
| STEMI | Reperfusion urgente: PCI primaria o fibrinolisis si PCI no llega. |
| Prinzmetal | CCB/nitratos; no beta-bloqueador reflejo. |
| RV infarct | Fluidos; no nitratos/diureticos. |

## Exam traps

| If the stem says... | Do not answer... | Answer logic |
|---|---|---|
| ST elevation + classic pain | Troponin first | Reperfusion route. |
| Troponin high during sepsis/anemia | NSTEMI type 1 automatically | Type 2 MI/injury possible. |
| Exertional pain relieved by rest | Fibrinolysis | Stable angina. |
| Rest/nocturnal pain with transient ST elevation | Beta-blocker | Prinzmetal -> CCB. |
| Inferior MI + hypotension + clear lungs | Nitrate | RV infarct -> fluids. |
| New murmur + EAP post-IAM | Simple HF | Papillary rupture/VSD until proven. |

Modelo nuclear: `dolor toracico -> ECG -> STEMI/NSTE/chronic -> troponina -> riesgo -> reperfusion`. --- Cardiopatia isquemica ocurre cuando el miocardio recibe menos oxigeno del que necesita. La causa mas comun es aterosclerosis coronaria. Mecanismos principales: | Mecanismo | Resultado clinico | |---|---| | Estenosis fija coronaria | Angina estable con esfuer

units.title: Enfermedades exantematicas
units.body:
# Enfermedades exantematicas

## Take-home

En un nino con fiebre y rash, no empieces por el color. Empieza por el tiempo:
cuando aparecio el exantema respecto a la fiebre, que prodromo lo precedio, que
morfologia tiene, donde empezo, que respeta y cual es el signo ancla.

La linea de razonamiento es:

`fiebre + rash -> peligro -> timing -> prodromo -> morfologia -> distribucion ->
signo ancla -> accion`

## Guion

### 1. Por que da

Las enfermedades exantematicas mezclan cuatro mecanismos:

| Mecanismo | Ejemplos | Concepto preguntable |
|---|---|---|
| Viral respiratorio sistemico | Sarampion, rubeola, varicela, roseola, parvovirus B19, HFMD | El rash es parte de una infeccion sistemica; la clave es el patron completo, no solo la piel. |
| Toxina bacteriana | Escarlatina | GAS produce toxina eritrogenica: pharyngitis + sandpaper rash + Pastia/strawberry tongue. |
| Vasculitis/inflamacion | Kawasaki | No es "otro viral": es un imitador peligroso por riesgo coronario. |
| Salud publica/vacunas | Sarampion, rubeola, varicela | La accion correcta puede ser aislamiento, notificacion, confirmacion y proteccion de contactos. |

Take-home: el mecanismo explica la accion. Viral comun se observa; sarampion se
notifica; GAS se trata; Kawasaki se deriva/trata rapido.

### 2. A quien

| Perfil | Diagnostico que sube |
|---|---|
| No vacunado, brote, contacto respiratorio | Sarampion, rubeola, varicela. |
| Lactante con fiebre alta y buen estado general | Roseola. |
| Escolar con slapped cheek o rash reticular | Parvovirus B19. |
| Escolar con fiebre, odinofagia y rash rugoso | Escarlatina. |
| Nino <5 anos con fiebre >=5 dias y mucocutaneo | Kawasaki. |
| Inmunocomprometido, neonato, gestante expuesta | Varicela/sarampion/rubeola/parvovirus con mayor riesgo. |

Take-home: edad y vacuna no diagnostican solas, pero cambian el ranking de
diferenciales y la urgencia.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Enfermedad | Patron clinico de examen |
|---|---|
| Sarampion | Fiebre alta + tos + coriza + conjuntivitis con fotofobia; Koplik; rash maculopapular cefalocaudal y confluente. |
| Rubeola | Cuadro leve + adenopatias retroauriculares/suboccipitales; rash maculopapular fino que inicia en cara. |
| Varicela | Prurito + lesiones en distintos estadios: macula, papula, vesicula, pustula, costra. |
| Roseola | Fiebre alta 3-5 dias; cuando la fiebre cae aparece rash rosado troncal. |
| Parvovirus B19 | Mejillas abofeteadas; luego exantema reticular/lacy en tronco/extremidades. |
| Escarlatina | Faringitis + lengua aframbuesada + exantema rugoso tipo lija + lineas de Pastia + palidez perioral. |
| Kawasaki | Fiebre >=5 dias + conjuntivitis no purulenta + cambios orales + extremidades + rash + ganglio cervical. |
| HFMD | Fiebre/odinofagia + lesiones orales + vesiculas en palmas/plantas. |

Take-home: el diagnostico vive en la combinacion de prodromo, rash y signo
ancla.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

La mayoria de exantemas clasicos se reconocen clinicamente en examen. En
paciente real, el umbral para confirmar sube si hay brote, embarazo, enfermedad
grave, inmunosupresion o implicancia de salud publica.

| Sospecha | Como se diagnostica en la practica/examen |
|---|---|
| Sarampion | Clinica compatible + confirmacion de laboratorio segun protocolo; aislamiento y notificacion desde la sospecha. |
| Rubeola | Clinica compatible + confirmacion si sospecha, brote o embarazo/contacto gestante. |
| Varicela | Clinica por lesiones en diferentes estadios; PCR si caso atipico, grave o inmunocomprometido. |
| Roseola | Clinica: fiebre alta que cede y luego rash. |
| Parvovirus B19 | Clinica en nino tipico; serologia/PCR si embarazo, anemia hemolitica o inmunosupresion. |
| Escarlatina | Clinica + prueba rapida/cultivo para GAS cuando corresponde. |
| Kawasaki | Diagnostico clinico; eco/cardiologia por riesgo coronario. |
| HFMD | Clinica; vigilar hidratacion y dolor oral. |

Take-home: si el diagnostico implica salud publica o dano coronario/fetal, no
lo trates como "rash comun".

### 2. Clasificacion

Una forma util de clasificar para examen:

| Grupo | Enfermedades | Regla mental |
|---|---|---|
| Maculopapulares respiratorias | Sarampion, rubeola | Tres catarros/Koplik vs adenopatias retroauriculares. |
| Vesiculares | Varicela, HFMD | Cielo estrellado vs boca-manos-pies. |
| Rash posterior a fiebre | Roseola | Fiebre se va, rash aparece. |
| Reticular/facial | Parvovirus B19 | Slapped cheek + lacy rash. |
| Bacteriana toxigenica | Escarlatina | Faringitis + lija + Pastia. |
| Imitador peligroso | Kawasaki | Fiebre >=5 dias + mucocutaneo + coronarias. |

Take-home: la clasificacion no es taxonomia decorativa; sirve para no elegir el
tratamiento equivocado.

### 3. Manejo

| Diagnostico | Manejo base | Excepcion que no debes olvidar |
|---|---|---|
| Sarampion | Soporte, aislamiento, notificacion, confirmacion, proteccion de contactos. | Vitamin A and PEP depend on age/risk/local protocol; source-lock before public manual. |
| Rubeola | Soporte y vigilancia; confirmar si sospecha relevante. | Embarazo/contacto gestante cambia el manejo de salud publica. |
| Varicela | Soporte, higiene, antipruriginosos; avoid aspirin. | Acyclovir/urgent evaluation if >12 unvaccinated, severe, neonatal, pregnant, immunocompromised or complicated. |
| Roseola | Soporte, hidratacion, antitermico; educar por convulsion febril. | Revalorar si toxicidad, fiebre persistente o signos no tipicos. |
| Parvovirus B19 | Soporte en nino sano. | Gestante, anemia hemolitica o inmunosupresion requieren evaluacion especifica. |
| Escarlatina | Penicillin/amoxicillin for 10 days; alternatives if allergy. | Antibiotics prevent rheumatic fever when GAS pharyngitis. |
| Kawasaki | IVIG plus aspirin and cardiac follow-up. | No demorar por confundirlo con escarlatina viral/bacteriana comun. |
| HFMD | Soporte, analgesia, hidratacion. | Deshidratacion, compromiso neurologico or severe disease require escalation. |

Take-home: la mayoria es soporte; las excepciones de alto valor son sarampion,
escarlatina, varicela de riesgo y Kawasaki.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Enfermedad | Complicaciones preguntables |
|---|---|
| Sarampion | Otitis, neumonia, encefalitis, panencefalitis esclerosante subaguda, anergia cutanea. |
| Rubeola | Artritis, purpura trombocitopenica, encefalitis, sindrome de rubeola congenita. |
| Varicela | Sobreinfeccion bacteriana, neumonia, ataxia cerebelosa, encefalitis, Reye with aspirin. |
| Roseola | Convulsion febril. |
| Parvovirus B19 | Crisis aplasica, anemia fetal/hidrops/aborto, artritis. |
| Escarlatina | Fiebre reumatica, glomerulonefritis postestreptococica. |
| Kawasaki | Aneurismas coronarios, miocarditis, trombosis coronaria. |
| HFMD | Deshidratacion; raramente neurologic/cardiopulmonary severe disease depending on enterovirus. |

Take-home: "rash infantil" puede esconder complicaciones de salud publica,
coronarias, neurologicas, hematologicas o fetales.

### 5. Seguimiento

| Caso | Seguimiento |
|---|---|
| Exantema viral tipico, nino estable | Control si fiebre persiste, aparece toxicidad, deshidratacion or rash no encaja. |
| Sarampion/rubeola sospechados | Seguimiento por protocolo de vigilancia, confirmacion y contactos. |
| Varicela | Vigilar infeccion bacteriana, dificultad respiratoria, ataxia or inmunosupresion. |
| Escarlatina | Confirmar mejoria clinica; completar antibiotico; vigilar complicaciones. |
| Kawasaki | Ecocardiograma/cardiologia; seguimiento de coronarias. |
| Parvovirus en gestante/anemia hemolitica | Seguimiento obstetrico/hematologico segun protocolo. |

Take-home: el seguimiento depende de la complicacion que estas intentando
prevenir, no de "ver si se va el rash".

### 6. Pronostico

| Enfermedad | Pronostico general |
|---|---|
| Roseola, parvovirus B19 en nino sano, HFMD | Usualmente autolimitadas. |
| Varicela en nino sano | Usualmente autolimitada, pero no banal si high-risk. |
| Escarlatina | Excelente con antibiotico adecuado; riesgo si no se trata GAS pharyngitis. |
| Sarampion | Puede ser grave por neumonia, encefalitis and outbreak impact. |
| Rubeola | Leve en nino, grave como problema fetal/congenito. |
| Kawasaki | Bueno si tratado temprano; riesgo central es coronario. |

Take-home: el pronostico cambia radicalmente por vacuna, embarazo,
inmunosupresion, edad y oportunidad de tratamiento.

## Mini algoritmo de examen

```text
fiebre + rash
  -> vesiculas?
       -> different stages = varicela
       -> mouth + hands/feet = HFMD
  -> pharyngitis + sandpaper/Pastia/strawberry tongue?
       -> escarlatina
  -> high fever + cough/coryza/conjunctivitis + Koplik?
       -> sarampion
  -> mild illness + posterior auricular/suboccipital nodes?
       -> rubeola
  -> fever resolves then trunk rash?
       -> roseola
  -> slapped cheek then reticular rash?
       -> parvovirus B19
  -> fever >=5 days + mucosa/conjunctiva/extremities?
       -> Kawasaki
```

## Common errors

| Error | Correction |
|---|---|
| Confundir sarampion y rubeola por rash maculopapular. | Sarampion es mas toxico, con 3 catarros, fotofobia and Koplik. |
| Usar Forchheimer como signo unico de rubeola. | No es pathognomonic; nodes are stronger. |
| Llamar varicela a cualquier vesicula. | Varicela has lesions in different stages; HFMD has mouth/hands/feet. |
| Dar aspirin en varicela. | Avoid aspirin because of Reye risk. |
| Tratar Kawasaki como escarlatina. | Fever >=5 days and mucocutaneous/extremity findings require Kawasaki route. |
| Olvidar notificacion/aislamiento in suspected sarampion. | Public-health action starts at suspicion. |

## Output rule

For qbank and classes, every exanthem vignette should force at least three of
these features:

1. Timing between fever and rash.
2. Prodrome.
3. Lesion morphology.
4. Distribution/spared areas.
5. Anchor sign.
6. One management or public-health action.
units.example: En un nino con fiebre y rash, no empieces por el color. Empieza por el tiempo: cuando aparecio el exantema respecto a la fiebre, que prodromo lo precedio, que morfologia tiene, donde empezo, que respeta y cual es el signo ancla. La linea de razonamiento es: `fiebre + rash -> peligro -> timing -> prodromo -> morfologia -> distribucion -> signo ancla -> accion` Las enfermedades exantematicas mezclan cuatro mecanismos: | Mecanismo | Ejemplos | Concepto preguntable | |---|---|---| | Viral respiratorio sistemico | Sarampion, rubeola, varicela, roseola, parvovirus B19, HFMD | El rash es parte de una

units.title: Pancreatitis
units.body:
# Pancreatitis

## Take-home

Pancreatitis se aprende como una ruta:

`dolor epigastrico en barra -> 2/3 diagnosticos -> gravedad -> etiologia ->
primeras 48-72 h -> CPRE/colecistectomia si biliar -> complicacion por tiempo`

El error caro es memorizar amilasa, TC y antibioticos como reflejos. El examen
quiere que sepas cuando diagnosticar, cuando estratificar, cuando buscar causa
biliar y cuando NO hacer una intervencion innecesaria.

## Guion

### 1. Por que da

La pancreatitis aguda aparece cuando enzimas pancreaticas se activan dentro del
pancreas y producen autodigestion, inflamacion local y respuesta sistemica.

| Causa | Mecanismo de examen | Clave |
|---|---|---|
| Litiasis biliar | Obstruccion transitoria de la ampolla por calculo/lodo. | Causa mas frecuente de PA. |
| Alcohol | Lesion acinar/ductal, inflamacion repetida. | Segunda causa de PA; central en pancreatitis cronica. |
| Hipertrigliceridemia | Toxicidad por acidos grasos y microcirculacion alterada. | TG >1000 mg/dL hace sospecharla. |
| Hipercalcemia | Activacion enzimatica favorecida por calcio. | Pensar si Ca alto. |
| Farmacos/iatrogenia | Azatioprina, algunos IECA/estatinas/mesalazina, didanosina, CPRE. | Siempre revisar exposiciones. |
| Autoinmune | IgG4, pseudomasas, estenosis biliares. | Responde a corticoides en casos seleccionados. |
| Hereditaria/genetica | PRSS1, CFTR, SPINK1. | Pensar en joven/recurrente/etiologia no clara. |

Take-home: la causa no es decorativa; decide ecografia, CPRE, colecistectomia,
consejeria o estudio adicional.

### 2. A quien

| Fenotipo | Perfil tipico |
|---|---|
| PA biliar | Mujer 40-60, obesidad, litiasis, dolor despues de comida grasa. |
| PA alcoholica | Varon 30-50, consumo cronico de alcohol. |
| PA metabolica | TG muy alto, hipercalcemia, diabetes/dislipidemia. |
| PA idiopatica | Sin litiasis/alcohol claro; puede ser microlitiasis oculta. |
| PA grave | Edad avanzada, comorbilidad, obesidad, SIRS, BUN/HCT altos o en ascenso. |
| Pancreatitis cronica | Alcohol + tabaco, recurrente, hereditaria, autoinmune u obstructiva. |
| Paciente >40 sin causa clara | Considerar neoplasia pancreatica como etiologia subyacente. |

Take-home: en examen, biliar y alcohol son primero; en paciente real, "sin
causa" no significa "sin trabajo".

### 3. Como se presenta

| Manifestacion | Lectura |
|---|---|
| Dolor epigastrico intenso irradiado en cinturon/dorso | Cuadro canonico de PA. |
| Nauseas, vomitos, ileo, distension | Soporta PA y severidad funcional. |
| Cullen/Grey-Turner | Hemorragia/PA grave en memoria clasica. |
| Shock, insuficiencia renal, insuficiencia respiratoria | Falla organica: gravedad. |
| Dolor persistente + masa + llenura precoz semanas despues | Pseudocyst or other late collection. |
| Dolor recurrente/cronico + esteatorrea + perdida de peso + diabetes | Pancreatitis cronica avanzada. |
| Calcificaciones pancreaticas | Muy sugestivas de pancreatitis cronica en contexto compatible. |

Take-home: el mismo dolor puede estar en fase aguda, complicacion tardia o
enfermedad cronica. El tiempo manda.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

Pancreatitis aguda se diagnostica con 2 de 3:

1. Dolor abdominal tipico.
2. Lipasa y/o amilasa >3 veces el limite superior normal.
3. Imagen compatible.

| Punto | Regla |
|---|---|
| Lipasa | Mejor que amilasa: mas sensible/especifica y permanece elevada mas dias. |
| Amilasa | Puede normalizarse o estar normal; su altura no mide gravedad. |
| Ecografia | Busca causa biliar; no estadifica bien el parenquima pancreatico. |
| TC | Usar si diagnostico incierto, no mejora o hay sospecha de complicacion; examen local recuerda 72-96 h para necrosis/colecciones. |
| TG/calcio | Pedir si no hay gallstones/alcohol claro o si el contexto lo sugiere. |

Take-home: no toda hiperamilasemia es pancreatitis, y no toda pancreatitis
necesita TC inmediata.

### 2. Clasificacion

#### Atlanta revisada

| Gravedad | Criterio |
|---|---|
| Leve | Sin falla organica y sin complicaciones locales/sistemicas. |
| Moderadamente grave | Falla organica transitoria <48 h y/o complicacion local/sistemica. |
| Grave | Falla organica persistente >48 h. |

Falla organica clave: respiratoria, renal o shock.

#### Ranson

Ranson es una escala clasica de memoria local. En ENAM/CTO, `>=3` sugiere PA
grave. Usala como recall, no como reemplazo de Atlanta ni de la evolucion
clinica.

#### Pancreatitis cronica

| Eje | Dato |
|---|---|
| Clinica | Dolor cronico/recurrente, esteatorrea, perdida de peso, diabetes. |
| Imagen | Calcificaciones, cambios ductales/parenchimales, atrofia. |
| Laboratorio | Amilasa/lipasa suelen ser normales en enfermedad establecida. |
| Prueba inicial moderna | CT o MRI; EUS/s-MRCP si persiste duda. |

Take-home: aguda se clasifica por falla organica y tiempo; cronica por dano
estructural y perdida funcional.

### 3. Manejo

#### Primeras 48-72 horas en PA

```text
confirmar PA
  -> evaluar gravedad y volumen
  -> fluidos guiados por metas, Ringer lactato preferido
  -> analgesia + antiemeticos
  -> monitorizar BUN/HCT/vitales/diuresis
  -> alimentacion oral temprana si PA leve y tolera
  -> enteral si no puede comer, evitar parenteral si es posible
  -> no antibiotico profilactico
  -> buscar etiologia biliar con ecografia
```

| Decision | Regla |
|---|---|
| Antibioticos | No profilacticos en necrosis esteril; usar si colangitis, colecistitis, necrosis infectada u otra infeccion. |
| CPRE/ERCP | Indicar si colangitis o obstruccion biliar persistente; no en toda PA biliar. |
| Colecistectomia | En PA biliar leve, preferir mismo ingreso tras estabilizacion/resolucion. |
| Necrosis infectada | Antibioticos que penetren necrosis + drenaje/necrosectomia si sepsis/persistencia; preferir abordaje step-up cuando posible. |
| PA cronica | Cese alcohol/tabaco, analgesia escalonada, PERT si insuficiencia exocrina, insulina si diabetes, intervencion si obstruccion/dolor refractario. |

Take-home: soporte primero; procedimientos solo cuando la indicacion existe.

### 4. Complicaciones

| Complicacion | Clave |
|---|---|
| Necrosis pancreatica | Mejor definida por TC contrastada cuando corresponde; infectada si gas o sepsis/infeccion probable. |
| Pseudocyst | Coleccion fluida encapsulada >4 semanas; puede dar dolor, plenitud, obstruccion o masa. |
| Walled-off necrosis | Coleccion necrotica encapsulada >4 semanas; no es lo mismo que pseudocyst. |
| Falla respiratoria/SDRA | Complicacion sistemica grave. |
| Shock/IRA | Falla organica grave. |
| Hipocalcemia | Saponificacion grasa; se asocia a severidad. |
| Diabetes/insuficiencia exocrina | Complicaciones de pancreatitis cronica. |

Take-home: la complicacion local se nombra por dos ejes: tiempo y presencia de
necrosis.

### 5. Seguimiento

| Situacion | Seguimiento |
|---|---|
| PA leve biliar | Colecistectomia antes del alta si factible; educar recurrencia. |
| PA idiopatica/recurrente | Repetir ecografia, MRI/MRCP o EUS segun disponibilidad; revisar TG, calcio, farmacos. |
| PA grave/necrotizante | Reevaluar organos, nutricion, infeccion, necesidad de drenaje diferido. |
| Pseudocyst asintomatico | Observacion si estable. |
| Pseudocyst sintomatico/complicado | Drenaje endoscopico/percutaneo/quirurgico segun anatomia y expertise. |
| Pancreatitis cronica | Peso, nutricion, vitaminas liposolubles, osteoporosis, diabetes, dolor, alcohol/tabaco. |

Take-home: el seguimiento no es "control de lipasa"; es prevenir recurrencia,
detectar complicaciones y recuperar nutricion/funcion.

### 6. Pronostico

| Fenotipo | Pronostico |
|---|---|
| PA leve | Usualmente resuelve en dias si no hay complicaciones. |
| PA biliar sin colecistectomia | Riesgo de recurrencia. |
| PA grave persistente | Mayor mortalidad por falla organica, necrosis infectada y sepsis. |
| Pseudocyst pequeno/asintomatico | Puede observarse; muchos resuelven. |
| Pancreatitis cronica | Curso progresivo con dolor, insuficiencia exocrina/endocrina y dano nutricional. |

Take-home: el pronostico depende menos del numero de lipasa y mas de falla
organica, causa corregible, infeccion, nutricion y recurrencia.

## Mini algoritmo de examen

```text
epigastric belt pain + nausea/vomiting
  -> lipase
  -> 2 of 3?
       -> yes: pancreatitis acute
  -> ultrasound for gallstones
  -> organ failure?
       -> persistent >48h = severe
  -> biliary + cholangitis/obstruction?
       -> ERCP/CPRE
  -> mild biliary AP improved?
       -> cholecystectomy same admission if feasible
  -> symptoms/mass after >4 weeks?
       -> pseudocyst if fluid-only
  -> chronic pain + steatorrhea/DM/calcifications?
       -> chronic pancreatitis
```

## Common errors

| Error | Correction |
|---|---|
| Pedir TC inmediata en todo paciente con clinica y lipasa clara. | CT is reserved for uncertainty, lack of improvement, or complications; exam recall often says 72-96 h. |
| Medir gravedad por valor de amilasa/lipasa. | Severity is organ failure/course/complications. |
| Dar antibiotico profilactico por necrosis esteril. | Antibiotics require infection concern or infection source. |
| Hacer CPRE en toda PA biliar. | ERCP/CPRE is for cholangitis or persistent obstruction. |
| Llamar pseudocyst a coleccion temprana. | Pseudocyst needs mature wall and usually >4 weeks. |
| Esperar enzimas altas en pancreatitis cronica establecida. | Chronic disease often has normal enzymes. |

## Output rule

For qbank and classes, every pancreatitis vignette should force at least three
features:

1. Diagnostic gate: pain, enzyme, image.
2. Etiology: biliar, alcohol, TG/Ca/drug/autoimmune.
3. Severity: organ failure, shock/renal/respiratory, BUN/HCT/SIRS.
4. Time: <4 weeks or >4 weeks.
5. Procedure decision: CT, ERCP/CPRE, cholecystectomy, drainage.
6. Chronic function: steatorrhea, weight loss, diabetes, calcifications.
units.example: Pancreatitis se aprende como una ruta: `dolor epigastrico en barra -> 2/3 diagnosticos -> gravedad -> etiologia -> primeras 48-72 h -> CPRE/colecistectomia si biliar -> complicacion por tiempo` El error caro es memorizar amilasa, TC y antibioticos como reflejos. El examen quiere que sepas cuando diagnosticar, cuando estratificar, cuando buscar causa biliar y cuando NO hacer una intervencion innecesaria. La pancreatitis aguda aparece cuando enzimas pancreaticas se activan dentro del pancreas y producen autodigestion, inflamacion local y respuesta sistemica. | Causa | Mecanismo de examen | Clave

units.title: Cirrosis hepatica
units.body:
# Cirrosis hepatica

## Take-home

Cirrosis hepatica es fibrosis difusa + nodulos de regeneracion que distorsionan
la arquitectura del higado. Sus dos consecuencias centrales son:

1. Menos higado funcional: ictericia, hipoalbuminemia, coagulopatia,
   encefalopatia.
2. Hipertension portal: ascitis, varices, esplenomegalia, PBE y sindrome
   hepatorrenal.

La linea de razonamiento es:

`cirrosis -> compensada/descompensada -> complicacion -> primer paso ->
profilaxis -> trasplante`

## Guion

### 1. Por que da

| Mecanismo | Consecuencia | Pregunta de examen |
|---|---|---|
| Fibrosis + nodulos | Perdida de arquitectura hepatica. | Definicion de cirrosis. |
| Menos funcion sintetica | Albumina baja, TP/INR alterado. | Child-Pugh, MELD, edema/ascitis. |
| Hipertension portal | Varices, ascitis, esplenomegalia. | HDA variceal, SAAG/GASLA, beta bloqueadores. |
| Vasodilatacion esplancnica + RAAS | Retencion renal de sodio/agua. | Ascitis y HRS. |
| Translocacion bacteriana | PBE sin foco perforado. | PMN >250 and ceftriaxone. |
| Bypass portosistemico + nitrogenados | Encefalopatia hepatica. | Lactulosa, rifaximina, precipitant search. |

Take-home: cada complicacion nace de uno de dos ejes: funcion hepatica perdida
o hipertension portal.

### 2. A quien

| Perfil | Etiologia probable |
|---|---|
| Alcohol cronico, GOT > GPT | Alcohol-associated liver disease. |
| VHC/VHB cronicos | Viral chronic liver disease, HCC risk. |
| Obesidad, DM, dislipidemia | MASLD/MASH. |
| Mujer con colestasis/autoinmunidad | Biliar primaria/autoinmune. |
| Joven, neurologic/hemolysis/family history | Wilson, hereditary/metabolic. |
| Iron overload pattern | Hemochromatosis. |

Take-home: la etiologia importa porque algunas causas se tratan aun en cirrosis
y porque cambian vigilancia, familiares y riesgo de HCC.

### 3. Como se presenta

| Estado | Claves |
|---|---|
| Compensada | Asintomatica or sintomas vagos; trombopenia, esplenomegalia, imagen compatible. |
| Descompensada | Ascitis, HDA variceal, encefalopatia, PBE, HRS, ictericia, HCC. |
| Exploracion | Aranas vasculares, eritema palmar, ictericia, caput medusae, ginecomastia, ascitis, esplenomegalia. |
| Laboratorio | Albumina baja, bilirrubina alta, TP/INR alterado, plaquetas bajas, gamma globulinas altas. |
| Alcoholica | GOT > GPT, macrocytosis can coexist. |

Take-home: el salto de compensada a descompensada cambia pronostico y activa
trasplante/evaluacion avanzada.

## Manejo

### 1. Diagnostico

| Pregunta | Respuesta util |
|---|---|
| Tiene cirrosis? | Historia + labs + imagen/elastografia; biopsia solo si duda cambia manejo. |
| Esta descompensada? | Ascitis, HDA, EH, PBE, HRS, ictericia or HCC. |
| Que tan grave? | Child-Pugh and MELD. |
| Cual es la complicacion ahora? | Ascites/PBE/HDA/EH/HRS router. |
| Cual es la etiologia? | Alcohol, VHB/VHC, MASLD/MASH, autoimmune/cholestatic/metabolic. |

Take-home: no basta diagnosticar cirrosis; hay que ubicar fase, causa,
complicacion y pronostico.

### 2. Clasificacion

#### Child-Pugh

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Bilirubin | Excretion/cholestasis. |
| Albumin | Synthetic function and oncotic state. |
| Prothrombin/INR | Synthetic coagulation function. |
| Ascites | Portal HTN/decompensation. |
| Encephalopathy | Liver failure/portosystemic shunting. |

Local exam framing:

- Child A: 5-6.
- Child B: 7-9.
- Child C: >=10.
- Local transplant trigger often: Child-Pugh >7 or MELD >=15.

#### MELD

MELD uses bilirubin, creatinine and INR. It is analytic and transplant-oriented;
it does not include ascites or encephalopathy directly.

Take-home: Child mixes clinic + labs; MELD is labs and renal function.

### 3. Manejo

#### General cirrhosis management

| Goal | Actions |
|---|---|
| Stop injury | Alcohol cessation, treat VHB/VHC, manage MASLD/MASH, stop hepatotoxins. |
| Prevent portal HTN events | NSBB/carvedilol or endoscopic strategy depending on varices/CSPH and contraindications. |
| Prevent HCC | Ultrasound-based surveillance with AFP depending on local protocol. |
| Prevent infections | Vaccines, PBE prophylaxis only in defined high-risk/secondary settings. |
| Preserve nutrition | Avoid chronic total protein restriction; treat sarcopenia/malnutrition. |
| Decide transplant | Decompensation, Child/MELD threshold, HRS, refractory ascites, recurrent EH. |

#### Complication-specific chain

| Complication | First move | Treatment anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Ascites new/inpatient | Diagnostic paracentesis. | Sodium restriction + spironolactone/furosemide; albumin after large-volume paracentesis. |
| PBE | Do not wait for culture if PMN >250. | Ceftriaxone/cefotaxime; albumin in selected high-risk/renal dysfunction. |
| HDA variceal | Resuscitate + vasoactive + antibiotics + urgent endoscopy. | Octreotide/somatostatin/terlipressin + EVL; TIPS if high risk/failure. |
| EH | Search precipitant and dangerous mimics. | Lactulose first; rifaximin add-on for recurrent/nonresponse. |
| HRS | Exclude other renal causes and volume-responsive prerenal state. | Albumin + terlipressin/norepinephrine; transplant definitive. |

Take-home: the first step is not always the "definitive" step. In cirrhosis,
order matters.

### 4. Complications

| Complication | Diagnostic clue | Must-not-miss |
|---|---|---|
| Ascites | Fluid in abdomen, SAAG/GASLA >=1.1 if portal HTN. | Paracentesis in new/inpatient/deterioration. |
| PBE | Ascitic PMN >250/mm3. | Start antibiotics even if culture pending/negative. |
| Variceal bleeding | Hematemesis/melena in cirrhosis/varices. | Vasoactive + antibiotic early; EVL at endoscopy. |
| EH | Confusion, sleep reversal, asterixis, coma. | Precipitant search; lactulose/rifaximin logic. |
| HRS | AKI in cirrhosis + ascites without intrinsic renal disease. | Albumin + vasoconstrictor; transplant evaluation. |
| HCC | Cirrhosis is risk state. | Surveillance, especially viral/alcohol/MASLD risk contexts. |

Take-home: a cirrhotic with a new symptom has a complication until proven
otherwise.

### 5. Seguimiento

| Scenario | Follow-up |
|---|---|
| Compensated cirrhosis | Etiology treatment, HCC surveillance, portal HTN risk assessment, vaccines, nutrition. |
| Ascites | Weight, Na/K/creatinine, diuretic tolerance, sodium intake, transplant referral if clinically significant. |
| PBE | Secondary prophylaxis, recurrence prevention, reassess renal function. |
| HDA variceal survivor | Secondary prophylaxis: NSBB + EVL; consider TIPS if recurrent/high-risk. |
| EH survivor | Precipitant prevention, lactulose adherence/titration, rifaximin if recurrent, driving/safety counseling. |
| HRS/refractory ascites/recurrent decompensation | Transplant center evaluation; palliative goals when not candidate. |

Take-home: follow-up is not passive control; it is prevention of the next
decompensation.

### 6. Pronostico

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Ascites | Often first decompensation; large survival drop. |
| HDA variceal | High early mortality; secondary prophylaxis mandatory. |
| EH | Higher mortality and impaired safety/quality of life. |
| HRS | Very poor prognosis without reversal/transplant. |
| Child C or high MELD | Advanced disease; transplant logic. |

Take-home: cirrhosis prognosis is event-driven. The first decompensation changes
the whole map.

## Mini algoritmo de examen

```text
cirrhosis patient
  -> ascites?
       -> paracentesis
       -> PMN >250 = PBE -> ceftriaxone
       -> large-volume tap -> albumin
       -> chronic ascites -> spironolactone + furosemide
  -> hematemesis/melena?
       -> octreotide/somatostatin/terlipressin + antibiotic + endoscopy/EVL
  -> confusion/asterixis?
       -> precipitant search + lactulose
       -> recurrent/nonresponse -> rifaximin
  -> AKI + ascites, no response to volume?
       -> HRS -> albumin + vasoconstrictor + transplant evaluation
  -> severity question?
       -> Child-Pugh vs MELD
```

## Common errors

| Error | Correction |
|---|---|
| Treating new ascites with diuretics before diagnostic paracentesis. | New/inpatient/deteriorating ascites needs paracentesis. |
| Excluding PBE because there is no fever. | PBE can be subtle; PMN >250 is the key. |
| Starting beta blocker during acute variceal bleed. | Acute bleed needs vasoactive drug, antibiotics and endoscopy; NSBB later. |
| Ordering ammonia as mandatory confirmation for EH. | HE is clinical; search precipitants and mimics. |
| Restricting protein chronically in HE. | Avoid chronic total protein restriction; malnutrition worsens outcomes. |
| Calling every renal failure prerenal. | HRS does not respond appropriately to volume and has bland urine. |

## Output rule

Every cirrhosis vignette should force at least three features:

1. Phase: compensated or decompensated.
2. Complication: ascites/PBE/HDA/EH/HRS.
3. First action.
4. Prevention after survival/stabilization.
5. Severity/prognosis: Child-Pugh, MELD, transplant.
6. Product modifier: exam key vs modern guideline nuance.

units.title: Hepatitis viral
units.body:
# Hepatitis viral

## 0. One-line exam model

Hepatitis viral is an icteric/hepatocellular syndrome where the exam asks you to
identify the virus, interpret markers and choose prevention or treatment:

`A/E fecal-oral and acute; B/C/D blood-sex-perinatal and chronic risk; D needs B`.

Take-home point: the question is rarely "hepatitis" in general. It is usually
"which marker proves which state?"

## 1. Why it happens

### Mechanism

Viral hepatitis injures hepatocytes directly and through immune response. The
clinical result is hepatocellular injury: ALT and AST rise, bilirubin handling
fails, bile pigments reach urine, and the patient may develop jaundice, coluria,
acolia and pruritus.

Residentado exact anchor: alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is the sensitive marker
of hepatocellular injury in acute disease.

### Conceptual split

| Group | Virus | Mechanism that matters |
|---|---|---|
| Fecal-oral acute | HAV, HEV | Exposure is water/food/sanitation; usually no chronic infection. |
| Blood/sex/perinatal chronic risk | HBV, HCV | Current infection must be proven with serology/RNA and followed for chronic disease. |
| Satellite virus | HDV | Needs HBV/HBsAg to complete infection; prevention is HBV vaccine. |

Take-home point: transmission route predicts chronicity and prevention.

## 2. Who gets it

### HAV

HAV appears in outbreaks, contaminated food/water, poor sanitation, household
contact, travel to high-endemicity areas and pediatric/community settings. It is
usually acute and self-limited.

### HBV

HBV is transmitted through blood, sexual exposure and perinatal transmission.
Risk groups include infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers, sexual contacts,
people exposed to needles or blood, hemodialysis, healthcare exposure and people
living with HIV. Perinatal infection has the highest chronicity risk.

### HCV

HCV is bloodborne. Exam clues include transfusion history, injection drug use,
hemodialysis, HIV coinfection, blood exposure or chronic liver disease found
after screening. There is no effective vaccine.

### HDV

HDV occurs only in a person with HBV infection. Coinfection means HBV and HDV
arrive together; superinfection means HDV arrives over chronic HBV and usually
has worse prognosis.

### HEV

HEV is fecal-oral and linked to unsafe water/sanitation. The exam danger group
is pregnancy, especially late pregnancy, because severe hepatitis and acute
liver failure are more likely.

Take-home point: if the stem gives pregnancy plus hepatitis E, do not treat it
as a harmless gastroenteritis-like virus.

## 3. How it presents

### Acute hepatitis syndrome

Common pattern:

- Prodrome: fever, malaise, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, arthralgias or right
  upper quadrant pain.
- Icteric phase: jaundice, coluria, acolia, pruritus and tender hepatomegaly.
- Lab pattern: ALT/AST high, often with ALT prominence; bilirubin may rise.

### Severe disease clues

Red flags:

- Encephalopathy.
- INR/prothrombin alteration or bleeding.
- Hypoglycemia.
- Persistent vomiting/dehydration.
- Pregnancy, especially if HEV is possible.
- Known chronic liver disease or immunosuppression.

Take-home point: acute viral hepatitis is usually supportive care, until the
patient has liver failure physiology.

## 4. Diagnosis

### First step

Recognize the syndrome, then order targeted markers. You cannot distinguish
HAV, HBV, HCV, HDV and HEV reliably by symptoms alone.

### Differential marker table

| Virus | Best exam marker for acute/current infection | What not to confuse |
|---|---|---|
| HAV | IgM anti-HAV. | IgG anti-HAV means past infection/vaccine immunity, not acute illness. |
| HBV acute | HBsAg positive + anti-HBc IgM positive. | HBsAg alone does not tell acute vs chronic. |
| HBV vaccine immunity | Isolated anti-HBs positive. | Anti-HBc is absent after vaccine-only immunity. |
| HBV past natural infection | Anti-HBs positive + anti-HBc total positive. | This is not active infection if HBsAg is negative. |
| HBV chronic | HBsAg persistent or HBsAg positive with anti-HBc total and no IgM pattern. | Chronicity needs duration/context. |
| HCV current infection | HCV RNA/NAT detected. | Anti-HCV positive alone can be past or current infection. |
| HDV | Anti-HDV/HDV RNA in HBsAg-positive patient. | HDV cannot be productive without HBV/HBsAg. |
| HEV | IgM anti-HEV or HEV RNA. | Symptoms overlap with HAV and other icteric infections. |

### HBV serology quick matrix

| HBsAg | Anti-HBs | Anti-HBc IgM | Anti-HBc total | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| - | - | - | - | Susceptible; vaccinate. |
| - | + | - | - | Vaccinated/protected. |
| - | + | - | + | Past natural infection; immune. |
| + | - | + | + | Acute HBV pattern or acute flare. |
| + | - | - | + | Chronic HBV pattern if persistent/context fits. |

### HCV testing rule

If anti-HCV is reactive, order HCV RNA/NAT. If recent exposure is suspected,
HCV RNA may be needed even when antibody is negative because antibody can lag.

Take-home point: for HCV, antibody answers "ever exposed"; RNA answers
"currently infected".

## 5. Classification

### By time/course

| Category | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Acute hepatitis | Recent symptomatic/asymptomatic infection with acute hepatocellular injury. |
| Chronic hepatitis | Persistent viral infection with ongoing risk of fibrosis, cirrhosis and HCC. |
| Acute liver failure | Acute liver injury plus encephalopathy/coagulopathy in a patient without known chronic liver disease. |

### By virus

| Virus | Usual course | Highest-yield exam label |
|---|---|---|
| HAV | Acute/self-limited. | IgM anti-HAV confirms acute HAV. |
| HBV | Acute or chronic. | HBsAg + anti-HBc IgM = acute; isolated anti-HBs = vaccine immunity. |
| HCV | Frequently chronic if untreated. | Confirm current infection with HCV RNA; treat with DAA. |
| HDV | Coinfection/superinfection with HBV. | Needs HBV/HBsAg. |
| HEV | Acute; severe in pregnancy. | Pregnancy is the risk modifier. |

Take-home point: chronicity is the axis that separates A/E from B/C/D.

## 6. Management

### Acute hepatitis approach

1. Assess severity: mental status, INR/prothrombin, glucose, bilirubin, hydration
   and comorbid liver disease.
2. Stop alcohol and avoid hepatotoxic medications.
3. Support hydration, nutrition and symptom control.
4. Refer/admit if red flags, pregnancy, severe labs, acute liver failure concern
   or uncertain diagnosis.
5. Notify/follow public health rules when the virus and local regulation require.

### HAV

Treatment is supportive. The exam confirms with IgM anti-HAV. Residentado has a
local control anchor of 7 days after symptom onset in an HAV-like pediatric case;
keep that as exam memory until source-locked for public infection-control use.

### HBV acute

Most acute HBV is supportive. Severe/fulminant disease or decompensation needs
urgent specialist/hospital management. Do not label a case as chronic unless
duration or chronic serology/context supports it.

### HBV chronic

Chronic HBV requires staging: ALT, HBV DNA, HBeAg/anti-HBe, fibrosis assessment
and HCC risk. Exam/local frames use tenofovir or entecavir-type therapy for
eligible chronic HBV, especially cirrhosis. Current WHO/AASLD updates broaden
and simplify treatment criteria, so public manual rules must be source-locked.

### HCV

Confirm active infection with HCV RNA/NAT. Direct-acting antivirals cure most
patients and modern guidance supports simplified pangenotypic treatment in
eligible patients. Before treatment, assess cirrhosis, medications/interactions,
HBV/HIV coinfection and pregnancy.

### HDV

Suspect in HBsAg-positive patients with severe disease, high-risk exposure or
unexpected ALT activity. Prevention is HBV vaccination; treatment is specialist.

### HEV

Supportive care for most cases, but pregnancy, fulminant hepatitis and
immunosuppression change risk. Pregnant symptomatic patients should not be
managed as low-risk routine cases.

Take-home point: management is not "give antiviral to everyone"; it is
`support acute A/E, stage chronic B/C, treat active HCV, prevent HBV/PTMI`.

## 7. Prevention and PTMI

### Vaccines

| Virus | Vaccine logic |
|---|---|
| HAV | Vaccine exists; use depends on local schedule/risk. |
| HBV | Vaccine exists; standard exam memory is 0-1-6 month series in older children/adults and birth-dose logic in newborns. |
| HCV | No effective vaccine. |
| HDV | No direct routine vaccine; HBV vaccine prevents HDV indirectly. |
| HEV | Not routine in Peru exam frame. |

### HBV post-exposure and contacts

For susceptible exposed persons, local NTS/ENCAPS frames use HBV vaccine and
IgHB depending on vaccination status, exposure type and timing. Exact dosing and
timing should not be turned into public answer keys without source-lock.

### PTMI hepatitis B

If the gestante is HBsAg positive:

1. Request maternal HBV evaluation: HBeAg, anti-HBc markers, HBV viral load and
   liver assessment according to local protocol.
2. Refer or coordinate with a level II/III or specialist route.
3. Start tenofovir prophylaxis/treatment if local criteria are met.
4. Delivery route is usually obstetric, not automatically cesarean for HBV.
5. Newborn receives HBV vaccine + IgHB in the first 12 hours in local NTS frame.
6. Breastfeeding is not suspended for HBV when neonatal prophylaxis is done.

Take-home point: PTMI is a timeline: mother now, newborn in first hours,
follow-up later.

## 8. Complications

| Complication | Viruses most relevant | Exam clue |
|---|---|---|
| Acute liver failure | HBV, HEV, severe HAV rarely; others possible. | Encephalopathy + coagulopathy. |
| Chronic hepatitis | HBV, HCV, HDV. | Persistent infection markers. |
| Cirrhosis | HBV, HCV, HDV. | Thrombocytopenia, fibrosis, portal hypertension. |
| Hepatocellular carcinoma | HBV, HCV, cirrhosis. | Chronic infection plus surveillance/risk. |
| Vertical transmission | HBV highest exam relevance; HCV also possible. | Gestante and newborn route. |

## 9. Follow-up

### HBV

Follow ALT, HBV DNA, HBeAg/anti-HBe when relevant, fibrosis/cirrhosis status and
HCC surveillance when indicated. Vaccinate susceptible contacts.

### HCV

After treatment, check HCV RNA 12 weeks or later after completion to document
SVR/virologic cure. Continue surveillance if cirrhosis or ongoing risk.

### HAV/HEV

Usually no chronic follow-up if recovery is complete, but persistent symptoms,
severe disease, pregnancy or immunosuppression require closer monitoring.

Take-home point: HBV and HCV need chronic-care loops; HAV and HEV usually need
recovery plus public-health/source-control logic.

## 10. Prognosis

| Virus | Prognosis anchor |
|---|---|
| HAV | Usually recovery; severe disease uncommon. |
| HBV | Adult acute infection often clears; perinatal infection frequently becomes chronic; chronic HBV can progress to cirrhosis/HCC. |
| HCV | Often chronic if untreated; DAAs cure most infections and reduce long-term risk. |
| HDV | Superinfection over chronic HBV is high-risk for rapid fibrosis and severe disease. |
| HEV | Usually self-limited; pregnancy is the classic high-mortality modifier. |

## 11. Exam blueprints

### Blueprint 1: Acute HBV

Stem: adult with acute icterus, ALT/AST >2000, HBsAg positive and anti-HBc IgM
positive.

Answer: acute hepatitis B.

Trap: choosing chronic HBV because HBsAg is positive.

### Blueprint 2: Vaccinated against HBV

Stem: child with unknown vaccine status; asks what result confirms protection.

Answer: anti-HBs positive / IgG anti-HBs.

Trap: anti-HBc means natural exposure, not vaccine-only immunity.

### Blueprint 3: Acute HAV

Stem: child with fever, abdominal pain, icterus and coluria.

Answer: IgM anti-HAV confirms.

Trap: ordering nonspecific liver tests as confirmatory.

### Blueprint 4: HCV

Stem: anti-HCV positive.

Answer: HCV RNA/NAT to confirm current infection.

Trap: treating anti-HCV alone as active infection.

### Blueprint 5: PTMI HBV

Stem: gestante HBsAg positive.

Answer: maternal evaluation plus prevention route; newborn vaccine + IgHB in
first hours according to local NTS.

Trap: solving only as adult hepatitis and forgetting the newborn timeline.

units.title: Medidas en epidemiologia
units.body:
# Medidas en epidemiologia

## 0. One-line exam model

Medidas en epidemiologia is a denominator exam.

`indicator = numerator / denominator * multiplier`

Take-home point: before memorizing formulas, ask who could have become part of
the numerator.

## 1. Concepto preguntable

Epidemiologic measures translate population events into comparable numbers.
They answer three different questions:

| Question | Family | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| How much disease exists or appears? | Frequency | Prevalence, incidence, incidence density, mortality. |
| How different are two groups? | Association | RR, OR, RP, rate ratio. |
| How much disease is explained, avoided or produced? | Impact/effect | Attributable risk, FAE, FAP, ARR/RAR, RRR, NNT, NNH. |

The shared structure is always:

`numerator / denominator * multiplier`

The multiplier makes the number readable: per 100, per 1000, per 10000 or per
100000. It does not fix a wrong numerator or denominator.

Take-home point: measures are not formulas first; they are answers to population
questions.

## 2. Basic language: ratio, proportion and rate

### Ratio

A ratio compares two quantities. The numerator does not need to be contained in
the denominator. Example: doctors per population, male/female ratio, or a
standardized comparison.

### Proportion

A proportion has a numerator contained inside the denominator. Example:
prevalence, cumulative incidence, lethality and attack rate.

### Rate

In strict epidemiology, a rate adds time to the denominator or describes events
over a defined time interval. In exam language, "tasa" is sometimes used more
loosely for proportions multiplied by 100, 1000 or 100000. Teach both: strict
meaning for reasoning, local wording for answer recognition.

Take-home point: proportion is "part of whole"; rate adds time or a population
period; exam Spanish sometimes uses "tasa" loosely.

## 3. Frequency measures

### Prevalence

Prevalence measures existing disease burden.

`prevalence = all current cases / population at the same point or period`

It includes old and new cases. It is useful for chronic disease, resource
planning and "extension/magnitude" in a population.

Local memory phrase: prevalence is the photo.

Prevalence increases when incidence rises, disease duration increases, survival
improves, or cure/recovery is slow. It can decrease when deaths, cure or short
duration remove cases quickly.

### Cumulative incidence

Cumulative incidence measures risk of becoming a case during a period.

`cumulative incidence = new cases during period / population at risk at start`

The denominator excludes people who already had the disease at baseline and
people who cannot develop the event.

Local memory phrase: incidence is the video.

### Incidence density

Incidence density measures speed when follow-up time differs.

`incidence density = new cases / sum of person-time at risk`

Residentado anchor: ventilator-associated pneumonia with ventilator-days is
incidence density, not prevalence.

### Attack rate

Attack rate is cumulative incidence in an outbreak setting.

`attack rate = new outbreak cases / population exposed or at risk * 100`

ENCAPS anchor: 50 varicella cases in 100 school students gives attack rate 50%.

Take-home point: prevalence uses all cases; incidence uses new cases; density
uses person-time; attack rate is outbreak cumulative incidence.

## 4. Mortality and severity measures

### Mortality

Mortality measures deaths in a population.

`mortality = deaths / population * multiplier`

Cause-specific mortality keeps the population denominator but restricts the
numerator to one cause.

Residentado anchor: lung cancer deaths divided by total population gives
cause-specific mortality, not lethality.

### Lethality

Lethality measures fatality among cases.

`lethality = deaths from disease / cases of disease * 100`

Residentado anchor: 5 deaths among 50 dengue cases gives 10% lethality, even if
the region has 500000 people.

### Maternal mortality ratio

Local exam rule:

`maternal mortality ratio = maternal deaths / live births * 100000`

The denominator is live births, not all women or all pregnancies.

### Standardized mortality ratio

SMR compares observed deaths with expected deaths after standardization.

`SMR = observed deaths / expected deaths`

Residentado has used language such as "if Lima had Tokyo rates, expected deaths
would be 0.78 times..." as standardized mortality reasoning. Keep exact public
claims locked until the source is reviewed.

Take-home point: mortality asks deaths in the population; lethality asks deaths
among the sick.

## 5. Association measures

### Two-by-two table

| | Disease + | Disease - |
|---|---:|---:|
| Exposed + | a | b |
| Exposed - | c | d |

Use the table only after identifying the study design.

### Relative risk

Relative risk compares risks.

`Ie = a / (a + b)`

`Io = c / (c + d)`

`RR = Ie / Io`

Use RR when the study can calculate incidence or risk: cohort or outbreak.

Interpretation:

- RR = 1: no association.
- RR > 1: exposure is associated with higher risk.
- RR < 1: exposure is associated with lower risk/protection.

### Odds ratio

Odds ratio compares odds.

`OR = (a * d) / (b * c)`

Use OR for case-control studies. OR approximates RR when the outcome is rare;
as disease becomes common, OR can exaggerate the RR.

### Prevalence ratio

Prevalence ratio compares prevalence between groups.

`RP = prevalence in exposed / prevalence in unexposed`

Use RP in cross-sectional studies. It shows association but does not prove
temporality.

### Confidence intervals

For association measures, the null value is 1.

- CI 95% includes 1: not statistically significant.
- CI 95% excludes 1: statistically significant.

Take-home point: cohort uses RR, case-control uses OR, cross-sectional uses RP.

## 6. Impact and effect measures

### Attributable risk

Attributable risk is an absolute excess.

`RA = Ie - Io`

It answers: how much extra risk in exposed is attributable to exposure?

### Attributable fraction among exposed

`FAE = (Ie - Io) / Ie`

It answers: what proportion of cases among exposed would be avoided if the
exposure disappeared, assuming causality?

### Population attributable fraction

`FAP = (Ip - Io) / Ip`

It answers: what proportion of cases in the population is attributable to the
exposure, assuming causality?

### Absolute risk reduction and NNT

For beneficial interventions:

`ARR/RAR = risk_control - risk_treatment`

`NNT = 1 / ARR`

If risks are expressed as percentages:

`NNT = 100 / absolute percentage reduction`

Example: placebo MI 10%, drug MI 5%. ARR = 5%, NNT = 20.

### Relative risk reduction

`RRR = ARR / risk_control`

RRR sounds impressive but hides baseline risk. NNT is usually more clinically
intuitive.

### Harm and NNH

For harm:

`ARI = risk_exposed - risk_unexposed`

`NNH = 1 / ARI`

A high NNH is safer than a low NNH.

For impact/difference measures, the null value is 0. If the confidence interval
includes 0, the difference is not statistically significant.

Take-home point: association tells "how related"; impact tells "how much could
change".

## 7. Exam algorithm

1. Identify the event: case, new case, death, exposure, avoided event or harm.
2. Identify the population that could enter the numerator.
3. Check if time/follow-up differs: if yes, consider person-time.
4. Identify the study design:
   - cohort/outbreak: RR.
   - case-control: OR.
   - cross-sectional: RP or prevalence.
5. Choose the multiplier only after the correct fraction.
6. Interpret the value and CI:
   - RR/OR/RP null = 1.
   - RA/ARR null = 0.

Take-home point: design chooses association measure; denominator chooses
frequency measure.

## 8. Local exam patterns

| Stem clue | Correct move |
|---|---|
| "Extension of chronic disease in a population in a year" | Prevalence. |
| "New cases among healthy at start" | Cumulative incidence. |
| "Ventilator-days, catheter-days, person-years" | Incidence density. |
| "Deaths among cases" | Lethality. |
| "Deaths from one cause among total population" | Cause-specific mortality. |
| "Maternal deaths / live births" | Maternal mortality ratio per 100000. |
| "Cohort exposed vs unexposed" | RR. |
| "Cases and controls" | OR. |
| "Cross-sectional exposure and disease at same time" | RP. |
| "How many treated to avoid one event" | NNT from ARR. |

## 9. Must-not-confuse list

- Prevalence is not risk of becoming sick.
- Incidence is not all cases.
- Mortality is not lethality.
- Attack rate is not an attack "speed"; it is outbreak risk.
- RR is not for classic case-control data.
- OR is not an exact RR when the outcome is common.
- NNT high is weaker benefit, not stronger.
- NNH high is safer harm profile.
- CI crossing 1 matters for ratios; CI crossing 0 matters for differences.

## 10. Product caution

This package is ready for internal class and qbank development. It remains
`fail_to_publish` for public manual use because SP-1.2 has no approved source A
for normative claims and several local labels require source-lock: "tasa",
SMR wording, R0 boundary, and "riesgo absoluto" as an exam synonym.
