units.title: Artritis reumatoide
units.body:
# Artritis reumatoide

## Guion de la condicion

Artritis reumatoide is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis. The classic exam picture is a middle-aged woman with symmetric synovitis of MCF, IFP/PIP, and wrists, morning stiffness >1 h, elevated inflammatory markers, and anti-CCP/RF positivity.

The practical danger is treating it as "joint pain". RA destroys cartilage and bone if DMARD therapy is delayed.

**Take-home point:** RA is inflammatory symmetric small-joint synovitis that needs early DMARD therapy.

## 1. Por que da

### Mechanism

- Genetic predisposition, classically HLA-DR4/HLA-DRB1 shared epitope.
- Environmental triggers such as smoking and mucosal inflammation can promote citrullination.
- Loss of tolerance generates autoantibodies such as anti-CCP/ACPA and RF.
- Synovial inflammation recruits T cells, B cells, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, cytokines, and osteoclast activation.
- Pannus erodes cartilage and bone, producing marginal erosions, deformity, and functional loss.

### Concepto preguntable

- Anti-CCP is highly specific and prognostic for erosive/aggressive disease.
- RF is supportive but nonspecific; it can be positive in infections, other autoimmune disease, chronic liver disease, and healthy older adults.
- ESR/CRP measure activity, not specificity.
- DMARDs change prognosis; NSAIDs and glucocorticoids do not prevent erosions by themselves.

**Take-home point:** The immune target is the synovium; the clinical consequence is erosive deforming disease.

## 2. A quien

### Typical patient

- Woman 40-60 years.
- Family history can appear.
- Smoking and seropositive disease increase risk and severity.
- Men with RA can have more extra-articular disease in local teaching.

### Local tested phenotypes

| Phenotype | Stem clue | Exam move |
|---|---|---|
| Classic diagnosis | MCF/IFP bilateral, morning stiffness, synovitis | Anti-CCP or ACR/EULAR classification |
| Treatment choice | "Drug of choice" in AR | Methotrexate |
| Advanced hand deformity | Ulnar deviation, boutonniere, swan neck | Chronic erosive RA |
| Extra-articular disease | Nodules, Felty, pleural effusion, Caplan, ILD | Seropositive/severe RA |
| Cervical complication | Neck pain/myelopathy in RA | Atlantoaxial subluxation |
| Drug toxicity | MTX + macrocytosis/transaminitis/pneumonitis | MTX toxicity/folate pathway |

**Take-home point:** The core exam patient is not elderly DIP osteoarthritis; it is inflammatory MCF/IFP synovitis.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Articular pattern

- Symmetric polyarthritis.
- MCF and IFP/PIP are classic.
- Wrists are common.
- Can involve elbows, shoulders, knees, ankles, and feet.
- DIP are typically spared.
- Sacroiliac, dorsal, and lumbar spine are not classic RA targets.
- Cervical C1-C2 can be affected in established disease.

### Symptoms and exam

- Morning stiffness >1 h.
- Pain, swelling, warmth, and limited range of motion.
- Improvement with movement can appear.
- Fatigue and constitutional symptoms may accompany active disease.

### Deformities

| Deformity | Pattern |
|---|---|
| Boutonniere | IFP/PIP flexion + DIP hyperextension |
| Swan neck | IFP/PIP hyperextension + DIP flexion |
| Ulnar deviation | MCF deviation toward ulnar side |
| Hallux valgus/forefoot disease | Chronic foot involvement |

**Take-home point:** RA loves MCF/IFP/wrist and spares DIP; that single map prevents many wrong answers.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Clinical diagnosis

Start with the phenotype:

- Definite clinical synovitis in at least one joint.
- Symmetric small-joint involvement.
- Duration often >=6 weeks.
- No better explanation such as septic arthritis, crystal arthritis, osteoarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, SLE, viral arthritis, or spondyloarthritis.

### Laboratory tests

| Test | Meaning | Exam use |
|---|---|---|
| Anti-CCP/ACPA | High specificity; prognostic for erosive disease | Best serologic/confirmatory exam answer |
| RF | Common but nonspecific | Supportive, not definitive |
| ESR/CRP | Inflammatory activity | Activity and ACR/EULAR points |
| CBC | Anemia of chronic disease; cytopenia/toxicity | Baseline and monitoring |
| Creatinine/LFTs | Drug safety | Before/while MTX and other DMARDs |
| Synovial fluid | Inflammatory; rule out infection/crystal | Use if monoarthritis/acute/septic concern |

### Imaging

- X-ray early: soft-tissue swelling or normal.
- X-ray established: juxta-articular osteopenia, joint-space narrowing, marginal/subchondral erosions, deformities.
- Ultrasound: synovitis, power Doppler activity, early erosions.
- MRI: sensitive for early synovitis/erosions, not routine for every initial exam case.

**Take-home point:** Anti-CCP helps confirm the classic stem, but RA remains a clinical inflammatory-synovitis diagnosis.

## 2. Clasificacion

### ACR/EULAR 2010 logic

Prerequisite:

- At least one joint with clinical synovitis.
- Synovitis not better explained by another disease.

Score domains:

| Domain | High-yield points |
|---|---|
| Joint involvement | More small joints = more points; >10 joints with at least one small joint gives highest joint score |
| Serology | RF and/or anti-CCP positive; high titer gives more points |
| Acute phase reactants | ESR and/or CRP elevated |
| Duration | >=6 weeks adds a point |

Exam shortcut:

- Small-joint polyarthritis + high anti-CCP + elevated CRP/ESR + duration >=6 weeks usually reaches classification threshold.

### Prognostic/severity features

- High anti-CCP or high RF.
- Early erosions.
- High disease activity.
- Many swollen joints.
- Extra-articular disease.
- Functional impairment.
- Smoking.

**Take-home point:** Use the criteria to structure the diagnosis, but first exclude better explanations.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Non-pharmacologic and baseline

- Refer early to rheumatology when possible.
- Educate about chronic relapsing disease and adherence.
- Stop smoking.
- Exercise/physical therapy and hand function protection.
- Vaccination review before immunosuppression.
- Assess cardiovascular risk, osteoporosis risk, infection risk, pregnancy plans, TB/hepatitis risk.

**Take-home point:** Non-drug care protects function and safety, but it does not replace DMARDs.

### B. Symptom control while DMARD works

- NSAIDs can reduce pain/stiffness but do not prevent erosions.
- Glucocorticoids can be used short-term as bridge therapy or for flares.
- Avoid chronic steroid monotherapy.

**Take-home point:** Steroids are a bridge, not the foundation.

### C. csDMARD anchor

Local exam first line:

- Methotrexate 15-25 mg/week PO or SC.
- Add folic acid 5-10 mg/week, often 1-2 days after MTX in local card.
- Expected onset: several weeks.

Before and during MTX:

- CBC.
- Creatinine.
- AST/ALT.
- Hepatitis/TB/infection risk as protocol indicates.
- Pregnancy avoidance: MTX is teratogenic.
- Review alcohol/liver disease and renal function.

Alternatives or adjuncts:

- Leflunomide.
- Sulfasalazine.
- Hydroxychloroquine.
- Triple therapy: MTX + sulfasalazine + hydroxychloroquine in selected contexts.

**Take-home point:** The local answer to "drug of choice" is MTX plus folic acid.

### D. Treat-to-target and escalation

Goal:

- Remission or low disease activity.

Monitoring:

- Reassess disease activity and tolerability within about 3 months.
- If no meaningful improvement or target is not reached, adjust therapy.

Escalation options:

- Optimize MTX dose/route if tolerated.
- Add/switch csDMARDs in lower-risk contexts.
- Add bDMARD or tsDMARD/JAK inhibitor in persistent active disease, especially with severe/erosive disease.
- Use biologics with MTX when possible to improve efficacy and reduce immunogenicity.

Current modifier:

- EULAR 2025 no longer emphasizes post-failure poor-prognosis stratification as strongly as older/local ladders; after initial treatment failure, failure itself is a risk marker.

**Take-home point:** RA treatment is adjusted until the target is reached, not left on the first prescription forever.

### E. Biologic and JAK safety

Before biologic/JAK therapy:

- Screen latent TB.
- Screen hepatitis B and C.
- Check vaccination status.
- Avoid live vaccines during significant immunosuppression.
- Consider history of serious infection, malignancy, demyelinating disease, severe heart failure, thrombosis/MACE risk, and pregnancy plans.

Class examples:

- Anti-TNF: infliximab, adalimumab, etanercept, certolizumab, golimumab.
- IL-6 pathway: tocilizumab, sarilumab.
- T-cell co-stimulation: abatacept.
- B-cell depletion: rituximab.
- JAK inhibitors: tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib.

**Take-home point:** The exam trap before anti-TNF is forgetting TB screening.

## 4. Complicaciones

### Articular

- Erosions.
- Joint-space narrowing.
- Deformities: ulnar deviation, boutonniere, swan neck.
- Tendon rupture.
- Carpal tunnel syndrome.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation and cervical myelopathy.
- Disability and loss of function.

### Extra-articular

| System | Manifestations |
|---|---|
| Skin/subcutaneous | Rheumatoid nodules over pressure areas |
| Hematologic | Anemia of chronic disease; Felty syndrome = RA + splenomegaly + neutropenia |
| Pulmonary/pleural | Pleural effusion, nodules, ILD, Caplan syndrome |
| Cardiac | Pericarditis most classic |
| Eye | Keratoconjunctivitis sicca, episcleritis, scleritis |
| Renal/systemic | AA amyloidosis in long uncontrolled disease |
| Bone | Osteoporosis from inflammation and steroids |

Pleural lock:

- Rheumatoid pleural effusion can have very low glucose, often <30 mg/dL, low pH/complement, and RF positivity.

**Take-home point:** Seropositive severe RA is the one that tends to leave the joints and become systemic.

## 5. Seguimiento

Follow:

- Tender/swollen joint counts and patient symptoms.
- ESR/CRP.
- Disease activity score if available.
- Functional status and pain.
- CBC, creatinine, AST/ALT for MTX and other DMARDs.
- Infection symptoms and vaccination status.
- Radiographic/ultrasound progression if disease remains active.
- Steroid exposure, osteoporosis prevention, cardiovascular risk.
- Pregnancy planning and drug safety.

When stable:

- Continue DMARD therapy.
- Dose reduction can be considered in sustained remission, but stopping completely is generally discouraged in current EULAR framing because flares are common.

**Take-home point:** Follow disease activity and toxicity together.

## 6. Pronostico

Prognosis improves when RA is diagnosed early and treated with DMARDs before erosions accumulate.

Poor prognostic factors:

- High anti-CCP or RF.
- Early erosions.
- Persistent high ESR/CRP.
- High swollen-joint count.
- Extra-articular disease.
- Smoking.
- Delayed DMARD therapy.

**Take-home point:** Early MTX/treat-to-target prevents the deforming version of the disease.

units.title: Hemorragia digestiva
units.body:
# Hemorragia digestiva

## Guion de la condicion

Hemorragia digestiva is bleeding into the GI tract. The exam does not reward naming every cause; it rewards choosing the next step from the patient's stability and the likely source.

The most dangerous error is trying to "diagnose with endoscopy" before resuscitating a hypotensive patient.

**Take-home point:** Hemorragia digestiva is source plus stability: stabilize first, then localize.

## 1. Por que da

### Mechanisms

- Mucosal/arterial erosion: peptic ulcer, erosive gastropathy, cancer.
- Portal hypertension: esophageal or gastric varices.
- Vascular lesion: angiodysplasia, Dieulafoy lesion.
- Diverticular vessel rupture.
- Ischemia: low-flow injury to watershed colon.
- Neoplasia or polyp bleeding.
- Anorectal lesion: hemorrhoids, fissure.

### Concepto preguntable

- HDA is bleeding proximal to the angle of Treitz.
- HDB is bleeding distal to the angle of Treitz.
- Hematemesis is upper until proven otherwise.
- Melena usually means upper bleeding or slow transit.
- Hematochezia usually means lower bleeding, but massive upper bleeding can also produce hematochezia.
- Obscure bleeding means EGD and colonoscopy are negative but bleeding persists; this is when small bowel evaluation/capsule enters.

**Take-home point:** The bleeding label is anatomical, but the first decision is physiologic: stable or unstable.

## 2. A quien

### High-yield patient groups

| Patient | Likely source | Exam clue |
|---|---|---|
| NSAID or H. pylori history | Peptic ulcer HDA | Epigastric pain, melena, hematemesis |
| Cirrhosis/alcohol/portal signs | Variceal HDA | Jaundice, telangiectasias, collateral circulation |
| Elderly painless hematochezia | Diverticular bleeding or angiodysplasia | Often spontaneous stop |
| Elderly with DM/HTN/vascular disease | Ischemic colitis | Pain + diarrhea + blood |
| Older adult with occult blood | CRC/polyp pathway | FIT/SOH positive |
| Chronic red flags | Gastric cancer | Early satiety, weight loss, Virchow node, melena |

### Local tested phenotypes

| Phenotype | Tested answer |
|---|---|
| NSAID HDA after omeprazole bolus | Continuous infusion `8 mg/h` |
| Variceal bleed controlled with endoligation | `Carvedilol` as secondary prophylaxis |
| Chronic epigastric pain, early satiety, Virchow node, melena | Gastric neoplasm |
| Tortuous bleeding artery in lesser curvature | Dieulafoy lesion |
| Melena with orthostatic change | `10-20` local blood-loss/volume rule |
| Population CRC screening | Immunochemical fecal occult blood test/FIT |
| Positive occult blood in 75-year-old | Colonoscopy |

**Take-home point:** The stem usually gives the source if you respect the risk profile.

## 3. Como se presenta

### HDA

- Hematemesis.
- Melena.
- Hematochezia if bleeding is massive/rapid.
- Syncope, dizziness, orthostasis, tachycardia, hypotension if significant.
- Elevated BUN/Cr ratio can support upper source.

### HDB

- Rectorrhagia or hematochezia.
- Diverticular bleeding is often painless.
- Ischemic colitis adds abdominal pain, urgency, diarrhea, and blood.
- Hemorrhoids classically cause bright red blood with defecation; internal hemorrhoids are often painless.

### Occult bleeding

- Positive fecal occult blood/FIT.
- Iron deficiency anemia.
- No visible hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia.

**Take-home point:** Vomit/stool language is the fastest source clue, but shock overrides source workup.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### First diagnostic act: severity

Assess immediately:

- Airway risk and aspiration risk.
- Blood pressure, heart rate, perfusion, mental status.
- Orthostatic changes.
- Active hematemesis/hematochezia.
- CBC, urea/creatinine, electrolytes, liver panel if relevant, PT/INR, type and crossmatch.
- Medication review: NSAID, anticoagulants, antiplatelets.
- Cirrhosis signs.

Initial stabilization:

- Two large-bore IV lines.
- Crystalloid resuscitation when unstable.
- Restrictive RBC transfusion: local/current anchor Hb <=7 g/dL, goal 7-9; cardiovascular disease threshold around <=8 with higher target.
- Do not delay resuscitation for endoscopy.

**Take-home point:** In the unstable patient, "diagnosis" begins with perfusion, not with the endoscope.

### Source tests

| Scenario | Test |
|---|---|
| Suspected HDA | Upper endoscopy/EGD after resuscitation, usually within 24 h |
| Suspected ulcer HDA | EGD with Forrest classification |
| Suspected variceal HDA | EGD with EVL capability; treat medically before confirmation if suspected |
| Stable HDB | Colonoscopy pathway |
| Ongoing hemodynamically significant HDB | CTA to localize active bleeding, then arteriography/embolization if indicated |
| Positive occult blood in older adult | Colonoscopy |
| Obscure bleeding after negative EGD and colonoscopy | Small bowel evaluation/capsule endoscopy |

**Take-home point:** Capsule is not the answer for first positive occult blood; colonoscopy is.

## 2. Clasificacion

### By source

- HDA: proximal to angle of Treitz.
- HDB: distal to angle of Treitz.
- Occult bleeding: lab/stool test positive or iron deficiency without visible bleeding.
- Obscure bleeding: persistent/recurrent bleeding after negative EGD and colonoscopy.

### By hemodynamic severity

- Stable: normal perfusion without ongoing significant blood loss.
- Orthostatic: suggests clinically significant volume loss; local RM row uses `10-20` in a melena/orthostasis stem.
- Unstable: hypotension, tachycardia, syncope, shock, altered perfusion.

### Forrest classification for ulcer bleeding

| Forrest | Finding | Local rebleed risk | Local exam action |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Ia | Spurting active bleeding | 55% | Endoscopic hemostasis |
| Ib | Oozing active bleeding | 50% | Endoscopic hemostasis |
| IIa | Nonbleeding visible vessel | 43% | Endoscopic hemostasis |
| IIb | Adherent clot | 22% | Local high-risk; see modifier |
| IIc | Flat pigmented spot/hematin | 7% | Low risk |
| III | Clean base/fibrin | 2% | Low risk |

Product modifier:

- Local ENAM card treats Ia-IIb as high-risk.
- ESGE 2021 treats Ia/Ib/IIa directly, considers clot removal in IIb, and does not treat IIc/III endoscopically.

**Take-home point:** Forrest is not decoration; it predicts rebleeding and changes therapy.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Universal first step

1. Stabilize airway/breathing/circulation as needed.
2. Place IV access, fluids, labs, type/crossmatch.
3. Transfuse restrictively unless special cardiovascular context.
4. Hold/reverse anticoagulants or antiplatelets only by risk logic; do not stop secondary-prevention aspirin casually.
5. Then choose HDA, HDB, occult, or obscure pathway.

**Take-home point:** If the patient is hypotensive, the correct first answer is resuscitation.

### B. Nonvariceal HDA, especially peptic ulcer

Local sequence:

1. Hemodynamic stabilization.
2. PPI IV.
3. Upper endoscopy in 12-24 h/within 24 h after resuscitation.
4. Forrest-guided endoscopic hemostasis.
5. High-dose PPI after hemostasis.
6. Treat the cause: eradicate H. pylori, stop NSAID when possible, evaluate gastric ulcer for malignancy.

Local RM anchor:

- After omeprazole bolus in ulcer-type HDA, continuous infusion `8 mg/h` is the tested answer.

Endoscopic therapy:

- Do not use epinephrine/adrenaline alone as definitive therapy.
- Combine injection with mechanical or thermal therapy when appropriate.
- Clips, thermal therapy, APC, hemostatic powder, or OTSC can appear depending on lesion and recurrence.

Escalation:

- Recurrent bleeding after initial endoscopic therapy: repeat endoscopy is favored in current ACG logic.
- Failed endoscopic therapy: TAE is favored before surgery when available.
- Surgery remains for unavailable/failed embolization, uncontrolled shock, or refractory/recurrent bleeding in local surgical thresholds.

**Take-home point:** Ulcer HDA is PPI plus early EGD; Forrest tells you how aggressive to be.

### C. Variceal HDA

Suspect when:

- Cirrhosis, chronic alcohol disease, jaundice, ascites, splenomegaly, telangiectasias, collateral circulation.
- Hematemesis/melena, often massive.

Acute bundle:

1. Stabilize.
2. Start vasoactive drug as soon as suspected: somatostatin, octreotide, or terlipressin depending on protocol.
3. Give antibiotic prophylaxis, locally ceftriaxone/third-generation cephalosporin or quinolone logic.
4. Perform EGD with EVL for esophageal varices.
5. Use cyanoacrylate/glue concepts for fundal gastric varices when applicable.
6. Prevent/treat hepatic encephalopathy with lactulose when indicated.
7. Do not start beta-blocker during the acute bleeding/hypotensive phase.

Local duration:

- Local ENAM/RM teaching uses vasoactive therapy for 5 days.
- Baveno VII current modifier: 2-5 days.

Failure/rescue:

- Balloon tamponade or self-expanding esophageal stent can bridge uncontrolled bleeding.
- Definitive rescue/high-risk strategy: TIPS.
- Preemptive TIPS in high risk: Child-Pugh C below 14/local <14, Child-Pugh B >7 with active bleeding, or HVPG >20 mmHg.

Secondary prophylaxis after control:

- Nonselective beta-blocker plus repeated EVL.
- Local RM row accepts carvedilol after endoligation in a stable post-bleed context.

**Take-home point:** Acute variceal bleed is vasoactive drug + antibiotic + EVL; carvedilol belongs after control, not during shock.

### D. Lower GI bleeding

Common causes:

- Diverticular disease: common in adults >40/elderly, often painless, often stops spontaneously.
- Angiodysplasia: elderly, intermittent, vascular.
- Ischemic colitis: pain + diarrhea + blood in elderly/vasculopathy.
- CRC: occult blood, rectal bleeding, bowel habit change, anemia.
- Hemorrhoids: bright red blood with defecation, internal often painless.
- IBD/polyps depending on age and chronic symptoms.

Management:

- Stabilize first.
- Stable lower bleeding: colonoscopy pathway.
- Ongoing hemodynamically significant lower bleeding: CTA to localize active bleeding; arteriography/embolization if positive and persistent.
- Surgery if embolization/endoscopic control fails or if peritonitis/gangrene.

Ischemic colitis:

- Typical: older patient with vascular risk, crampy abdominal pain, urgency, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding.
- Usually left colon/splenic flexure; rectum often spared.
- Colonoscopy in first 48 h with low insufflation and no prep in local card.
- Conservative treatment: bowel rest, fluids, antibiotics when indicated.
- Surgery for gangrene, peritonitis, persistent bleeding, or deterioration.

**Take-home point:** Lower bleeding is not one pathway: stable goes colonoscopy, ongoing significant bleeding goes CTA localization.

### E. Occult, neoplasm, and special lesions

Occult blood:

- Screening test/FIT positive in an older adult requires colonoscopy.
- Capsule is for obscure bleeding after negative EGD and colonoscopy.

Gastric neoplasm:

- Chronic epigastric pain not relieved by food, early satiety, weight loss, melena, Virchow node, and epigastric mass point to gastric cancer.
- Gastric ulcer requires malignancy evaluation/biopsy and follow-up until healing in manual-grade teaching.

Dieulafoy lesion:

- Acute upper bleeding from a tortuous/submucosal artery, classically in the lesser curvature, with little surrounding mucosal disease.
- RM clue: "arteria tortuosa sangrante en curvatura menor".

**Take-home point:** Occult blood means colonoscopy; named lesions are recognition traps, not the main algorithm.

## 4. Complicaciones

- Hypovolemic shock.
- Rebleeding.
- Aspiration.
- Myocardial ischemia in vulnerable patients.
- Acute kidney injury.
- Transfusion complications.
- In cirrhosis: spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, worsening liver failure, death.
- In ischemic colitis: gangrene, perforation, peritonitis, stricture.
- Missed malignancy.

**Take-home point:** Rebleeding risk is why risk scores, Forrest, and monitoring matter.

## 5. Seguimiento

After ulcer HDA:

- Continue PPI strategy according to lesion risk.
- Test and eradicate H. pylori.
- Avoid NSAIDs or protect if unavoidable.
- Plan antiplatelet/anticoagulant restart by thrombotic versus bleeding risk.
- Biopsy/follow gastric ulcer if malignancy concern.

After variceal HDA:

- Secondary prophylaxis: NSBB plus serial EVL.
- Monitor highest rebleed risk first week; local ENAM mentions monitoring across 6 weeks.
- Assess TIPS/transplant pathway if recurrent/high risk.

After HDB/occult bleeding:

- Complete colon evaluation.
- Treat lesion found.
- Repeat testing/surveillance according to pathology and local norm.

**Take-home point:** Follow-up is source-specific: H. pylori for ulcer, NSBB/EVL for varices, colon completion for occult/lower.

## 6. Pronostico

- Most diverticular bleeding and many ulcer bleeds stop spontaneously, but rebleeding risk determines management.
- Variceal first bleeding has high mortality; local card states >20%.
- Forrest Ia/Ib/IIa have high rebleeding risk; IIc/III are low risk.
- Ischemic colitis is often reversible when mucosal/left-sided, but right-sided/gangrenous disease is high risk.
- Cancer-associated bleeding prognosis depends on stage and diagnostic delay.

**Take-home point:** Prognosis is not "how much blood came out"; it is source, stability, comorbidity, and rebleeding risk.

## Mini-Drills

1. NSAID user, hematemesis, BP 80/50: first step?
   - Stabilize with IV access/resuscitation; PPI/endoscopy come after initial stabilization.

2. Same patient after omeprazole bolus; infusion rate answer in local RM?
   - 8 mg/h.

3. Cirrhotic with hematemesis, EVL done, now stable follow-up medication?
   - Nonselective beta-blocker; local row answer carvedilol.

4. Elderly diabetic/hypertensive with abdominal pain, diarrhea, rectal blood?
   - Ischemic colitis.

5. 75-year-old with positive occult blood?
   - Colonoscopy.

6. Negative EGD and colonoscopy but ongoing bleeding?
   - Obscure bleeding; evaluate small bowel/capsule.

## Traceability

- ENAM HDA/HDB/variceal/Forrest/HDB content: `Cards/107_hemorragia_digestiva.md`.
- Cirrhosis-variceal bundle: `Cards/026_cirrosis_hepatica.md`.
- Ulcer HDA/H. pylori/gastric ulcer support: `Cards/208_ulcera_peptica.md`.
- RM exact answers: Residentado phenotype rows listed in `source-map.md`.
- Current guidance modifiers: ACG 2021 UGI/ulcer, ESGE 2021 NVUGIH, ACG 2023 LGIB, Baveno VII.

## QA Status

`qa_pending`

Do not mark as public clinical protocol until `qa.md` is resolved.
units.example: Hemorragia digestiva is bleeding into the GI tract. The exam does not reward naming every cause; it rewards choosing the next step from the patient's stability and the likely source. The most dangerous error is trying to "diagnose with endoscopy" before resuscitating a hypotensive patient. **Take-home point:** Hemorragia digestiva is source plus stability: stabilize first, then localize. - Mucosal/arterial erosion: peptic ulcer, erosive gastropathy, cancer. - Portal hypertension: esophageal or gastric varices. - Vascular lesion: angiodysplasia, Dieulafoy lesion. - Diverticular vessel rupture.

units.title: Patologia testicular
units.body:
# Patologia testicular

## Guion del cluster

Patologia testicular is a cluster, not a single condition. The safest mental map has two doors:

1. Acute scrotal pain: rule out torsion first.
2. Testicular/scrotal mass: decide solid intratesticular cancer versus fluid/benign/extratesticular lesion.

**Take-home point:** Pain asks about ischemia; mass asks about cancer.

## 1. Por que da

### Mechanisms

- Torsion: twisting of the spermatic cord blocks venous return first, then arterial flow, then infarction.
- Epididymitis/orchiepididymitis: infection/inflammation from STI pathogens or enteric/uropathogens.
- Testicular cancer: usually germ-cell tumor; cryptorchidism and gonadal dysgenesis increase risk.
- Hydrocele: fluid around the testis, often communicating through a patent processus vaginalis in children.
- Varicocele: dilated pampiniform venous plexus, usually left-sided.
- Cryptorchidism: undescended testis; relevant for fertility and cancer risk.

### Conceptos preguntables

- Torsion is a time-dependent surgical emergency.
- Doppler can support diagnosis, but classic torsion should not wait for imaging.
- A hard painless solid intratesticular mass is cancer until proven otherwise.
- AFP never rises in pure seminoma.
- Tumor markers help classify/stage/follow, but normal markers do not exclude cancer.
- Testicular cancer surgery is inguinal, not scrotal.

**Take-home point:** Vascular loss, infection, tumor, and fluid have different first moves.

## 2. A quien

| Patient | Most likely exam entity | Key clue |
|---|---|---|
| Child/adolescent with sudden severe scrotal pain | Torsion | High testis, absent cremasteric reflex, nausea/vomiting |
| Young sexually active man with progressive pain | Orchiepididymitis STI | Fever, dysuria/discharge, Prehn positive |
| Older man with urinary symptoms and scrotal pain | Orchiepididymitis enteric | Uropathy/instrumentation context |
| Man 20-35 with painless hard mass | Testicular cancer | Non-transilluminating intratesticular mass |
| Child with soft intermittent transilluminating scrotal mass | Communicating hydrocele | Size fluctuates |
| Older man with testicular mass | Lymphoma or secondary concern | >50 years |

### Local RM tested phenotypes

| Phenotype | Local answer |
|---|---|
| Sudden pain + high testis + decreased Doppler flow | Torsion testicular |
| Diagnostic test requested in acute suspected torsion | Eco Doppler |
| Sudden painful scrotal swelling | Exploracion quirurgica antes de las 6 horas |
| Diagnosed torsion, ideal timing | 00-06 |
| Absent cremasteric reflex, elevated/rotated testis | Exploracion quirurgica inmediata |
| Soft intermittent fluctuating transilluminating mass in 3-year-old | Hidrocele comunicante |

**Take-home point:** The RM cluster is mostly torsion timing and recognition; ENAM adds cancer markers.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Acute scrotum matrix

| Feature | Torsion | Orchiepididymitis | Tumor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Onset | Sudden | Progressive | Insidious |
| Pain | Severe acute | Progressive inflammatory | Usually painless |
| Fever | Usually absent early | Common | No |
| Cremasteric reflex | Absent | Usually present | Not central |
| Prehn sign | Negative/worse | Positive/improves | Not applicable |
| Testis position | High/horizontal | Normal polarity | Palpable mass |
| Doppler | Decreased/absent flow | Hypervascularity | Solid intraparenchymal mass |
| Treatment | Urgent surgery | Antibiotics | Inguinal orchiectomy |

### Testicular cancer presentation

- Painless hard intratesticular mass.
- Non-transilluminating.
- Sometimes heaviness or dull ache.
- 10% can debut as acute scrotum in local card.
- Gynecomastia can appear with hCG-producing tumors.
- Metastatic symptoms can be pulmonary/abdominal/back depending spread.

**Take-home point:** Sudden pain is torsion until proven otherwise; painless solid mass is cancer until proven otherwise.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Acute scrotal pain

Immediate clinical assessment:

- Time from onset.
- Pain onset: sudden versus progressive.
- Nausea/vomiting.
- Fever.
- Dysuria or urethral discharge.
- Testis position.
- Cremasteric reflex.
- Prehn sign as supportive local exam clue.
- Abdominal/inguinal exam for hernia.

Tests:

- Doppler ultrasound: absent/decreased flow supports torsion; increased flow supports epididymitis.
- Urine/NAAT/cultures: for epididymitis once torsion is not the priority.

Product modifier:

- If the exam asks "examen diagnostico" and the patient is not framed as a management emergency, local RM answer can be Eco Doppler.
- If the exam asks "conducta" in a classic torsion stem, answer urgent exploration, not delayed imaging.

**Take-home point:** Doppler is a diagnostic tool, not a permission slip to delay classic torsion.

### Testicular/scrotal mass

Initial evaluation:

- Physical exam: is it intratesticular, hard, solid, transilluminating?
- Scrotal/testicular ultrasound.
- Serum markers: AFP, hCG, LDH before orchiectomy.
- Repeat markers after orchiectomy according to half-lives.
- CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for staging after diagnosis in current guideline logic.

Marker interpretation:

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| AFP | Yolk sac tumor or embryonal carcinoma component; never pure seminoma |
| hCG | Choriocarcinoma; can rise in seminoma |
| LDH | Tumor burden/nonspecific staging marker |

**Take-home point:** Markers help, but ultrasound and pathology define the route; normal markers do not clear cancer.

## 2. Clasificacion

### Acute scrotum categories

- Torsion of spermatic cord.
- Torsion of appendix testis.
- Epididymitis/orchiepididymitis.
- Incarcerated hernia.
- Trauma/rupture.
- Tumor presenting acutely.
- Hydrocele/varicocele mimics.

### Testicular cancer histology

Germ-cell tumors are the majority.

| Type | Marker pattern | High-yield clue |
|---|---|---|
| Seminoma | hCG may rise; AFP never | Radiosensitive; common |
| Embryonal carcinoma | AFP may rise | Aggressive/mixed tumors |
| Yolk sac tumor | AFP | Classic pediatric germ-cell tumor |
| Choriocarcinoma | Very high hCG | Hematogenous spread, small primary |
| Teratoma | Variable | Mature elements; residual mass matters |

Non-germ-cell:

- Leydig cell tumor: hormonal effects/puberty signs.
- Sertoli cell tumor: can associate with Peutz-Jeghers.
- Lymphoma: think age >50.

### Staging frame

- Stage I: limited to testis.
- Retroperitoneal nodes are first typical nodal spread.
- Hematogenous spread: lung, liver, bone, CNS.
- Choriocarcinoma can spread hematogenously early.

**Take-home point:** Cancer classification is marker plus histology plus spread, not marker alone.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Torsion

Local exam chain:

1. Recognize sudden severe pain with high/horizontal testis and absent cremasteric reflex.
2. If diagnostic test is requested: Doppler can be the local answer.
3. If management is requested and suspicion is high: urgent surgical exploration.
4. Ideal local timing: 0-6 h.
5. Definitive operation: detorsion plus bilateral orchiopexy.

Manual detorsion:

- Can be attempted as a bridge when immediate surgery is not available.
- Must not delay surgical exploration.

Viability local table:

- >90% if treated <6 h.
- <50% by 12 h.
- <10% by 24 h.

**Take-home point:** Torsion is a clock, not a culture problem.

### B. Orchiepididymitis

Recognition:

- Progressive pain.
- Fever and inflammatory scrotal signs.
- Dysuria or urethral discharge.
- Prehn positive in local exam teaching.
- Doppler hypervascularity.

Cause split:

- <35 years or STI risk: Chlamydia and gonorrhea.
- >35 years, urinary obstruction, instrumentation: enteric/uropathogens.
- Brucellosis only if systemic/zoonotic exposure context.

Treatment local:

- STI: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline.
- Enteric/uropathogen: fluoroquinolone.

Current CDC modifier:

- Chlamydia/gonorrhea likely: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once plus doxycycline 100 mg BID for 10 days.
- Enteric-only when gonorrhea ruled out: levofloxacin 500 mg daily for 10 days.
- Severe pain/fever or uncertain diagnosis needs specialist/hospital consideration because torsion/infarction/abscess are alternatives.

**Take-home point:** Treat epididymitis only after torsion is no longer the dangerous missed diagnosis.

### C. Testicular cancer

Initial route:

1. Ultrasound of testis/scrotum.
2. AFP, hCG, LDH before orchiectomy.
3. Radical inguinal orchiectomy for suspicious solid intratesticular tumor.
4. Repeat markers after surgery using half-lives.
5. Stage with cross-sectional imaging after diagnosis.
6. Discuss fertility/sperm banking before treatment when possible.

Do not:

- Do not perform transscrotal biopsy.
- Do not reassure because AFP/hCG are normal.
- Do not call AFP-positive tumor a pure seminoma.

Post-treatment marker logic:

- AFP local half-life: 7 days; current range 5-7 days.
- hCG local half-life: 3 days; current range 1-3 days.
- Failure to fall as expected suggests residual/metastatic disease.

Residual mass local:

- Seminoma residual mass >3 cm after chemotherapy: PET if available.
- Nonseminomatous residual mass: resect.

**Take-home point:** The cancer answer is inguinal orchiectomy plus markers, not scrotal biopsy.

### D. Hydrocele, varicocele, cryptorchidism

Hydrocele:

- Soft, fluid, transilluminating.
- Communicating hydrocele fluctuates in size.
- RM 3-year-old intermittent/transilluminating mass: communicating hydrocele.
- Ultrasound if doubt about the mass.

Varicocele:

- "Bag of worms" venous plexus.
- Usually left-sided.
- Consider renal/retroperitoneal mass if sudden, right-sided, nonreducible, or in older adult.
- Fertility/growth implications require source-lock before manual-grade protocol.

Cryptorchidism:

- Risk factor for testicular cancer and infertility.
- Also a screening/pediatric prevention concept.
- Management timing needs local pediatric source-lock before public protocol expansion.

**Take-home point:** Transillumination points to fluid; solid intratesticular mass points to cancer.

## 4. Complicaciones

- Torsion: infarction, testicular loss, infertility/subfertility, chronic pain.
- Epididymitis: abscess, chronic pain, infertility, missed torsion or tumor.
- Testicular cancer: metastatic spread, residual disease, treatment infertility, second tumor risk.
- Hydrocele/hernia context: missed hernia or underlying testicular pathology.
- Cryptorchidism: infertility and increased cancer risk.

**Take-home point:** The complications are preventable only if the first split is correct.

## 5. Seguimiento

After torsion:

- Urology follow-up.
- Confirm bilateral orchiopexy status.
- Assess testicular viability/atrophy if delayed presentation.

After epididymitis:

- Reassess if no improvement within 72 h.
- Test/treat partners when STI suspected.
- Evaluate persistent swelling for tumor, abscess, infarction, TB/fungal causes.

After cancer:

- Repeat AFP/hCG/LDH according to half-life and follow-up protocol.
- Imaging surveillance or adjuvant therapy by stage/histology.
- Fertility/endocrine counseling when relevant.

After hydrocele/varicocele/cryptorchidism:

- Follow by age, symptoms, fertility/growth risk, and local pediatric/urology protocol.

**Take-home point:** Follow-up is where missed tumor and residual disease are caught.

## 6. Pronostico

- Torsion prognosis depends on time: local exam anchors excellent salvage before 6 h and sharp decline afterward.
- Testicular cancer prognosis is generally favorable in local card, with cure >90%, but depends on stage, histology, markers, and metastatic pattern.
- Seminoma is generally radiosensitive/chemosensitive.
- Nonseminomatous tumors and choriocarcinoma can behave more aggressively.
- Hydrocele is benign but can hide hernia or pathology if atypical.

**Take-home point:** Time determines torsion outcome; stage and marker kinetics determine cancer outcome.

## Mini-Drills

1. 10-year-old, sudden testicular pain for 3 h, nausea, high testis, decreased Doppler flow?
   - Torsion testicular.

2. Diagnosed torsion: ideal time window for surgery in RM?
   - 00-06 h.

3. 10-year-old after sport, absent cremasteric reflex, elevated/rotated testis: best treatment?
   - Exploracion quirurgica inmediata.

4. 14-year-old with sudden scrotal pain; exam asks diagnostic test?
   - Eco Doppler, if not delaying management.

5. 3-year-old with intermittent soft transilluminating scrotal mass?
   - Hidrocele comunicante.

6. Solid painless testicular mass with normal AFP/hCG?
   - Cancer still possible; markers normal do not exclude.

7. AFP elevated in a supposed seminoma?
   - Not pure seminoma; think nonseminomatous component.

## Traceability

- ENAM core: `Cards/090_patologia_testicular.md`.
- Epididymitis local support: `Cards/007_infeccion_del_tracto_urinario.md`.
- RM exact rows: Residentado rows listed in `source-map.md`.
- Current modifiers: EAU pediatric urology, CDC STI epididymitis, EAU testicular cancer, AUA testicular cancer/acute scrotum.

## QA Status

`qa_pending`

Do not mark as public clinical protocol until `qa.md` is resolved.

units.title: Infecciones micoticas de la piel
units.body:
# Infecciones micoticas de la piel

## Guion del cluster

Superficial cutaneous mycoses are a morphology cluster. The exam almost always gives the answer through location and lesion shape before it gives the organism.

The practical danger is saying "hongo = any antifungal". The drug and route depend on organism and site.

**Take-home point:** Identify the pattern first, then choose organism and route.

## 1. Por que da

### Organism groups

| Group | Agents | What they affect |
|---|---|---|
| Dermatophytes | Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton | Skin, hair, nails; not mucosa |
| Yeasts | Candida, Malassezia | Candida: folds/mucosa/nails; Malassezia: seborrheic skin |
| Special subcutaneous fungi | Sporothrix | Nodular lymphangitic pattern after thorn/trauma |

### Conceptos preguntables

- Dermatophytes eat keratin; that is why they involve skin, hair, and nails.
- Candida likes moisture, maceration, antibiotics, diabetes, pregnancy, immunosuppression.
- Malassezia is lipophilic; that is why it appears on trunk/back/seborrheic areas.
- Hair and nail infections often need systemic therapy because topical penetration is poor.
- Corticosteroids can hide tinea and create tinea incognito.

**Take-home point:** Site predicts organism because each fungus has a preferred ecological niche.

## 2. A quien

| Patient/context | Likely entity |
|---|---|
| Young person, heat, humidity, oily skin | Pityriasis versicolor |
| Child with scalp scaling/alopecia | Tinea capitis |
| Animal exposure + inflammatory scalp plaque | Kerion |
| Athlete/occlusive shoes/interdigital scaling | Tinea pedis |
| Obesity/diabetes/moist folds | Candida intertrigo |
| Adult/older with thick dystrophic toenail | Onychomycosis |
| Immunosuppressed/extensive/recurrent disease | More likely systemic therapy or broader workup |

### Local ENAM phenotypes

| Phenotype | Task |
|---|---|
| P01 | Identify classic diagnosis from lesion morphology |
| P09 | Choose tailored treatment |
| P07 | Choose first-line drug |
| P05 | Identify causal organism |

**Take-home point:** ENAM asks mostly "what is it?", then drug/route traps.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Morphology matrix

| Entity | Morphology | Key clue |
|---|---|---|
| Pityriasis versicolor | Hypo/hyperchromic macules with fine scale on trunk/back | Sign of scratching scale, Wood yellow-orange |
| Tinea corporis | Annular/circinate erythematosquamous plaque | Active raised border, centrifugal growth |
| Tinea pedis | Interdigital scaling or plantar scaling | Athlete's foot |
| Tinea cruris | Inguinal erythematosquamous plaque | Active border in groin |
| Tinea capitis | Alopecic scaly patches with broken hairs | Child |
| Kerion | Boggy erythematous exudative scalp plaque | Pus through follicles; inflammatory tinea |
| Onychomycosis | Thick/yellow nail, subungual hyperkeratosis, onycholysis | No perionychia if dermatophyte |
| Candida intertrigo | Erythematous fold plaque, fissure, satellite papules/pustules | Moist fold + diabetes/obesity |
| Candida nail | Proximal nail involvement | Perionychia |

**Take-home point:** Border, fold, hair, nail, and pigment are the five fast discriminators.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Clinical first

Most exam stems can be solved by:

- Location: trunk/back, scalp, feet, groin, folds, nails.
- Shape: annular active edge, macerated fold, pigment macules, alopecia, nail dystrophy.
- Host: child, diabetic, obese, immunosuppressed, animal contact, heat/humidity.

### Tests

| Test | Finding | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| KOH dermatophyte | Septate hyphae | Tinea |
| KOH Candida | Pseudohyphae + blastoconidia | Candidiasis |
| KOH Malassezia | Short hyphae + round spores, spaghetti-and-meatballs | Pityriasis versicolor |
| Wood lamp yellow-orange | Pityriasis versicolor | Malassezia clue |
| Wood lamp green | Microsporum canis | Some tinea capitis |
| Wood lamp coral red | Erythrasma | Bacterial mimic |
| Culture | Organism/species confirmation | Useful if atypical, recurrent, severe, treatment failure |

Product modifier:

- CDC/current practice supports confirming fungal nail infection before oral therapy when possible.

**Take-home point:** KOH tells the fungal architecture; Wood lamp gives a few high-yield colors.

## 2. Clasificacion

### By organism

- Dermatophytes: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton.
- Yeasts: Candida, Malassezia.
- Subcutaneous: Sporothrix when nodules climb lymphatics after thorn/trauma.

### By site

- Glabrous skin: tinea corporis.
- Scalp hair: tinea capitis, kerion, favus.
- Feet: tinea pedis.
- Groin: tinea cruris.
- Nails: tinea unguium/onychomycosis.
- Folds/mucosa: Candida.
- Trunk/back seborrheic: pityriasis versicolor.

### By treatment route

Topical usually:

- Localized tinea corporis/pedis/cruris.
- Localized pityriasis versicolor.
- Mild Candida intertrigo.

Systemic usually:

- Tinea capitis.
- Kerion/inflammatory tinea.
- Significant onychomycosis.
- Numerous/extensive lesions.
- Immunosuppression or recurrent/severe disease.

**Take-home point:** Hair and nail disease push you toward systemic therapy.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Pityriasis versicolor

Diagnosis:

- Malassezia.
- Young patient.
- Heat/humidity/sebum.
- Hypochromic or hyperchromic macules on trunk/back.
- Sign of scratching scale.
- Wood yellow-orange.
- KOH spaghetti-and-meatballs.

Treatment:

- Localized: topical azole such as ketoconazole/clotrimazole or selenium sulfide.
- Extensive or immunosuppressed: oral itraconazole or fluconazole in local card.
- Recurrences are common.

**Take-home point:** Malassezia changes pigment; it does not create an annular active border.

### B. Dermatophytosis/tinea of skin

Diagnosis:

- Annular/circinate erythematosquamous plaque.
- Active raised border.
- Centrifugal growth.
- Pruritus.
- KOH septate hyphae.

Treatment:

- Localized: topical terbinafine or azole.
- Extensive, numerous, inflammatory, hair/nail involvement: systemic antifungal.
- Avoid corticosteroid monotherapy; it can create tinea incognito.

**Take-home point:** The active edge is the dermatophyte signature.

### C. Tinea capitis and kerion

Tinea capitis:

- Child.
- Alopecic scaly plaques.
- Broken hairs.
- Gray scale.
- Trichophyton or Microsporum.
- Local classic treatment: oral griseofulvin 10-25 mg/kg/day for 6-8 weeks.

Kerion:

- Inflammatory tinea, often zoophilic.
- Boggy erythematous exudative scalp plaque.
- Pus from follicles when pressed.
- Can scar and cause alopecia cicatricial.
- Needs systemic therapy.

Current modifier:

- CDC says scalp ringworm needs oral prescription therapy; topical creams do not work for scalp ringworm.

**Take-home point:** Scalp hair involvement is systemic treatment territory.

### D. Onychomycosis

Dermatophyte nail disease:

- Thick/yellow nail.
- Subungual hyperkeratosis.
- Onycholysis.
- No perionychia.
- T. rubrum is common.

Candida nail disease:

- Proximal involvement.
- Perionychia.
- More tied to chronic wet work/immunometabolic context.

Treatment local:

- Adult dermatophyte onychomycosis: oral terbinafine 250 mg/day.
- Toenails: 2-3 months in local card.
- Fingernails: 6 weeks in local card.
- Topical therapy if chosen: at least 6 months.

**Take-home point:** Nail disease is not one bucket; perionychia points Candida, distal hyperkeratosis points dermatophyte.

### E. Candida cutaneous disease

Intertrigo:

- Moist fold.
- Erythematous plaque.
- Fissure at the base of the fold.
- Satellite papules/pustules.
- Risks: obesity, diabetes, humidity, antibiotics, pregnancy, immunosuppression.

Treatment:

- Keep area dry and reduce friction/moisture.
- Topical azole for localized disease.
- Consider systemic azole only for extensive/refractory/immunosuppressed cases after source-lock.
- Do not use oral terbinafine for Candida.

Other Candida forms:

- Muguet/oral candidiasis and vulvovaginitis are adjacent topics; do not let them dominate this skin package.

**Take-home point:** Satellite pustules in folds are Candida until proven otherwise.

### F. Special traps

Tinea incognito:

- Tinea altered by corticosteroid use.
- Border becomes atypical and less classic.
- Treat as dermatophyte and stop the wrong steroid-only logic.

Sporotrichosis:

- Nodular lesion after thorn/plant/soil trauma.
- Nodules ascend along lymphatics.
- Agent: Sporothrix schenckii.
- Belongs as an organism trap more than a main superficial tinea pathway.

Wood lamp:

- Yellow-orange: pityriasis versicolor.
- Green: Microsporum canis.
- Coral red: erythrasma.
- Trichophyton dermatophytes usually negative.

**Take-home point:** The exam loves wrong-color and wrong-spectrum traps.

## 4. Complicaciones

- Tinea capitis/kerion: alopecia cicatricial if severe/inflammatory/delayed.
- Tinea incognito: spread and atypical morphology after corticosteroid misuse.
- Onychomycosis: chronic nail dystrophy, recurrence, secondary bacterial infection risk in vulnerable feet.
- Candida intertrigo: maceration, fissures, bacterial superinfection, recurrence if moisture/diabetes persists.
- Resistant dermatophyte: persistent/recurrent/widespread disease despite standard therapy.

**Take-home point:** Complications usually come from delay, wrong steroid, wrong route, or untreated risk factor.

## 5. Seguimiento

- Reassess if no improvement with appropriate topical therapy.
- Confirm diagnosis with KOH/culture if atypical, recurrent, extensive, immunosuppressed, nail disease, or treatment failure.
- For systemic antifungals, check contraindications, pregnancy, liver disease, interactions, and local monitoring protocol.
- In Candida intertrigo, address moisture, glycemic control, obesity/friction, antibiotics, and occlusion.
- In recurrent/widespread tinea, consider resistant dermatophyte or steroid combination exposure.

**Take-home point:** Failure to improve should trigger diagnostic confirmation, not more steroid.

## 6. Pronostico

- Most localized superficial mycoses respond well to correct topical therapy.
- Pityriasis versicolor commonly recurs and pigment may take time to normalize after organism clearance.
- Tinea capitis and kerion need early systemic treatment to avoid scarring.
- Onychomycosis is slow to clear and often recurs.
- Candida intertrigo recurs if moisture and metabolic risk persist.

**Take-home point:** Prognosis is good when route and risk factors are correct; recurrence is the common enemy.

## Mini-Drills

1. Young patient, hypochromic macules on back, fine scale, Wood yellow-orange?
   - Pityriasis versicolor by Malassezia.

2. Annular pruritic plaque with active raised border?
   - Tinea corporis/dermatophyte.

3. Child with alopecia, broken hairs, gray scale?
   - Tinea capitis; oral griseofulvin is local classic answer.

4. Diabetic obese patient, erythematous fold plaque with satellite pustules?
   - Candida intertrigo.

5. Thick nail with subungual hyperkeratosis and no perionychia?
   - Dermatophyte onychomycosis.

6. Nail disease with proximal involvement and perionychia?
   - Candida nail disease.

7. Oral terbinafine for Candida intertrigo?
   - Wrong: oral terbinafine does not cover Candida.

## Traceability

- ENAM core: `Cards/047_infecciones_micoticas_de_la_pi.md`.
- Antifungal class support: `Cards/225_farmacologia_antimicrobiana.md`.
- Residentado direct source: none found; see `source-map.md`.
- Current modifiers: CDC ringworm treatment, CDC fungal nail guidance, CDC emerging/resistant dermatophytes.

## QA Status

`qa_pending`

Do not mark as public clinical protocol until `qa.md` is resolved.

units.title: Trastornos de ansiedad
units.body:
# Trastornos de ansiedad

## Guion del cluster

Los trastornos de ansiedad se resuelven con una matriz simple: tiempo, gatillo, cognicion y seguridad. Si el episodio es abrupto y espontaneo, piensa panico; si es preocupacion sostenida, piensa TAG; si es ritualizado, piensa TOC; si viene despues de trauma, piensa TEPT; si aparece solo ante un estimulo, piensa fobia.

El error caro es tratar toda ansiedad como "nervios" y saltar a benzodiazepina. Antes hay que descartar enfermedad medica, sustancias, abstinencia, depresion y riesgo suicida.

**Take-home point:** En ansiedad, el diagnostico sale de "cuando aparece" y "que lo dispara".

## 1. Por que da

### Mecanismos preguntables

| Trastorno | Mecanismo clinico util |
|---|---|
| Panico | Falsa alarma autonomica + interpretacion catastrofica de sensaciones corporales |
| TAG | Amenaza anticipada permanente, intolerancia a incertidumbre, tension sostenida |
| OCD/TOC | Obsesion intrusiva produce ansiedad; compulsiones alivian y refuerzan el ciclo |
| TEPT | Memoria traumatica + hipervigilancia + evitacion |
| Fobias | Aprendizaje de miedo ligado a un objeto/situacion concreta |
| Secundaria | Tiroides, hipoglucemia, arritmia, TEP/neumotorax/asma, estimulantes, abstinencia |

### Conceptos de examen

- Ataque de panico no equivale a trastorno de panico.
- Trastorno de panico exige ataques inesperados recurrentes mas preocupacion persistente o cambio conductual, tipicamente mas de 1 mes.
- TAG es preocupacion excesiva sobre muchos temas durante meses, classically 6 months.
- En TOC, las obsesiones son propias, intrusivas y ego-distonicas; no son delirios si hay juicio de realidad.
- En TEPT, el tiempo importa: menos de 1 mes post-trauma sugiere estres agudo; mas de 1 mes sugiere TEPT.

**Take-home point:** La fisiopatologia examinable no es molecular; es el circuito amenaza-evitacion-refuerzo.

## 2. A quien

| Contexto | Diagnostico probable |
|---|---|
| Mujer joven con crisis abruptas impredecibles, palpitaciones y miedo a morir | Trastorno de panico si recurrente + preocupacion |
| Persona con preocupacion por todo, tension muscular e insomnio durante meses | TAG |
| Adolescente/joven con rituales de lavado o verificacion | TOC |
| Paciente post-accidente/agresion/desastre con pesadillas y evitacion | TEPT o estres agudo segun tiempo |
| Adolescente con miedo intenso a evaluacion social | Ansiedad social |
| Paciente con miedo a sangre/inyecciones y sincope | Fobia especifica sangre-inyeccion-herida |
| Taquicardia, temblor, perdida de peso, calor, diarrea | Hipertiroidismo hasta demostrar lo contrario |
| Ansiedad tras suspender alcohol/BZD u opiaceos | Abstinencia |

### Local frequency

- ENAM card: 4 questions in 3 years.
- Residentado: 3 direct RM-GT-124 cases.
- Essalud: ledger mismatch; topics_current says 0, essalud_freq says n=4, priority ledger says Bronce.

**Take-home point:** El examen usa joven + temporalidad + gatillo para separar los cuadros.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Matrix de reconocimiento rapido

| Entidad | Presentacion clave | Trampa |
|---|---|---|
| Ataque de panico | Inicio brusco, pico en minutos, menos de 1 hora, palpitaciones/disnea/miedo a morir | Si es situacional, no es necesariamente trastorno de panico |
| Trastorno de panico | Crisis espontaneas recurrentes + preocupacion persistente/agorafobia/evitacion | Dar BZD cronica como unica respuesta |
| TAG | Preocupacion por multiples asuntos, tension, insomnio, fatiga, irritabilidad | No descartar hipertiroidismo, estimulantes, abstinencia |
| TOC | Obsesiones ego-distonicas + compulsiones de lavado/verificacion | Confundir con psicosis o personalidad anancastica |
| TEPT | Flashbacks/pesadillas + evitacion + hiperalerta | Dar BZD en trauma agudo |
| Fobia especifica | Miedo excesivo ante estimulo concreto | Llamarlo panico si hay sintomas autonomicos |
| Ansiedad social | Miedo a escrutinio social, debut adolescente | Alcohol "social" como automedicacion |

### Sintomas somaticos frecuentes

- Palpitaciones.
- Disnea/hiperventilacion.
- Dolor toracico.
- Sudoracion.
- Temblor.
- Mareo.
- Parestesias.
- Nauseas.
- Tension muscular.
- Insomnio.

**Take-home point:** El cuerpo grita parecido en muchos cuadros; la clave es el patron temporal.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Paso 1. Nombrar el patron

| Pregunta | Si responde "si" | Diagnostico que sube |
|---|---|---|
| Es abrupto, intenso, espontaneo y dura minutos? | Si | Panico |
| Son ataques recurrentes con miedo a nuevos ataques por mas de 1 mes? | Si | Trastorno de panico |
| Es preocupacion excesiva por muchas cosas durante meses? | Si | TAG |
| Hay pensamientos intrusivos propios + rituales? | Si | TOC |
| Hay trauma + flashbacks/pesadillas + evitacion + hiperalerta? | Si | TEPT |
| Solo aparece ante sangre, altura, animal, avion o publico? | Si | Fobia o ansiedad social |

### Paso 2. Descartar mimics antes de cerrar

Considerar segun contexto:

- TSH si hay perdida de peso, temblor, intolerancia al calor, diarrea, bocio.
- Glucemia si hay episodios con hambre, sudoracion, confusion o diabetes/tratamiento.
- ECG/troponina si dolor toracico, edad/riesgo cardiovascular o palpitaciones atipicas.
- Evaluacion respiratoria si disnea real, asma, neumotorax, TEP o hipoxemia.
- Sustancias: cafeina alta, cocaina/anfetaminas, cannabis en predispuestos.
- Abstinencia: alcohol, benzodiazepinas, opiaceos.
- Farmacos: SSRI al inicio, broncodilatadores, corticoides, antipsicotico con acatisia.

### Paso 3. Seguridad

Preguntar por:

- Ideacion suicida o autolesion.
- Depresion comorbida.
- Abuso de alcohol/sedantes.
- Psicosis, mania o delirium.
- Violencia/trauma activo.
- Deterioro funcional grave.

**Take-home point:** Antes de tratar ansiedad primaria, descarta cuerpo, sustancias y suicidio.

## 2. Clasificacion

### Por temporalidad y gatillo

| Tipo | Temporalidad | Gatillo |
|---|---|---|
| Panico | Minutos, episodico | Espontaneo/inesperado |
| TAG | Meses, continuo/fluctuante | Muchas preocupaciones cotidianas |
| TOC | Continuo/ritualizado | Obsesion interna |
| Estres agudo | Menos de 1 mes post-trauma | Trauma |
| TEPT | Mas de 1 mes post-trauma | Trauma/cues |
| Fobia especifica | Solo con estimulo | Objeto/situacion concreta |
| Ansiedad social | Situacional social | Evaluacion/escrutinio |
| Secundaria | Variable | Enfermedad, droga, abstinencia |

### Por urgencia

- Urgente: crisis de panico severa, suicidality, intoxicacion/abstinencia, dolor toracico/disnea con red flags, delirium/psicosis/mania.
- Ambulatorio estructurado: TAG, OCD, fobias, social anxiety, TEPT estable.
- Referir/coordinar: alto riesgo suicida, trauma severo, comorbilidad sustancias, falla terapeutica, diagnostico incierto, sintomas organicos.

**Take-home point:** Clasificar por urgencia evita convertir un IAM, TEP, hipertiroidismo o abstinencia en "ansiedad".

## 3. Manejo

### A. Trastorno de panico

Diagnostico:

- Ataques inesperados recurrentes.
- Inicio brusco, pico en minutos, duracion breve.
- Palpitaciones, disnea, dolor toracico, mareo, parestesias, sudoracion.
- Miedo a morir/enloquecer o desrealizacion/despersonalizacion.
- Preocupacion persistente o cambio conductual por mas de 1 mes.
- Agorafobia y ansiedad anticipatoria son complicaciones frecuentes.

Manejo:

- Crisis aguda: contencion, explicar que es autolimitada, controlar hiperventilacion, descartar emergencia cardiopulmonar si red flags.
- Farmaco agudo exam-first: BZD puede abortar crisis.
- Mantenimiento: SSRI first-line; efecto tarda semanas.
- Puente: BZD al inicio solo corto plazo si ansiedad intensa, con plan de retiro.
- Psicoterapia: TCC, especialmente si hay agorafobia o evitacion.

**Take-home point:** Panico agudo puede usar BZD; panico cronico se sostiene con SSRI/TCC, no con BZD indefinida.

### B. TAG

Diagnostico:

- Preocupacion excesiva e incontrolable por multiples areas.
- Curso cronico por meses, classically 6 months.
- Tension muscular, fatiga, irritabilidad, insomnio, cefalea, palpitaciones.
- Alta comorbilidad con depresion, somatizacion y otros trastornos de ansiedad.

Manejo:

- Psicoeducacion: explicar ciclo de preocupacion, tension y evitacion.
- TCC o tecnicas de relajacion/applied relaxation.
- SSRI o SNRI si sintomas moderados/severos o deterioro funcional.
- Buspirona: alternativa TAG, no adictiva, tarda 2-4 semanas.
- Evitar BZD cronicas por dependencia, caidas, sedacion y no resolver el ciclo.
- Seguimiento: respuesta, efectos adversos, sueno, consumo de alcohol/sedantes, suicidality.

**Take-home point:** TAG no es crisis; es preocupacion sostenida. La respuesta sostenida es TCC/relajacion + SSRI/SNRI, no sedacion cronica.

### C. TOC

Diagnostico:

- Obsesiones: pensamientos/impulsos recurrentes, intrusivos, propios, absurdos o excesivos, ego-distonicos.
- Compulsiones: actos mentales o motores para disminuir ansiedad.
- Sindromes clasicos: lavadores por contaminacion y comprobadores por duda.
- Diferencial: psicosis si pierde juicio de realidad; OCPD/anancastico si rasgo ego-sintonico.

Manejo:

- SSRI first-line, usualmente a dosis mas altas que depresion y con respuesta en semanas.
- ERP/TCC: exposicion con prevencion de respuesta; trabaja compulsiones y recaida.
- Combinacion SSRI + ERP si moderado/severo o respuesta parcial.
- Clomipramina si SSRI falla/no se tolera, vigilando cardiotoxicidad y anticolinergia.
- Refractario: psiquiatria; considerar antipsicotico atipico si tics y protocolos especializados.

**Take-home point:** TOC no se convence con logica; se rompe el ciclo con ERP y serotonergicos.

### D. TEPT y estres agudo

Diagnostico:

- Trauma real o amenaza de muerte/lesion/violencia sexual.
- Re-experimentacion: flashbacks, pesadillas, recuerdos intrusivos.
- Evitacion: lugares, personas, conversaciones, pensamientos.
- Hiperarousal: insomnio, irritabilidad, hipervigilancia, sobresalto.
- Menos de 1 mes: estres agudo; mas de 1 mes: TEPT.

Manejo:

- Primeros auxilios psicologicos si evento reciente y contexto comunitario/desastre.
- Trauma-focused TCC o EMDR para TEPT.
- SSRI/SNRI pueden ser opciones farmacologicas segun caso.
- Evitar benzodiazepinas como tratamiento de TEPT o fase aguda post-trauma.
- Evaluar depresion, suicidality, sustancias, violencia activa y seguridad.

**Take-home point:** TEPT se trata con trauma-focused therapy y/o serotonergicos; BZD es la trampa.

### E. Fobias y ansiedad social

Fobia especifica:

- Miedo excesivo a objeto/situacion concreta.
- La exposicion dispara ansiedad y evitacion.
- Sangre-inyeccion-herida puede causar sincope vasovagal.
- Tratamiento base: exposicion gradual/en vivo.

Ansiedad social:

- Miedo a evaluacion negativa o escrutinio.
- Debut tipico adolescente.
- Puede automedicarse con alcohol.
- Tratamiento base: CBT especifica.
- SSRI si generalizada/severa o CBT no disponible/no aceptada.
- Propranolol: solo para performance-only puntual, no para trastorno generalizado.

**Take-home point:** Si el miedo tiene gatillo estrecho, el tratamiento aprende seguridad con exposicion.

### F. Ansiedad secundaria

No cerrar trastorno primario si hay:

- Fiebre, hipoxia, dolor toracico, sincope, deficit neurologico.
- Inicio nuevo en edad atipica sin historia previa.
- Signos de hipertiroidismo.
- Uso de estimulantes o cannabis.
- Abstinencia alcohol/BZD.
- Acatisia por antipsicotico.
- Crisis hipertensiva, TEP, neumotorax, IAM, hipoglucemia.

**Take-home point:** La ansiedad secundaria se cura tratando la causa; sedar puede esconder peligro.

## 4. Complicaciones

| Trastorno | Complicaciones |
|---|---|
| Panico | Agorafobia, ansiedad anticipatoria, hipocondria, depresion, abuso alcohol/sedantes, suicidality |
| TAG | Cronificacion, insomnio, somatizacion, depresion, consumo de sedantes/alcohol |
| TOC | Deterioro funcional, dermatitis por lavado, aislamiento, depresion, suicidality |
| TEPT | Depresion, sustancias, suicidality, violencia/revictimizacion, discapacidad |
| Fobia social | Aislamiento, bajo rendimiento, abuso de alcohol |
| BZD mal usadas | Dependencia, caidas, sedacion, retirada con ansiedad/insomnio/convulsiones |

**Take-home point:** La ansiedad no tratada cronifica evitacion; la BZD mal usada agrega dependencia.

## 5. Seguimiento

Monitorear:

- Frecuencia/intensidad de crisis o preocupacion.
- Evitacion y funcionamiento.
- Sueno, alcohol/sustancias, adherencia.
- Efectos adversos SSRI/SNRI: nauseas iniciales, activacion/insomnio, disfuncion sexual, serotonin syndrome risk if combinations.
- Riesgo suicida, especialmente con depresion comorbida.
- Uso de BZD: dosis, duracion, plan de retiro.
- En primer nivel, usar herramientas como GAD-7 cuando el producto lo requiera.

**Take-home point:** El seguimiento mide funcionamiento y evitacion, no solo "si esta mas tranquilo".

## 6. Pronostico

- Panico y TAG responden bien a tratamiento sostenido, pero recaen si se trata solo el sintoma agudo.
- OCD suele requerir dosis/tiempo suficientes y ERP; respuesta parcial es frecuente.
- TEPT mejora con intervencion trauma-focused, seguridad y manejo de comorbilidades.
- Fobias pueden mejorar mucho con exposicion bien ejecutada.
- Mal pronostico: comorbilidad depresiva, suicidality, sustancias, trauma activo, evitacion severa, dependencia de BZD, enfermedad medica no reconocida.

**Take-home point:** Buen pronostico depende de romper evitacion y tratar comorbilidad; sedacion aislada no es recuperacion.

## Exam Traps

| Trap | Correct move |
|---|---|
| "Tuvo un ataque de panico" = "trastorno de panico" | Exigir recurrencia inesperada + preocupacion/cambio conductual |
| Public speaking panic = panic disorder | Social/performance anxiety if tied to scrutiny |
| Fear of blood with syncope | Specific phobia blood-injection-injury |
| OCD = psychosis | OCD keeps ownership/insight; psychosis loses reality testing |
| TAG = any anxious patient | TAG is chronic multi-domain worry; exclude medical/substance causes |
| TEPT = give BZD | Avoid BZD; trauma-focused therapy/SSRI |
| Conversion-like RM case = core anxiety | Treat as local classification debt; teach separately from anxiety taxonomy |

units.title: Hematoma Epidural y Subdural
units.body:
# Hematoma Epidural y Subdural

## Guion de la enfermedad

El hematoma epidural y el hematoma subdural son colecciones traumaticas extra-axiales que se reconocen por el espacio donde sangran, la forma en tomografia y el tipo de vaso roto. En examen, la pregunta suele esconderse en cuatro datos: edad, mecanismo, evolucion de conciencia y CT.

La regla mental es simple: epidural = arteria meningea media + lente biconvexa + deterioro rapido; subdural = venas puente + semiluna + agudo grave o cronico en anciano.

**Take-home point:** No empiezas por el nombre; empiezas por la forma en CT y el vaso.

## 1. Por que da

### Hematoma epidural

- Sangra en el espacio entre la tabla interna del craneo y la duramadre.
- El vaso classico es la arteria meningea media, rama de la maxilar interna.
- Suele asociarse a fractura temporal o parietotemporal.
- Como la duramadre esta fijada a las suturas, la sangre no cruza suturas y forma una coleccion biconvexa/lenticular.
- Al ser arterial, puede crecer rapido y producir herniacion uncal.

### Hematoma subdural

- Sangra en el espacio entre duramadre y aracnoides.
- El mecanismo classico es ruptura de venas puente corticales por aceleracion-deceleracion.
- La sangre se extiende sobre la convexidad cerebral y puede cruzar suturas, por eso se ve como semiluna/crescent.
- En ancianos, alcoholicos y pacientes anticoagulados, la atrofia cerebral estira las venas puente y permite sangrados con trauma minimo.
- En cronico puede haber membranas y resangrado, lo que explica evolucion por semanas.

### Conceptos preguntables

- Epidural no siempre tiene intervalo lucido; es una pista, no un criterio obligatorio.
- Subdural agudo puede deteriorar muy rapido y tiene mayor mortalidad.
- Subdural cronico puede simular demencia, ACV, depresion, delirium o trastorno psiquiatrico.
- Monro-Kellie: dentro del craneo, sangre extra aumenta presion, desplaza estructuras y reduce perfusion.
- Herniacion uncal: pupila ipsilateral fija/dilatada + caida de conciencia + hemiparesia contralateral.

**Take-home point:** Epidural pregunta arteria y lente; subdural pregunta vena y semiluna.

## 2. A quien

| Perfil | Lesion que sube |
|---|---|
| Joven con trauma temporal/parietotemporal, accidente de transito o caida directa | Hematoma epidural |
| Trauma con breve perdida de conciencia, aparente mejoria y luego deterioro | Hematoma epidural, aunque no siempre esta completo |
| TCE severo con deterioro progresivo, deficit focal y crescent hiperdenso | Hematoma subdural agudo |
| Adulto mayor, anticoagulado o alcoholico con caida leve o no recordada | Hematoma subdural cronico |
| Anciano con semanas de cefalea, confusion, deterioro cognitivo o hemiparesia fluctuante | Hematoma subdural cronico hasta demostrar lo contrario |
| Lactante con subdural + hemorragias retinianas + fracturas costales | Maltrato infantil/sindrome de nino zarandeado |

### Local frequency

- ENAM card: rank #54/191; 7 questions in 3 years.
- Residentado: 2 direct RM-GT-289 cases.
- Current topic signal: total=13, priority Oro.
- Essalud signal: no direct ledger hit found.

**Take-home point:** Epidural es joven y temporal; subdural cronico es anciano, anticoagulacion, alcohol o trauma minimo.

## 3. Como se presenta

### Reconocimiento rapido

| Entidad | Clinica frecuente | CT sin contraste |
|---|---|---|
| Epidural | TCE, posible LOC breve, intervalo lucido, cefalea, vomitos, confusion, deterioro brusco, anisocoria | Hiperdenso biconvexo/lenticular, no cruza suturas |
| Subdural agudo | TCE severo, somnolencia/coma progresivos, deficit focal, hipertension intracraneal | Hiperdenso en semiluna/crescent, puede cruzar suturas |
| Subdural subagudo | Dias a semanas, sintomas progresivos | Isodenso o mixto en semiluna |
| Subdural cronico | Semanas, cefalea, confusion, deterioro cognitivo, marcha alterada, hemiparesia leve | Hipodenso o mixto en semiluna |
| Lesion axonal difusa | Coma o alteracion persistente tras aceleracion-deceleracion | CT normal o hallazgos pequenos no evacuables |
| Contusion hemorragica | Deficit, convulsion o alteracion tras golpe directo | Hiperdensidad intraparenquimatosa frontal/temporal |

### Red flags de masa/herniacion

- Deterioro del Glasgow.
- GCS cae 2 o mas puntos.
- Anisocoria.
- Pupila fija y dilatada.
- Hemiparesia contralateral.
- Vomitos repetidos.
- Cefalea intensa progresiva.
- Convulsion post-TCE.
- Desviacion de linea media.
- Triada de Cushing: hipertension, bradicardia, alteracion respiratoria.

**Take-home point:** En TCE, anisocoria o caida de conciencia convierte el caso en neurocirugia, no en observacion tranquila.

## Manejo

## 1. Diagnostico

### Paso 1. ABC del TCE

- Asegurar via aerea si GCS bajo o deterioro.
- Proteger columna cervical si mecanismo lo exige.
- Oxigenar y evitar hipotension; la hipoxia y la hipotension empeoran lesion secundaria.
- Calcular GCS; no confiar en que el stem lo haya sumado correctamente.
- Buscar focalidad neurologica, pupilas, deficit motor y signos de fractura de base.

### Paso 2. Imagen correcta

- CT de craneo sin contraste es la prueba clave.
- No esperar laboratorio si hay deterioro neurologico y CT/neurocirugia son necesarias.
- CT con ventana osea ayuda si se sospecha fractura.
- No hacer puncion lumbar en sospecha de masa, HTIC o TCE con deficit.

### Paso 3. Leer la CT como matriz

| CT | Diagnostico probable | Vaso/mecanismo |
|---|---|---|
| Hiperdenso biconvexo/lenticular | Hematoma epidural | Arteria meningea media, classically |
| Hiperdenso en semiluna | Hematoma subdural agudo | Venas puente |
| Isodenso en semiluna | Hematoma subdural subagudo | Venas puente, evolucion dias |
| Hipodenso en semiluna | Hematoma subdural cronico | Venas puente, semanas |
| CT normal con coma post-rotacional | Lesion axonal difusa | Cizallamiento axonal |
| Hiperdensidad intraparenquimatosa | Contusion hemorragica | Lesion parenquimatosa |

**Take-home point:** La CT sin contraste resuelve la pregunta; LP esta prohibida si hay masa/HTIC.

## 2. Clasificacion

### Por espacio

- Epidural: craneo-duramadre.
- Subdural: duramadre-aracnoides.

### Por tiempo en subdural

- Agudo: <3 dias; usualmente hiperdenso.
- Subagudo: 3-21 dias; puede ser isodenso.
- Cronico: >21 dias; usualmente hipodenso o mixto.

### Por severidad del TCE

- TCE leve: GCS 14-15.
- TCE moderado: GCS 9-13.
- TCE severo: GCS <=8.

### Por urgencia

- Emergencia neuroquirurgica: deterioro neurologico, anisocoria, herniacion, gran espesor, desviacion de linea media, ICP refractaria.
- Observacion neuroquirurgica estricta: lesion pequena, neurologicamente estable, criterios de bajo riesgo, CT seriada disponible.
- Referencia/traslado: cualquier centro sin CT/neurocirugia ante deterioro, deficit focal, anticoagulacion peligrosa o sospecha de lesion evacuable.

**Take-home point:** Clasificar no es decorar; decide quirofano, UCI, observacion o traslado.

## 3. Manejo

### A. Hematoma epidural

Craniotomia/evacuacion urgente si:

- Volumen >30 mL.
- Espesor >15 mm.
- Desviacion de linea media >5 mm.
- Deterioro neurologico o GCS cae >=2 puntos.
- Anisocoria o focalidad.
- Signos de herniacion.

Observacion solo si todo esto se cumple:

- Volumen <30 mL.
- Espesor <15 mm.
- Shift <5 mm.
- GCS >8.
- Sin deficit focal.
- Neurologicamente estable.
- Neurocirugia, monitorizacion y CT seriada disponibles.

**Take-home point:** Epidural grande o que deteriora = evacuar; el intervalo lucido no te autoriza a esperar.

### B. Hematoma subdural agudo

Craniotomia/evacuacion urgente si:

- Espesor >10 mm.
- Desviacion de linea media >5 mm.
- GCS cae >=2 puntos.
- Pupilas asimetricas, fijas o dilatadas.
- ICP >20 mmHg refractaria.
- Deterioro neurologico o focalidad.

Medidas asociadas:

- Revertir anticoagulacion si existe y segun farmaco.
- Corregir coagulopatia y plaquetas si corresponde.
- Manejar HTIC mientras se prepara cirugia/traslado.

**Take-home point:** Subdural agudo grande no espera a que el GCS sea dramatico; >10 mm o shift >5 mm ya es quirurgico.

### C. Hematoma subdural cronico

Pensar en cronico si:

- Anciano, alcoholico o anticoagulado.
- Trauma minimo o no recordado.
- Semanas de cefalea, confusion, deterioro cognitivo, marcha alterada o hemiparesia.
- CT en semiluna hipodensa o mixta.

Manejo:

- Sintomatico, espesor >10 mm, shift >5 mm o deterioro: burr holes/trepanacion + drenaje.
- Asintomatico pequeno y estable: observacion neuroquirurgica, CT seriada y vigilancia clinica.
- Revisar anticoagulacion, caidas, alcohol, fragilidad y riesgo de recurrencia.

**Take-home point:** El subdural cronico es la "demencia reversible" post-caida que no debes dejar pasar.

### D. Puente de hipertension intracraneal

Mientras se organiza neurocirugia o traslado:

- Elevar cabecera 30 degrees.
- Mantener oxigenacion y perfusion; evitar hipoxia e hipotension.
- Analgesia/sedacion segun protocolo y estado neurologico.
- Mannitol 0.25-1 g/kg IV o solucion salina hipertonica segun disponibilidad/protocolo.
- Hiperventilacion transitoria si hay herniacion inminente, objetivo PaCO2 30-35, solo como puente.
- Revertir anticoagulacion si aplica.
- Tratar convulsiones segun protocolo.
- No usar corticoides para traumatic brain injury.

**Take-home point:** El puente baja presion mientras llega el quirofano; no reemplaza evacuacion de una masa quirurgica.

## 4. Complicaciones

- Herniacion uncal.
- Hipertension intracraneal.
- Isquemia por baja perfusion cerebral.
- Convulsiones.
- Deficit neurologico persistente.
- Recurrencia de subdural cronico.
- Infeccion o complicaciones del drenaje/cirugia.
- Muerte, especialmente en subdural agudo severo.

**Take-home point:** La complicacion central es masa + presion + herniacion.

## 5. Seguimiento

- Monitorizacion neurologica seriada: GCS, pupilas, fuerza, signos de HTIC.
- CT de control segun evolucion, protocolo y manejo conservador/postoperatorio.
- Vigilancia de drenaje en subdural cronico si se coloco.
- Rehabilitacion si hay deficit cognitivo, motor o lenguaje.
- Reevaluar anticoagulacion: indicacion, momento de reinicio y riesgo de caidas.
- Educacion de retorno: cefalea progresiva, vomitos, somnolencia, confusion, convulsion, debilidad, anisocoria.
- En lactantes/ninos con sospecha de maltrato: activar ruta de proteccion y reporte.

**Take-home point:** El seguimiento busca detectar expansion, recurrencia y lesion secundaria.

## 6. Pronostico

- Epidural puede tener buen pronostico si se evacua antes de herniacion o coma prolongado.
- Subdural agudo tiene peor pronostico porque suele asociarse a trauma severo y lesion cerebral subyacente.
- Subdural cronico suele mejorar con drenaje, pero puede recurrir.
- Peor pronostico: edad avanzada, GCS bajo, pupilas anormales, hipotension, hipoxia, gran shift, anticoagulacion y retraso quirurgico.

**Take-home point:** En epidural, rapidez salva; en subdural agudo, el dano asociado pesa mucho; en cronico, diagnosticarlo evita llamarlo demencia.

## Trampas de examen

- Biconvexo no es subdural; es epidural.
- Semiluna no es epidural; es subdural.
- Arteria meningea media no es el vaso classico del subdural.
- Venas puente no son el vaso classico del epidural.
- Lucid interval no es obligatorio para epidural.
- Anciano confundido semanas despues de caida minima no es "solo demencia".
- No dar dexamethasone por traumatic brain injury.
- No hacer LP ante masa intracraneal/HTIC.
- No olvidar anticoagulacion en subdural.
- No confundir lesion axonal difusa con hematoma evacuable si CT es normal y coma persiste.
